content.jobHook: Join Gorilla Dash as a Sales Executive! Help us scale our powerful franchise SaaS platform by driving inbound leads and outbound prospecting.
content.unEditedContent:
Gorilla Dash is a powerful SaaS platform purpose-built for franchise and multi-location businesses. We bring website management, marketing, internal communication, CRM, recruitment, and real-time performance analytics into a single dashboard — with a centralised master account and unlimited child accounts so franchisors and franchisees stay perfectly aligned.

Our customers are franchise networks who are tired of stitching together five different tools to run their business. Your job is to find them, show them a better way, and bring them on board.

A minimum of 1-2 years sales experience is required for this position.

SaaS sales experience is preferred but not essential for this role.

Knowledge of the franchise industry is preferred but not essential.

Australian citizenship is required for this position.

This sales role involves a combination of inbound lead management and outbound prospecting activities.

What you'll do day-to-day:

  • Prospect into franchise companies and multi-site operators across Australia and New Zealand through outbound calls, email, LinkedIn, and industry events.

  • Qualify opportunities and run discovery conversations with franchisors, marketing leaders, and operations executives.

  • Deliver tailored product demonstrations that map Gorilla Dash's capabilities to each prospect's pain points — websites, marketing, recruitment, analytics, communication.

  • Manage your pipeline end-to-end: follow-ups, proposals, negotiation, and contract sign-off.

  • Coordinate a smooth handover to our onboarding and support team once a deal is signed.

  • Work closely with marketing, product, and customer success — feeding insights back so we keep getting sharper.

  • Hit (and beat) monthly and quarterly revenue targets.

What we're looking for:

  • Strongly preferred: prior experience inside a franchise system — as a business advisor / franchise consultant, franchise development manager (BDM), operations or network manager, or similar field-support role. You already understand how franchisors and franchisees think, what they buy, and what they push back on.

  • 1–6+ years of B2B sales experience is ideal (SaaS preferred), but we'll absolutely consider strong franchise-system operators making the transition into sales — we'll teach you the SaaS sales motion. We're equally happy to hear from BDR/SDR candidates ready to step up and seasoned Account Executives.

  • Confident, professional outbound communicator — phone, email, video, and LinkedIn.

  • Comfortable running product demos and articulating ROI to senior decision-makers.

  • Disciplined pipeline management — you live in your CRM, not your inbox.

  • Self-starter who thrives in a remote environment and doesn't need micromanaging.

  • Coachable, curious, and genuinely interested in the customer's business.

  • Resilient — you understand sales is a numbers game and don't take "no" personally.

  • Excellent written and spoken English.

  • Full working rights in Australia or New Zealand.

Bonus points for:

  • Experience selling into the franchise industry (vendor side) on top of working in it.

  • Background selling marketing, website, CRM, or business management software.

  • An existing network of franchise contacts across ANZ.

  • Familiarity with tools like HubSpot, Salesforce, Apollo, Outreach, Gong, or similar.

  • Prior experience working a fully remote sales role.

json.title: Dove Ceremony Assistant / Dove Release Attendant

content.jobHook: Assist with professional white dove releases at funerals, memorials, and weddings — a unique, meaningful role.
content.unEditedContent:
White Wings Dove Service – Caboolture QLD

White Wings Dove Service provides professional white dove releases for funerals, memorials, and weddings across South-East Queensland.

We are seeking a calm, reliable, well-presented person to assist with ceremonial dove releases at meaningful life events.

This is a unique role suited to someone who is comfortable working in emotional environments, enjoys working with animals, and presents professionally in formal settings.


About the role

Duties include:

  • Handling and transporting white doves

  • Loading and unloading travel crates

  • Setting up release displays and cages

  • Assisting families and clients during ceremonies

  • Travelling to venues across Brisbane and surrounding areas

  • Working independently and following established procedures

Most work involves funerals and memorial services, with occasional weddings.


Important information

  • This is occasional, event-based work only

  • It is best suited as supplementary income rather than regular full-time employment

  • Many services occur on weekdays between mid-morning and early afternoon

  • Some jobs involve extended driving times and Brisbane traffic

  • Applicants must live within reasonable distance of Caboolture due to bird collection and travel requirements

Applicants must live within 20km of Caboolture to meet the bird collection and travel requirements for this role.


The ideal applicant will be:

  • Calm, respectful, and emotionally mature

  • Comfortable around birds and animals

  • Physically capable of lifting cages, kneeling, standing outdoors, and driving longer distances

  • Well presented with a polished and modest appearance suitable for funerals and formal occasions

  • Reliable and able to work independently

  • Comfortable interacting with families, funeral professionals, and wedding clients

Experience with birds, pigeons, aviculture, events, funerals, animal care, hospitality, or customer service is highly regarded but not essential.

A current driver licence and reliable vehicle are required.

A reliable medium sedan or hatchback vehicle is required to safely transport dove crates and equipment to venues.


Please include:

  • Your location/suburb

  • Availability

  • Relevant experience

  • Why this role interests you


CONTACT: Mobile 0405 623 953

Email: fiona@whitewingsdoveservice.com.au

content.unEditedContent:
• Assistant Project Officer
  • Package includes salary ($99,938 - $110,271) plus superannuation and annual leave loading
  • Ongoing full-time role located in Audley (Flexible location by negotiation)

  

Do you want your work to make a difference for NSW? 
Together, we create thriving environments, communities, and economies

 

About the Role 

National Parks and Wildlife Service (NPWS) has a unique opportunity for an Assistant Project Officer within the Assets & Infrastructure Branch insurance team.

As the Assistant Project Officer, you will undertake a diverse range of tasks supporting the NPWS insurance program. This includes frontline customer service responsibilities, such as managing the Outlook mailbox and support helpline, and providing advice to NPWS staff on insurance-related matters. In this role, you will also contribute to claims management processes by undertaking activities such as claims processing, analysis, reporting, and implementation, along with other related administrative tasks.

Further details regarding the role’s specific functions and requirements are outlined in the Statement of Works.

 

About You   
To be successful in the role, you will have demonstrated ability to deliver program outcomes and support activities in line with Statement of Works, given tight deadlines and competing demands and priorities.

 

Essential requirements

  • Experience in the provision of administrative and support services
  • Experience in development and delivery of programs and projects.
  • Understanding of contemporary project management principles and practices.

 


Role description: Assistant Project Officer and Statement of Works

 

Who we are

The Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) works to protect the state’s environment and heritage. It leads the way on climate change, driving the sustainable transition to a net zero economy, powered by affordable, reliable, and clean energy.

DCCEEW conserves and protects the state’s natural environment. It manages the NSW national park estate, including its rich and diverse biodiversity and Aboriginal cultural heritage for future generations.


DCCEEW also ensures sustainable management of water resources across the state, to support the environment, communities and industry.


We acknowledge the ongoing custodial responsibilities of the Aboriginal peoples of NSW to care for Country and water and are committed to establishing meaningful partnerships with Aboriginal peoples in the management of the environment.

 

What we can offer you
NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service is a great place to expand your career and grow your skills and knowledge.


What we do
About NSW National Parks & Wildlife Service
Visit a park


How to apply
Submit your application, including your resume and cover letter expressing your interest and suitability for the role.  Ensure that you answer all pre-screening questions.

To be eligible for an ongoing role in the NSW Public Sector you need to be an Australian Citizen, New Zealand Citizen or Permanent Resident. For temporary and casual roles, you need to hold a valid visa giving you permission to work in Australia as required by the role.


Applications close: Tuesday 9 June 2026 at 11:55pm.


For more information about the role contact Nathan Mapstone, Manager Asset Management Assurance & Systems, Assets & Infrastructure Branch, NPWS on 0439445947 or nathan.mapstone@dcceew.nsw.gov.au.


A recruitment pool may be created for ongoing and temporary opportunities of the same role or role type that may become available over the next 18 months.


Our goal is to build a workforce that not only represents but also understands and serves the diverse communities of New South Wales. We are committed to making our state a vibrant and inclusive place to live, work, and thrive for everyone. Our workforce represents people of all ages and genders, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people with disabilities, the LGBTQI+ community, and people from diverse ethnic and cultural backgrounds. 


Looking for more information or assistance in applying? 

  • Our commitment to a diverse and inclusive workplace.

If you are an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander use our Aboriginal applicants guide to assist with applying for roles or contact our Aboriginal Career pathways team for a yarn.

content.jobHook: Talent Acquisitions coordinator to assist with hiring needs, are you new to your recruitment career? or experienced part time recruiter
content.unEditedContent:
About CTM 
CTM is a global award-winning provider of innovative and cost-effective travel management solutions to the corporate, events, leisure and loyalty travel markets. CTM provides personalised service excellence with client-facing technology solutions in offices all around the world, including New Zealand, Australia, Asia, North America and Europe with over 3000 employees.
  
At CTM, our people are our greatest asset. We are a team of collaborative, innovative and future focused professionals we work with the company's values in mind; Connect, Deliver and Evolve.

About the Role 
The Talent Acquisition Coordinator plays a key role in delivering a seamless and engaging recruitment experience across the employee lifecycle, providing operational and administrative support throughout the hiring process.

Supporting the TA Lead and partnering closely with the ANZ People Team and business leaders across Australia, New Zealand, and Global teams, this role supports the attraction, coordination, and hiring of top talent in line with CTM's recruitment policies and processes.

The role is instrumental in driving efficient recruitment operations, supporting job advertising, candidate management, interview coordination, and onboarding activities, while supporting the TA Lead on ongoing projects.

Responsibilities 
  • Provide recruitment consulting administrative support including but not limited to supporting end to end recruitment task, this includes job briefs, posting job advertisements, managing candidate applications, updating the ATS (JobAdder) and other recruitment platforms (Linkedin & SEEK)
  • Respond to recruitment enquiries via Outlook, FreshService and JobAdder, action tasks and requests from the business as required
  • Drafting advertisements that attract and engage candidates for positions.
  • Co-ordinate recruitment processes, coordinating with the hiring manager and updating the ATS and other HR related systems.
  • Support managing candidates from application through to onboarding whilst providing an exceptional experience.
  • Assist with shortlisting candidates and candidate screening calls
  • Submit references checks through reference check platform 
  • Maintain and develop strong relationships with internal stakeholders
Education and Experience 
  • Demonstrated experience within an internal recruitment team or recruitment agency (desirable) with up to 2 years' experience 
Why CTM?  
As a global organisation CTM offers a range of employee benefits that including;
  • Travel discounts  
  • Perkbox - Retail, Lifestyle, Entertainment, Health & Wellness discounts
  • Training and Development opportunities  - online lessons & certificates
  • Annual Volunteer Day  
  • x2 Wellness/Chillout Days  
  • Blended work arrangements with hybrid WFH flexibility 
  • 2 Weeks extra leave - Purchase Leave
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Sonder - EAP Platform 
CTM offer a strong, established and sustainable work environment which will support your career development and wellbeing.
  
CTM is committed to the unique contributions of all our people and actively encourage candidates with all abilities and diverse backgrounds to apply. Come work for a global award winning company that values its people, community, and technological innovation.

content.jobHook: As Club Manager, you’ll lead sales, culture, member experience, and growth at an Anytime Fitness club in Melbourne’s Inner West.
content.unEditedContent:
Join Anytime Fitness as Club Manager – Melbourne Inner West


We’re looking for an exceptional Club Manager to lead one of our Melbourne Inner West locations as we enter an exciting new phase of growth.


This is an opportunity for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, loves people, takes pride in high standards, and is motivated by results, culture, and leadership.


About the Role


As Club Manager, you’ll lead the day-to-day operations of the club while driving sales, member experience, team culture, and overall performance.


You’ll be supported by an experienced ownership group with a strong track record of building high-performing clubs known for customer experience, operational excellence, and community impact.


We’re looking for someone who:

• Brings positive energy and initiative every day

• Has proven sales and customer service experience

• Communicates confidently and professionally

• Naturally connects with people and builds relationships

• Takes ownership and solves problems proactively

• Performs well under pressure and can multitask effectively

• Leads by example and genuinely cares about creating a welcoming environment


What We Offer

• Competitive salary package + performance incentives

• Industry-leading training and development

• Career progression opportunities within a growing group

• Free Anytime Fitness membership worldwide

• Supportive, energetic, and team-focused culture


If you’re driven, people-focused, and ready to lead from the front, we’d love to hear from you.


Please apply with your resume and cover letter.


Please note: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Successful applicants will require a Working with Children Check and First Aid/CPR certification.

content.jobHook: Feeling stuck? Join a fast-growing sales startup with uncapped earning potential, paid training, and clear progression into leadership.
content.unEditedContent:
Feeling Stuck? Build Something Bigger.

A lot of people hit a point where they realise they’re working hard… but not actually moving forward.

Same routine.
Same income.
Same ceiling.

At Pinnacle Sales Group, we’re building a fast-growing sales startup based in Surry Hills, focused on developing high-performance people from the ground up.

We partner with well-known Australian organisations, brands and non-profit organisations, specialising in customer acquisition and brand awareness through face-to-face marketing.

This role is built for people who want:
• More growth
• More responsibility
• A stronger environment
• A career where performance actually matters

No experience is needed - just the right attitude, communication skills, and willingness to learn.

What you’ll be doing:

• Speaking with new people daily, representing our clients face-to-face
• Building confidence through real-world communication and sales experience
• Working towards daily and weekly performance targets
• Learning from experienced leaders in a fast-paced environment
• Developing transferable skills in communication, influence and leadership

What we offer:

• $65,000–$85,000 base salary + uncapped commissions. Top performers earn $110K–$125K+
• Paid training, daily coaching and hands-on development from experienced leaders
• Clear, performance-based progression into leadership and management
• A fast-paced, high-performance team culture where effort is recognised
• Weekly incentives, competitions, team events and all-expenses-paid trips for top performers
• Real-world skills in communication, confidence and leadership

Who this suits:

• People who feel under-utilised in their current role
• Competitive and ambitious individuals
• Strong communicators who enjoy working with people
• Reliable people ready to commit to full-time work
• People looking to grow personally and professionally

Location:

Based in Surry Hills - 2 minutes from Central Station.

Next steps:

Successful applicants will be contacted within 1–3 days for a short phone pre-screening call.

content.jobHook: This role offers the opportunity to oversee financial operations, drive strategic decision-making, and contribute to organisational success.
content.unEditedContent:
This role offers the opportunity to oversee financial operations, drive strategic decision-making, and contribute to organisational success.

Client Details

A growth-oriented, ASX-listed resources organisation with significant capital investment programs, focused on developing and operating large-scale projects while maintaining strong governance, reporting discipline, and investor engagement.

Description

Reporting to the CFO, the General Manager Finance leads the finance function, with an emphasis on ASX reporting, statutory compliance, and maintaining the integrity of financial control across the Group. The role is accountable for delivering timely and accurate monthly, quarterly, half-year, and annual reporting, while acting as the primary interface with auditors and supporting continuous disclosure requirements. A key focus is on financial planning and analysis (FP&A), including budgeting, forecasting, and providing clear, actionable insights to support capital allocation and operational decision-making. The CFO will partner closely with business units to assess project performance, cash flow, and profitability, translating complex financial data into commercial recommendations for leadership and investors. Additionally, the role oversees treasury, tax, and financial modelling activities, supporting strategic initiatives, funding requirements and growth opportunities.

Profile

The successful candidate is likely a technically strong finance leader (CA/CPA qualified) with experience in a publicly listed or similarly regulated environment, ideally within resources or other capital-intensive sectors. They will bring a proven track record across financial control, ASX reporting, and FP&A, with the ability to operate both strategically and hands-on. Experience navigating growth, transformation, or project-heavy environments is important, along with strong stakeholder engagement skills across executives, boards, auditors, and investors. They will be a commercially minded operator who can balance governance with insight, and influence decision-making through high-quality analysis. Strong leadership capability and experience building high-performing teams in complex environments will be critical to success.

Job Offer

High-impact, end-to-end role - Broad ownership across financial control, ASX reporting, FP&A, treasury, and tax, with a direct line to the CFO and influence on business strategy.

Growth and scale opportunity - Exposure to a capital-intensive, expanding organisation where finance plays a critical role in supporting major projects and investment decisions.

Strong commercial and investor exposure - Opportunity to lead financial insights, partner with operations, and contribute directly to investor reporting, market communication, and strategic decision-making.

In your application, please confirm if you are interested in an interim or permanent opportunity. If you have any questions please email brodiemcdougall@michaelpage.com.au

bulletPoints: Established Australian manufacturing with over 50 years industry presence.
Strong pipeline of work, continued investment and long-term growth outlook.
High-autonomy leadership role with genuine influence across the business.
content.jobHook: An opportunity for an experienced manufacturing leader to take ownership of a busy operation, build team capability, and drive business growth.
content.unEditedContent:
About the Business

ASM Sheet Metal is a well-established Australian manufacturing business supplying customised steel and aluminium cabinetry solutions to the electrical and data centre sector. Backed by strong demand, long-standing industry relationships, and continued investment through CSM, the business is entering its next stage of operational growth.

Our client is seeking an experienced Manufacturing Operations Manager to lead day-to-day manufacturing operations and help strengthen production performance, operational consistency, team capability, and commercial outcomes across the business.

This is a high-impact leadership role suited to a practical and commercially minded manufacturing leader who enjoys building strong teams, improving systems, and creating disciplined operational environments.

You take pride in building capable teams, creating operational clarity and maintaining high standards across safety, quality and delivery.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to the Director, you will take ownership of a busy manufacturing operation across fabrication, welding, powder coating, assembly, planning, and operational support functions.

The role offers a high level of autonomy and influence, with genuine responsibility for operational and commercial performance across the manufacturing function, including improving workflow discipline, strengthening accountability, supporting team development and helping scale operations to support continued business growth.

The environment will suit someone who enjoys balancing people leadership, production demands, operational improvement and customer expectations within a busy manufacturing setting.

You will work closely with supervisors, operational staff, engineering, administration, and customers to drive operational performance, continuous improvement, and reliable delivery outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead day-to-day manufacturing and production operations.

  • Improve workflow discipline, productivity, and operational consistency.

  • Manage labour performance, output, and operational accountability.

  • Build capability and ownership within supervisors and operational teams.

  • Coordinate production priorities, schedules, and workflow bottlenecks.

  • Strengthen communication across operations, engineering, administration, and customers.

  • Support customer relationships through reliable delivery and proactive communication.

  • Drive practical continuous improvement initiatives across production operations.

  • Reinforce strong safety, quality, and operational standards.

  • Support operational financial performance through labour management, cost control, and operational efficiency.

About You

You are an experienced manufacturing operations leader with a collaborative and practical leadership style.

You build strong accountability across teams, communicate effectively across a broad range of people and personalities, and are comfortable making difficult decisions when required.

You understand how disciplined operational leadership influences productivity, quality, customer outcomes, team performance, and commercial performance.

You take pride in running well-organised operations, building strong team standards, and creating environments where people can perform at their best.

You will ideally bring:

  • Experience leading manufacturing, fabrication, industrial, or production operations.

  • Strong operational leadership capability within fast-paced production environments.

  • Experience leading teams of 25-50 people across manufacturing operations.

  • Experience improving productivity, workflow, and operational performance.

  • A visible and hands-on leadership approach with strong floor presence.

  • Strong communication and relationship management skills.

  • The ability to build capability, trust, and accountability across teams.

  • Commercial awareness across labour, productivity, and operational performance.

  • A customer-focused mindset and commitment to delivery outcomes.

  • A continuous improvement mindset with experience implementing practical operational improvements.

  • You have minimum of 8 years manufacturing operations leadership experience.

  • Experience gained across any manufacturing sector will be considered.

What's on Offer

  • Established and respected Australian manufacturing business.

  • Strong pipeline of work and long-term growth outlook.

  • High level of operational autonomy and influence.

  • Opportunity to shape systems, people, and operational performance.

  • Stable ownership and ongoing investment in the business.

  • Competitive salary package between $175,000 – $195,000 + super.

If you are an experienced manufacturing operations leader looking for an opportunity to make a genuine impact within a growing and well-established business, we welcome your application.

Please note, unsolicited approaches or resumes from recruitment agencies will not be accepted for this role.

bulletPoints: Up to $35/hr (based on experience & age) + Super + Perks and more via Healthia!
Be part of a supportive, passionate team in a modern healthcare setting
Enjoy excellent benefits and opportunities for further professional development
content.jobHook: Join a vibrant, supportive clinic! Deliver exceptional service and grow your career with Back In Motion Como. Apply today!
content.unEditedContent:
Back In Motion Como is seeking a dedicated, customer-focused Admin Assistant to be the face of our clinic, providing exceptional service to our clients and assisting our team in delivering the highest quality care.

What's In It For You?

  • Employee Perks: Enjoy Healthia Group Employee Discounts – up to 30% off all services and products, including podiatry, Pilates, strength classes, physiotherapy & footwear!

  • Keep Fit, Stay Active: Access a range of gyms, swimming pools, and health centres across Australia at discounted rates for you and your family with Fitness Passport.

  • Professional Growth: Access formal career development pathways, advanced clinical and leadership training, and extensive professional development opportunities through Healthia's network.

  • Comprehensive Training: Receive thorough training in all aspects of the role to ensure your success.

  • Supportive Team: Work with a passionate team that genuinely cares about your success

  • Modern Setting: Work in a modern clinic with a focus on holistic patient care.

Joining Back In Motion means being part of a team that’s committed to making a difference in the lives of our clients. Whether you're helping someone get back to their best or supporting our team in delivering top-tier care, your role is integral to our success.

The Opportunity

We are currently on the look-out for a committed and enthusiastic Admin Assistant to join our thriving clinic on a part-time basis.

This role will involve some shifts with an 8PM finish in addition to fortnightly Saturdays, ideally suiting an individual who can offer flexibility as our clinic needs evolve. We are more than happy to be reasonably flexible in our roster to support the right candidate.

As our valued Admin Assistant, your key responsibilities will include but not be limited to:

  • Greeting clients with a warm and friendly smile, creating a welcoming atmosphere.

  • Managing appointment bookings, client queries, and payments with efficiency and professionalism.

  • Providing administrative support to our team of physiotherapists and allied health professionals.

  • Assisting with clinic organisation, including maintaining a clean and tidy reception area.

  • Handling phone and email correspondence promptly and effectively.

What We’re Looking For

To thrive in this role, you’ll need:

  • A genuine passion for customer service and helping people.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Strong organisational abilities and attention to detail.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office; experience with practice management software is a bonus.

  • Reliability, flexibility, and a proactive attitude.

About Us

Back In Motion Como is part of the well-regarded Back In Motion Health Group, a leader in physiotherapy and allied health. Our boutique clinic is known for providing personalised care to a diverse range of clients. We pride ourselves on offering a welcoming and dynamic environment for our clients and staff alike.

We are proudly part of the Healthia Group, a company that offers a supportive and cohesive workplace culture with integral educational and career growth opportunities. If you are successful in this application, you will immediately be connected to a network of Allied Health Practitioners and Support Services in over 300 practices across Australia and New Zealand.

Ready to be Part of Something Bigger?

If this sounds like the opportunity you’ve been waiting for, we’d love to hear from you! Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter detailing your availability and why you’d be the perfect fit for this role by clicking APPLY NOW.

To learn more about who we are and what we do, please feel free to visit us at www.backinmotion.com.au

We can’t wait to welcome you to our Back In Motion Como team!

json.title: SALES ASSOCIATE - FULL TRAINING PROVIDED

content.jobHook: Join a fast-growing team where you’ll build confidence, communication, leadership, daily mentorship, and uncapped earning potential.
content.unEditedContent:
SWISH MARKETING
Most jobs teach you how to survive.

We teach people how to communicate, lead, sell, influence, and build confidence for life.

At SWISH MARKETING, we’re creating one of Australia’s most ambitious face-to-face teams — built for driven individuals who want growth, opportunity, and a future bigger than the 9–5 grind.

No experience?
That's fine.

Some of our best performers came from hospitality, retail, gyms, labouring, sport, or had never worked sales before.

What matters most is:

  • Energy

  • Coachability

  • Work ethic

  • Confidence (or the willingness to build it)

  • A hunger to grow

What You'll Be Doing

You'll be speaking with homeowners face-to-face, educating people on their water quality, and booking or closing appointments for premium home water filtration systems.

Candidates must have access to reliable public transport to reach customer locations.

No hard-pressure selling.
No cold corporate environment.
Just real conversations, real training, and real opportunity.

What Makes Us Different?

Most companies give you a script and tell you to "figure it out."

We actually develop people.

You'll receive:

  • Daily communication training

  • Leadership development

  • Mentorship from high-performing team leaders

  • A fun, competitive team culture

  • Clear progression pathways into leadership and management

If you want to become better at:

  • Communication

  • Confidence

  • Leadership

  • Public speaking

  • Sales

  • Influence

  • Personal growth

…this environment will change you.

The Opportunity

  • Uncapped commissions + bonuses

  • Full training provided

  • Rapid progression opportunities

  • Weekly team events and incentives

  • High-energy culture

  • Flexible pathways into leadership roles

Top performers are earning significantly above average income levels because the harder and smarter you work, the more you make.

Who This Suits

This is perfect for:

  • Candidates must be at least 18 years of age

  • Athletes or competitive personalities

  • People tired of dead-end jobs

  • Individuals wanting personal growth and higher income

  • Future entrepreneurs and leaders

  • Valid Australian work visa required for this position

If you're looking for a safe, predictable, low-energy workplace… this probably isn't for you.

But if you want:

  • growth,

  • challenge,

  • skill development,

  • better income,

  • and a team that pushes you to become more —

Apply now.

Your future self will thank you.

@swishmarketng - Instagram

json.title: Admin Assistant to the Director

content.jobHook: Your expertise will directly influence our success, and your contributions will be recognised, celebrated, and rewarded.
content.unEditedContent:
Admin Assistant

Our Mission

We’re a growing, people-focused business dedicated to delivering exceptional service and building lasting relationships with our customers. We thrive on collaboration, integrity, and a genuine passion for helping clients succeed.

The Impact You'll Make

As our Admin Assistant, you’ll be the friendly, organised, and proactive force that keeps our operations running smoothly while supporting our sales team to deliver outstanding results. Your work will directly contribute to creating seamless customer experiences and driving business growth.

What You'll Do

  • Provide day-to-day administrative support, including managing emails, scheduling, and maintaining records.

  • Assist the sales team with preparing quotes, processing orders, and following up with customers.

  • Keep our CRM system up to date with accurate client and sales information.

  • Help prepare reports, presentations, and marketing materials.

What You'll Bring

  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.

  • Confident communication skills—both written and verbal.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and basic CRM systems.

  • A proactive, can-do attitude and willingness to learn.

  • Previous experience in administration or sales support is highly regarded.

Why You'll Love It Here

  • Supportive, friendly team environment where your contributions are valued.

  • Opportunities for training and professional growth.

  • Flexible working arrangements to help balance work and life.

  • opportunity to receive commissions based on performances

We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Join Us

If you’re organised, people-focused, and ready to make a difference, we’d love to hear from you. Send us your resume and a short note about why this role excites you.

content.jobHook: Join Solar Link Australia and work with warm leads, uncapped commissions, career growth, and Australia’s booming renewable energy sector.
content.unEditedContent:
Dingley Village, Melbourne VIC
Full Time

OTE $100,000 – $180,000+ | Warm Qualified Leads | Uncapped Commissions

Solar Link Australia is expanding.

Due to strong demand for solar and battery storage solutions, we are looking for a motivated and professional Solar & Battery Sales Consultant to join our growing Melbourne team.

This is an opportunity to work with warm, qualified leads and represent high-quality energy solutions in one of Australia’s fastest-growing industries.

About the Role

You’ll work directly with homeowners and businesses to design tailored solar and battery solutions, conduct consultations, and guide customers through the sales process from enquiry to close.

Consultations are conducted via phone.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Managing warm inbound enquiries and qualified appointments

  • Conducting professional sales consultations with residential and commercial customers

  • Recommending tailored solar and battery storage solutions

  • Building strong customer relationships and referral opportunities

  • Working closely with the operations team to ensure smooth project delivery

  • Staying up to date with products, rebates, and industry developments

  • Consistently achieving and exceeding sales targets

What We’re Looking For

  • Proven sales experience with a strong closing ability

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills

  • Clear, confident and professional spoken English

  • A polished and customer-focused approach

  • Confidence conducting consultations over phone

  • Self-motivated with strong organisational skills

  • Experience in solar, electrical, energy, automotive, real estate or in-home sales is highly regarded

  • Driver’s licence required

What We Offer

  • Uncapped commissions with strong earning potential

  • Warm, qualified leads provided

  • Supportive and experienced management team

  • Full product and sales training

  • Career progression opportunities within a growing company

  • Modern office in Dingley Village with on-site parking

  • Opportunity to work in a rapidly growing industry with long-term demand

At Solar Link Australia, we help customers reduce energy costs and transition to smarter energy solutions. If you are driven, professional, and ready to build a rewarding career in renewable energy sales, we’d love to hear from you.

content.unEditedContent:
Join the Team at Mogo Wheelchairs

Sales Representative / Wheelchair Seating & Product Specialist

Want a career where you can actually make a difference — without sitting behind a desk all day?

At Mogo Wheelchairs, we help people regain independence, confidence, and freedom through customized mobility solutions. We are looking for a motivated, personable, and driven individual to join our team as a Sales Representative / Seating & Product Specialist.

This is an ideal opportunity for:

  • Occupational Therapists wanting to stay involved in disability and client outcomes without spending their life writing reports

  • Rehab consultants or support industry professionals looking for a more rewarding and flexible role

  • Sales professionals who enjoy relationship-building and meaningful work

  • Anyone passionate about helping people while working with innovative equipment and technology

About the Role

You’ll work closely with clients, therapists, support coordinators, and care teams to help prescribe and supply customized mobility solutions that genuinely improve lives.

Your role will include:

  • Conducting wheelchair and seating assessments

  • Recommending customized mobility solutions

  • Building strong relationships with OTs, providers, and clients

  • Demonstrating products and equipment

  • Managing appointments and customer follow-up

  • Working alongside our technical and clinical team to achieve great outcomes

We are based in Sydney and mainly service the Sydney metro area, with occasional travel within approximately 3 hours of Sydney for client appointments and regional support.

No two days are the same, one day you could be helping a young athlete get back into sport, the next helping someone gain independence at home.

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong communication and people skills

  • Confidence building relationships and working independently

  • OT, rehab, disability, mobility, or sales background highly regarded

  • Passion for helping people

  • Organized, motivated, and solution-focused attitude

  • Current driver’s license

  • Current Working With Children Check (or willingness to obtain)

What We Offer

  • Excellent salary package + incentives

  • Company vehicle

  • Phone, laptop, and tools provided

  • Flexible and supportive team environment

  • Career growth opportunities within a respected Australian company

  • Meaningful work where you see real-life impact every day

We also believe work should be enjoyable.

Mogo proudly sponsors charity golf days, community events, and industry functions, giving our team plenty of opportunities to connect with great people and have some fun along the way.

If you’re looking for a rewarding role with purpose, flexibility, and a genuinely good team culture, we’d love to hear from you.

json.title: Inventory Controller

content.jobHook: Opportunity to lead and develop warehouse operations into a first-class function, driving growth, efficiency, and excellence.
content.unEditedContent:
About LETO Technology

LETO Technology is a leader in product identification and coding systems, delivering world-class service and support to major FMCG, pharmaceutical, and manufacturing customers. With strong growth and national expansion, we're building a high-performance team that thrives on ownership, accountability, and delivering reliability at scale.

Role Overview

We are seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Inventory Controller to join our Brisbane team. In this role, you will own the end-to-end inventory process — ensuring stock accuracy, efficient movement of parts, forecasting demand, and supporting services/repairs with the right components at the right time. You'll be at the forefront leading Warehouse Operations.


Key Duties & Responsibilities

  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve inventory control procedures, policies, and best practices

  • Maintain accurate stock records in an ERP/WMS system (cycle counts, reconciliations, adjustments)

  • Coordinate incoming receipts, quality inspections, and put-away / storage

  • Oversee and coordinate the dispatch of goods and freight, ensuring compliance with schedules, documentation, and customer requirements.

  • Authorise and document stock transfers, returns, disposals, and write-offs

  • Forecast part demand based on historical usage, upcoming service schedules, and growth projections

  • Analyse inventory trends, identify slow movers, and recommend action plans (e.g. rebalancing, obsolescence)

  • Work collaboratively with procurement / purchasing to order parts timely and cost-effectively

  • Liaise with field service, operations, and production to ensure parts availability and prevent service delays

  • Perform regular audits, identify discrepancies, and investigate root causes

  • Produce inventory reports and KPIs (accuracy, turnover, stock days, shrinkage) for management

  • Lead stocktake events (annual or periodic)

  • Train or support junior staff in inventory practices and controls


Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Proven experience (2+ years preferred) in an inventory control, stock management, or similar role

  • Strong familiarity with inventory systems, ERP or WMS (or similar software)

  • Excellent analytical skills, attention to detail, and comfort working with data and spreadsheets

  • Ability to forecast demand, manage stock levels, and mitigate overstock / stockouts

  • Good communication skills — able to coordinate across functions (tech, operations, procurement)

  • Process-oriented, with aptitude for continuous improvement and systemisation

  • Ability to operate independently with minimal supervision, deliver clear and timely reports, take full ownership of assigned tasks, and manage priorities to meet business objectives.

  • Tertiary qualification in logistics, supply chain, business, or related field is a plus

  • Experience in a technology, field service, industrial, or technical environment is advantageous

  • Current Australian work authorisation required at time of application


What You'll Get (Why Join LETO)

  • Clear pathways for career progression — from operations into senior roles

  • Be part of a company undergoing national expansion — your role will be key to scaling

  • Investment in training, development, and upskilling

  • Strong team culture where your input and ideas are valued

  • High autonomy and ownership — you won't be micromanaged

  • Competitive remuneration plus super.


Apply Now

If you're motivated, detail-driven, and ready to take ownership of inventory processes in a fast-paced, growth environment — we'd love to hear from you.

json.title: Sales Consultant

content.jobHook: Join a premium home solutions business, driving high-value sales and delivering outstanding customer experiences across Sydney's residential market
content.unEditedContent:
Our client is a well-established Australian business known for delivering premium design-focused solutions into residential homes.

We're looking for a confident and personable Sales Consultant to join their Pagewood-based team, looking after showroom consultations as well as occasional on-site client meetings. 

This is a hands-on, end-to-end sales role that will see you work with a high-end product, and engage with homeowners, builders and design professionals. You'll guide customers through their purchasing journey from initial enquiry through to final delivery.

THE PERKS
  • Full-time, permanent opportunity with regular business hours
  • Monday-Friday, 8:30am-5:00pm, no late nights or weekends
  • Pagewood location with onsite parking (car required for occasional client visits)
  • Realistic OTE circa $250,000 (base + super + commission + car allowance)
  • Premium, design-led product with strong market demand
  • Supportive, close-knit team environment with full product training
  • Amazing office with onsite gym & wellness facilities and a fully stocked kitchen
  • Opportunity to work autonomously on high-value, rewarding projects
THE DAY-TO-DAY
  • Managing inbound enquiries and proactively following up leads
  • Welcoming clients into the showroom and conducting consultations
  • Attending occasional site visits to understand project scope, requirements and progress
  • Presenting solutions that balance compliance, practicality and design 
  • Preparing quotes, managing negotiations and closing sales
  • Attending trade shows, site visits and handovers
  • Keeping clients informed at every stage of the project
  • Coordinating project documentation and updating CRM systems
YOUR SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Experience in sales, BDM, B2B or a consultative client-facing role
  • Confident building relationships with a range of stakeholders including homeowners, builders and designers
  • Comfortable following up leads as well as new business development
  • Strong communication skills with a personable, professional approach
  • Exposure to construction, residential projects, building plans or design, or keen to learn
  • Experience with premium high-value products would be ideal
  • Organised with solid admin and CRM capability
  • A proactive, positive mindset with a willingness to learn
You'll be joining a well-regarded business that values quality and service, delivering solutions that elevate both functionality and design of client homes.

If you enjoy relationship-driven sales and a premium product, APPLY NOW or contact Sonja or Will at SMAART Recruitment on 1300 762 278 for a confidential chat.

content.jobHook: Organisation's culture:  honest and authentic - dynamic team!
content.unEditedContent:
•   You choose – 5 days or 4 days

  •   Newly created role

  •   Hybrid working arrangements with city offices

 

Micale Recruitment is  delighted to partner with our client, a leading, national professional organisation dedicated to advancing standards practice, education and research in the health sector in Australia.  We are seeking an experienced and motivated Executive Officer to support the Office of the CEO. You will demonstrate strong initiative, sound judgement, exceptional attention to detail and outstanding stakeholder management skills.

About the Role The Executive Officer (EO) is responsible for the efficient operation of the Office of the CEO, providing high- level administrative support to the CEO and the provision of confidential executive administration services to support the achievement of the organisation’s strategic and operational objectives. 

Responsibilities include but not limited to:

  • Manage and maintain CEO schedule, including appointments, meetings, and travel arrangements. Schedule, organise, and coordinate meetings and events, including preparing agendas, developing minutes, and ensuring follow-up on action items.

  • Prepare and edit correspondence, communications, presentations, and other documents. Maintain confidential files and records, ensuring they are well-organised and easily accessible. Conduct research and compile data to support executive decision-making.

  • Serve as a point of contact between the CEO and the Board, Faculties, Members and external stakeholders, managing information flow and communication.  Screen and direct emails, and other correspondence, responding on behalf of the CEO when appropriate.

  • Support Board governance by scheduling meetings, support preparing agenda and papers, maintain accurate records, and ensure compliance with the Constitution, By-laws and ACNC requirements.

  •   Arrange detailed travel plans, itineraries, and agendas for CEO, handling travel-related tasks such as coordinating flights, accommodations, transportation, and resolving any travel issues.

  • Assist with special projects as assigned, providing project management support and ensuring timely completion. Handle miscellaneous tasks to support the CEO as required.

  • Strategic Support: Conduct research, prepare reports and provide briefs that inform executive decision-making with a focus on insights and impact.

  • Benchmark and implement best practice in workflows and maintain efficient organisational systems for document and information management.

What you will bring:

  • Demonstrated 5+ years’ experience in providing exceptional support at the C-suite executive level

  • Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to work collaboratively with stakeholders at all levels.

  • Exceptional organisational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks, manage time effectively, and meet competing deadlines. 

  • Well-developed verbal and communication skills, including the ability to analyse and present information to a diverse range of stakeholders.

  • IT Systems proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, document management systems and other relevant systems 

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy, with the ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information appropriately.  

  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to troubleshoot issues, analyse data, and implement solutions. 

  • Exceptional organisational skills and strong administrative competence.

  • Ability to work autonomously and proactively, with initiative to successfully achieve tasks.

  • High level of professionalism, discretion and confidentiality.


This role is fast- paced and has substantial responsibility that requires a broad range of skills and the ability to exercise considerable judgement, initiative, discretion and independence while interacting daily with staff across the organisation and with external stakeholders.

 This position attracts an outstanding salary package! For a confidential discussion please contact Rosa on 03 9347 7780 or email your resume and covering letter to rosa@micalerecruitment,com

json.title: Customer Experience Officer

content.jobHook: Join a global multinational industry leader today with a growing Australian operation.
content.unEditedContent:
About SKF

SKF is an international company recognised as a specialist in the manufacture and sale of bearings, seals, power transmission, machine condition monitoring equipment and associated products and services. Our 42,000 employees in 129 countries enjoy exceptional career opportunities, intercultural teamwork and a highly varied professional environment focused on delivering strong operational results.

With offices across Australia, SKF supplies the industrial manufacturing and end-user sectors, including mining, power generation, railways, defence, agriculture, and many others, supporting the industrial aftermarket business through its independent distribution channels to market.

SKF’s purpose is Together, we reimagine rotation for a better tomorrow, creating intelligent and clean solutions for people and the planet.

The Opportunity

Do you love working with customers? Do you pride yourself on delivering quality service with a focus on customer needs in a proactive and timely manner?

SKF has an exciting opportunity for a Customer Experience Officer to join our Customer Experience Team. This role is based in Mentone, VIC. Responsible for managing the end-to-end journey of our key customers, your main duties will include:

  • Responding to customer queries in a timely and effective manner, via phone, email, social media, or chat applications

  • Entry and management of customer orderbook to deliver best possible outcomes in terms of product availability and supply

  • Maintaining our customer information on the Customer Relationship Management System (CRM) - C4C

  • Working closely with our both our Sales, Logistics & Delivery teams

  • Completing customer invoicing

  • Documenting processes and logging technical issues, as well as customer compliments and complaints

  • Identifying customer needs and taking proactive steps to maintain positive experiences

  • General administrative duties

About you

Success in this role requires the ability to gather and interpret customer experience information.

  • 3 years + in customer service or similar role

  • Solid knowledge of online customer engagement platforms and channels

  • Proficiency in MS O-365, especially Excel (advanced) is essential

  • Experience with SAP (Sales and Distribution Module) preferred

  • Aptitude for CRM software (SAP Cloud 4 Customer)

  • Experience in industrial goods or engineering sector with a bearings product knowledge is highly desirable

content.jobHook: Are you an innovative go getter who is passionate about change and driving engagement? Join BrightHR as an Onboarding & Engagement Manager
content.unEditedContent:
At BrightHR, we’re leading the charge in transforming the HR tech landscape with our cutting-edge, all-in-one software solution. With over 110,000 businesses relying on us to simplify and streamline their HR management, we’re committed to supporting businesses at every step of their journey.

Backed by one of the world's largest privately-owned business services groups, we're a market leader in HR, Employment Relations, and Health & Safety advisory.

Due to internal career progression, we have an opportunity for an Onboarding & Engagement Manager to join our team. This is a critical role that requires you to lead an ambitious, hungry team who are responsible for enhancing our client’s experience, optimising process and exceeding service levels. 

Key Responsibilities:
  • Ensure new clients are onboarded within agreed SLAs.
  • Track themes and trends across the wider market which will be shared with the wider business, to drive onboarding and engagement through smarter service delivery.
  • Identify areas of improvement throughout onboarding and engagement 
  • Drive and create innovative material to increase adoption of the service. 
To succeed in this role, you'll bring:
  • Strong team leadership experience 
  • Strong reporting and analytical background
  • Confident navigating priorities with a sense of urgency and professionalism.
  • Exceptional communication and problem-solving skills, with a calm, empathetic approach.
  • The ability to influence and partner with a range of stakeholders 
What you'll get in return:

Working with us is awesome, our Bright Perks continue to be the best in market, some of these include:
  • BrightHR Profit Share – receive an annual bonus based on the business performance.
  • Enhanced Leave – As your career grows, we continue to offer even more enhanced leave up to a maximum of 31 days leave at 5 years!
  • Bright Exchange- Access to 1000's of curated discounts just for you
  • Education Assistance Program - BrightHR values the continued development of our people, and we continue to support you with our Education Assistance Program
  • Career Pathways - move your career forward with clearly defined career pathways 
  • Health & Fitness - We value work life balance, gain access to discounted Gyms and discounted private health insurance 
  • Reward & Recognition - We love to celebrate success with monthly super service awards (get $1K on us as a thank you) and Global MVP awards to celebrate you & your contribution.
Ready to take your marketing career to the next level, APPLY NOW

BrightHR is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates.

**A note to recruitment agencies: We politely ask that you avoid making any approaches or sending any unsolicited resumes**

json.title: Warehouse Assistant

content.jobHook: The ideal candidate will have prior experience working with lubricants and hold a current forklift certification.
content.unEditedContent:
We are recruiting on behalf of one of the world’s most respected energy and lubricant companies; a major global player with operations across more than 100 countries. This is a great opportunity to join their Australian warehouse team, supporting the distribution and logistics of oil & lubricant products.

You will work on-site with the client, gaining hands-on experience in a high-performing, safety-focused environment with world-class standards and career development opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Receive, inspect, and store incoming large goods, bulk lubricants and packaged related products.

  • Pick, pack, and prepare orders for dispatch in accordance with company procedures.

  • Operate forklifts safely and efficiently to move stock around the warehouse.

  • Assist with regular inventory checks.

  • Ensure all products are stored in compliance with safety and environmental standards.

  • Assist with general warehouse housekeeping to maintain a clean and organised work area.

  • Load and unload delivery large bulk tanker vehicles as required.

  • Report any safety hazards, incidents, or equipment faults promptly.


Selection Criteria

  • Previous experience working in a warehouse environment, with preference given to candidates experienced in handling lubricants.

  • Current forklift licence and demonstrated ability to operate forklifts safely.

  • Good understanding of workplace health and safety practices.

  • Ability to follow instructions and work both independently and as part of a team.

  • Strong attention to detail and organisational skills.

  • Physically fit and able to undertake manual handling tasks.

  • Good communication skills and a positive attitude.

Desirable Attributes

  • Familiarity with inventory management systems.

  • Experience working with hazardous materials or chemicals.


Working Conditions

This position is based in Lytton and involves shift work, including

some early mornings or arvos as required. The role requires manual handling, operation

of forklifts and other warehouse equipment, and adherence to strict safety guidelines.

content.jobHook: Eligibility Officer to determine Worker's Comp claims liability. Join our team and make a real impact.
content.unEditedContent:
Introduction

At Gallagher Bassett, we're there when it matters most because helping people through challenging moments is more than just our job, it’s our purpose. Every day, we help clients navigate complexity, support recovery, and deliver outcomes that make a real difference in people’s lives. It takes empathy, precision, and a strong sense of partnership—and that’s exactly what you’ll find here. We’re a team of fast-paced fixers, empathetic experts, and outcomes drivers — people who care deeply about doing the right thing and doing it well. Whether you're managing claims, supporting clients, or improving processes, you’ll play a vital role in helping businesses and individuals move forward with confidence. Here, you’ll be supported by a culture that values teamwork, encourages curiosity, and celebrates the impact of your work. Because when you’re here, you’re part of something bigger. You’re part of a team that shows up, stands together, and leads with purpose.


Overview

See yourself in our team:

We have a great opportunity for an Eligibility Officer to join our team. In this role, you will be the first point of contact responsible for coordinating and obtaining information from key stakeholders to determine the acceptance or rejection of Worker’s Compensation claims in line with legislation. You’ll also be responsible for conducting investigations as necessary to ensure every decision made for new claims are of the highest quality and consideration for our customers.


How you'll make an impact

On a day to day basis you will:

  • Working as part of the Eligibility team to make sustainable, appropriate and quality initial liability determinations for your portfolio of newly lodged Work Cover claims
  • Driving an effective investigatory process in order to make quality initial liability decision
  • Communicating updates and outcomes relating to decisions to both injured workers and employers
  • Providing a quality customer service experience for our internal and external customers
  • Communicating the initial decision rational to the Dispute Resolution Team to support the conciliation process
  • Working together with your Team Manager, Case Managers & Technical Managers and to determine liability and review of entitlement

About you

We’re looking for

  • Claims management experience is desirable, but transferable skills in Customer Service & Administration are essential 
  • Exceptional time management and organisational skills and the ability to prioritise your tasks
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and a team-player attitude
  • An aptitude for working within a dynamic, fast paced and challenging environment

Compensation and benefits

On top of a competitive salary, great teams and exciting career opportunities, we also offer a wide range of benefits. 

Below are the minimum core benefits you’ll get, depending on your job level these benefits may improve:

  • 4 weeks annual leave plus up to 2 weeks additional purchased Lifestyle Leave
  • Novated Leasing opportunities
  • Two paid volunteer days annually
  • Health Insurance Discounts with our Group Insurance Plan
  • Employee Stock Purchase Program
  • Paid parental leave

Other benefits include:

  • Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
  • Mental Health and Wellbeing Support for yourself and immediate family members
  • Employee Recognition Awards and Service Milestone Recognitions
  • Peer Support Program
  • Annual flu vaccinations
  • Access to Reward Gateway – discount offers at over 350 retailers!
  • And more...

We value inclusion and diversity

Inclusion and diversity (I&D) is a core part of our business, and it’s embedded into the fabric of our organization. For more than 95 years, Gallagher has led with a commitment to sustainability and to support the communities where we live and work.

Gallagher embraces our employees’ diverse identities, experiences and talents, allowing us to better serve our clients and communities. We see inclusion as a conscious commitment and diversity as a vital strength. By embracing diversity in all its forms, we live out The Gallagher Way to its fullest.

Gallagher believes that all persons are entitled to equal employment opportunity and prohibits any form of discrimination by its managers, employees, vendors or customers based on race, color, religion, creed, gender (including pregnancy status), sexual orientation, gender identity (which includes transgender and other gender non-conforming individuals), gender expression, hair expression, marital status, parental status, age, national origin, ancestry, disability, medical condition, genetic information, veteran or military status, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected (herein referred to as “protected characteristics”) by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

Equal employment opportunity will be extended in all aspects of the employer-employee relationship, including, but not limited to, recruitment, hiring, training, promotion, transfer, demotion, compensation, benefits, layoff, and termination. In addition, Gallagher will make reasonable accommodations to known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified person with a disability, unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on the operation of our business.

On a day to day basis you will:
Working as part of the Eligibility team to make sustainable, appropriate and quality initial liability determinations for your portfolio of newly lodged Work Cover claims
Driving an effective investigatory process in order to make quality initial liability decision
Communicating updates and outcomes relating to decisions to both injured workers and employers
Providing a quality customer service experience for our internal and external customers
Communicating the initial decision rational to the Dispute Resolution Team to support the conciliation process
Working together with your Team Manager, Case Managers & Technical Managers and to determine liability and review of entitlement
About you
We’re looking for
Claims management experience is desirable, but transferable skills in Customer Service & Administration are essential
Exceptional time management and organisational skills and the ability to prioritise your tasks
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and a team-player attitude
An aptitude for working within a dynamic, fast paced and challenging environment
Compensation and benefits
On top of a competitive salary, great teams and exciting career opportunities, we also offer a wide range of benefits.
Below are the minimum core benefits you’ll get, depending on your job level these benefits may improve:
4 weeks annual leave plus up to 2 weeks additional purchased Lifestyle Leave
Novated Leasing opportunities
Two paid volunteer days annually
Health Insurance Discounts with our Group Insurance Plan
Employee Stock Purchase Program
Paid parental leave
Other benefits include:
Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
Mental Health and Wellbeing Support for yourself and immediate family members
Employee Recognition Awards and Service Milestone Recognitions
Peer Support Program
Annual flu vaccinations
Access to Reward Gateway – discount offers at over 350 retailers!
And more...
We value inclusion and diversity

Inclusion and diversity (I&D) is a core part of our business, and it’s embedded into the fabric of our organization. For more than 95 years, Gallagher has led with a commitment to sustainability and to support the communities where we live and work.

Gallagher embraces our employees’ diverse identities, experiences and talents, allowing us to better serve our clients and communities. We see inclusion as a conscious commitment and diversity as a vital strength. By embracing diversity in all its forms, we live out The Gallagher Way to its fullest.

Gallagher believes that all persons are entitled to equal employment opportunity and prohibits any form of discrimination by its managers, employees, vendors or customers based on race, color, religion, creed, gender (including pregnancy status), sexual orientation, gender identity (which includes transgender and other gender non-conforming individuals), gender expression, hair expression, marital status, parental status, age, national origin, ancestry, disability, medical condition, genetic information, veteran or military status, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected (herein referred to as “protected characteristics”) by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

Equal employment opportunity will be extended in all aspects of the employer-employee relationship, including, but not limited to, recruitment, hiring, training, promotion, transfer, demotion, compensation, benefits, layoff, and termination. In addition, Gallagher will make reasonable accommodations to known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified person with a disability, unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on the operation of our business.

content.unEditedContent:
LO-GO Appointments is a national boutique recruitment agency, which has been providing recruitment and HR solutions to Western Australian Councils for over 30 years. We specialise in the provision of high-quality staff covering the full range of Council activities from Executive Management to Technical, Office and on-site Field positions. We work exclusively within the Local Government industry with our WA office being based in the heart of Subiaco.
  
We currently have an exciting opportunity for a Recruitment Consultant who enjoys a challenge and thrives on providing exceptional customer service to join our team.
  
This position requires a pro-active individual with excellent time management and organisational skills, the ability to communicate with people at all levels and a real passion to find the best candidates for the right roles.

Click apply now and provide your resume and cover letter and we will be in contact with you for a confidential discussion about the role.
   
Alternatively, if you have any queries please call Laura Russo, Manager WA on 08 9380 4505 or email wa@logoapp.com.au

content.unEditedContent:
Supermarket Store Manager

We are seeking an experienced and highly capable Supermarket Store Manager to oversee the daily operations of our independently owned supermarket in Glenroy VIC.

This is a subcontracting position for an experienced operator who can confidently manage the store, staff, stock control, and day-to-day operations with minimal supervision.

We are currently completing an onboarding process with the existing owner over the coming weeks and require someone who can step into a leadership role and ensure the smooth ongoing operation of the business.

The store currently operates with approximately 20 existing part-time staff.

This role is ideal for an experienced supermarket professional looking for long-term stability, autonomy, and the opportunity to take ownership of store performance and operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Oversee all daily store operations

  • Lead, supervise, and manage staff

  • Rostering and labour management

  • Stock ordering and inventory control

  • Supplier management and coordination

  • Ensure excellent customer service standards

  • Manage merchandising and store presentation

  • Monitor store performance, sales, and profitability

  • Minimise stock loss and wastage

  • Ensure compliance with food safety and workplace procedures

  • Drive accountability, efficiency, and team culture

  • Problem solve operational issues independently

About You

  • Previous experience managing a supermarket or large retail store

  • Strong leadership and staff management experience

  • Confident with stock ordering and inventory systems

  • Able to work independently and take ownership of operations

  • Strong understanding of supermarket workflows and procedures

  • Excellent organisational and communication skills

  • Reliable, proactive, and solutions-focused

  • Experience managing rosters, wages, and operational costs

Position Details

  • Subcontracting position

  • Consistent weekly hours provided

  • Hours and roster structure can be discussed with the successful applicant

  • Long-term opportunity for the right candidate

Salary / Package

  • $2,320 per week contractor rate

  • Monthly performance bonuses based on store performance and KPIs

  • Long-term opportunity with autonomy and stability

content.unEditedContent:
About the role

We’re searching for a Conservation Program Officer to join our passionate team.

Reporting to the Area Manager this role supports the delivery of Trust for Nature’s key conservation programs including the Covenanting Program, Stewardship Program, Offsets Program, Revolving Fund Program, and BushBank Program through the North West area of Victoria. The role will act as a point of contact between Trust for Nature and conservation covenantors and potential landholders in the catchment.

The role is based in Castlemaine office with regular travel throughout North West Victoria.  The key focus of the role will be landholder engagement, ecological assessment of areas protected by conservation covenants, discussions with landholders about conservation management techniques and the development of conservation management plans.

To read more about the responsibilities of the role take a look at the Position Description.

What’s on offer

This is a part time (0.8 FTE) fixed term contract for two years.

The role offers an annual salary range of $71,117 – $76,083 plus 12% super, the pro rata amount based on 0.8 FTE is $56,893 – $60,866. The salary offered will be aligned with the candidates’ experience.

The role operates in a hybrid model, with a blend of work from home, face to face days and field work. Regular travel throughout the North West region is a core part of the role and therefor a driver’s licence is required.

About you

We are searching for someone who is passionate about conservation who is looking to grow their career in the Environmental sector. The successful candidate will bring;

  • A degree in natural resource management, ecology, or other environmental science.
  • At least 2 years of field-work experience.
  • Understanding of land management practices, and understanding of Ecological Vegetation Communities, flora and fauna, common threats, and recommended management actions.
  • Sound written and verbal communication skills, including technical report writing.
  • Excellent time management skills and flexibility to reprioritise workload.
  • Experience liaising with a range of stakeholders including land managers.

This role offers a strong foundation for developing your conservation career while contributing to meaningful, long-term protection of biodiversity on private land across Victoria.

companyProfile.overview: Our native plants and wildlife provide us with not only important services, such as clean water and resources, but they are important in and of themselves., However, as two-thirds of Victoria is privately owned, many of these species and their habitats are not currently getting the necessary protection., The Trust was established under the Victorian Conservation Trust Act 1972 to enable people to contribute permanently to nature conservation by donating land or money., We have since evolved into one of Victoria’s primary land conservation organisations, with several tools to help people protect biodiversity on private land., In 1978, Trust for Nature developed conservation covenants as a way to protect native plants and wildlife on private land, and we have now protected more than 58,000 hectares through over 1,300 perpetual conservation covenants., The Trust has also purchased and preserved more than 59 properties across Victoria through its Revolving Fund, as well as currently owning and managing 44 properties that cover over 36,000 hectares of Victoria., Source: This is an extract from the company's own website.

content.jobHook: Join MTM as a Rail Protection Coordinator. Safeworking 3.2 mandatory.
content.unEditedContent:
Melbourne is Australia's fastest growing city, and public transport is vital to keeping it moving. Since 2009, Metro has proudly operated and maintained a world-class train service and delivered major transport projects that shape the future of our city. Guided by our value of Safely Always, we are one team dedicated to ensuring everyone gets home safely while helping to connect and create a better Melbourne.



We are looking for an experienced Occupation Safeworking Planner to play a key role in the safe planning and delivery of Facilities occupations across the network. In this role, you'll ensure works are carried out safely, efficiently, and with minimal disruption to passengers. You will provide expert guidance, coordinate access, and help drive continuous improvement in safeworking practices.

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan and coordinate safeworking protection for all Facilities occupations, resolving clashes and ensuring alignment across Infrastructure and internal teams
  • Assess and manage passenger-facing impacts, working closely with MTM Operations on disruptive and non‑disruptive occupation planning
  • Assist with safeworking queries, providing safeworking advice and resourcing numbers
  • Support the development of safeworking policies, procedures, and best-practice frameworks
  • Work collaboratively with AROs, Projects and Third Parties to ensure access, streamlined occupations and successful work delivery
  • Conduct onsite visits to carry out safeworking risk assessments for upcoming occupations.
  • Design Protection Diagrams using Adobe software in accordance with all current Metro policies and procedures.

About You

  • TFPC Level 3.2
  • Minimum 3 years' experience in safeworking, rail operations, and network environments
  • Ability to work under pressure, manage competing priorities and meet tight deadlines
  • Experience with Adobe InDesign and Photoshop (preferred)

If you're a dedicated safeworking professional looking to contribute to the safe and reliable delivery of rail operations, we encourage you to apply now.
