content.jobHook: Rewarding career in environment, supporting safe, sustainable operations
content.unEditedContent:
Advisor Environment | Yarwun

  • Global mining and mineral processing organisation with an exceptional safety culture
  • Competitive salary and benefits
  • Supporting Yarwun Operations | Residential in Gladstone, QLD
  • Permanent Full Time | Mon to Friday - 9-day fortnight

About the role

Finding better ways to provide the materials the world needs.

We are looking for a site-based Environment Advisor to join our HSE team at Rio Tinto Yarwun.

In this role you will partner with site operations and other service function professionals to champion Environmental, Safety and Health performance. This is a great opportunity for an Environmental Advisor who strives for excellence and enjoys working on both core functions and dynamic project work.

We are an open, connected global team that includes some of the industry's best professionals and developing talent. We offer competitive, performance-based remuneration and a wide range of benefits to reward your contribution. With a global reach, the opportunities to develop and grow your career are broad and exciting.

Reporting to the Superintendent Environment, and working as part of a team of environmental professionals, you will be:

  • Partnering with operations and maintenance teams and stakeholders to support environmental risk management & reduction.
  • Implementing and verifying the business' Integrated Environmental Management System alongside other Rio Systems.
  • Managing a range of environmental issues, for example: fauna/flora, surface and ground water quality, stormwater and erosion control, marine environment impacts, air emissions, extraction, land clearing & rehabilitation activities & offset area management.
  • Project management of contractors and consultants providing environmental services.
  • Providing environmental advice in the interpretation of legislation, acts and regulations.
  • Preparing and submitting compliance and investigation assessment reports in association with our licence to operate.
  • Collating, reviewing and interpreting data for internal Rio Tinto and statutory reporting purposes.

What you'll bring

  • A Bachelor's degree in an Environmental (or related discipline) with knowledge of key concepts theories and practices related to environmental aspects & impacts, risk management, State and Federal Legislation and integrated environmental management systems.
  • Knowledge of Management Systems ISO 14000:1 and the Queensland Environment regulatory framework.
  • Relevant industry (large scale mineral processing or chemical manufacturing) or mining experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in executing work with a strong attitude towards environmental, health & safety improvement.
  • Excellent communication and partnering skills with the ability to work both independently & as part of a multidisciplinary.
  • Resilience and a dynamic approach to problem solving.

What we offer

  • A work environment where safety is always the number one priority.
  • A competitive base salary reflective of your skills and experience with annual incentive program.
  • Comprehensive medical benefits including subsidised private health insurance & access to health and medical wellbeing support for employees and immediate family.
  • Attractive share ownership plan.
  • Company provided insurance cover.
  • Extensive salary sacrifice & salary packaging options.
  • Career development & education assistance to further your technical or leadership ambitions.
  • Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation/annual, paid parental, sick leave)
  • Exclusive employee discounts (banking, accommodation, cars, retail and more); and
  • Relocation packages where suitable for Australian based citizens only

About Rio Tinto

Rio Tinto is a leading global mining and materials company. We operate in 35 countries where we produce iron ore, copper, aluminium, critical minerals, and other materials needed for the global energy transition and for people, communities, and nations to thrive.

We have been mining for 150 years and operate with knowledge built up across generations and continents. Our purpose is finding better ways to provide the materials the world needs - striving for innovation and continuous improvement to produce materials with low emissions and to the right environmental, social and governance standards. But we can't do it on our own, so we're focused on creating partnerships to solve problems, create win-win and meet opportunities.

Where you'll be working

With production beginning in 2004 at our Yarwun alumina refinery, located approximately 10 kilometres north-west of Gladstone in Central Queensland, today the operation produces more than three million tonnes of alumina per year. Thanks to its 'Industry 4.0' focus, Yarwun is also a leader in trialling new technologies to improve operations on site, including hydrogen generation, biofuels and is home to Rio Tinto's innovative Queensland Research and Development Centre (QRDC). Along with Boyne Smelters Limited and Queensland Alumina Limited, our Yarwun Operation supports the local community in a wide range of initiatives through Here for Gladstone.

Respect and Inclusion

At Rio Tinto, we particularly welcome and encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, women, the LGBTI+ community, mature workers, people with disabilities and people from different cultural backgrounds.

We are committed to an inclusive environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome - they are essential to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation or anything else that makes us different.

About the Role:

We’re seeking an experienced electrician for a major infrastructure project in Cairns. The role involves overseeing and inspecting electrical installation works by multiple contractors, ensuring compliance with contract documentation, Australian Standards, and site QA requirements. You’ll be representing a professional electrical contracting business and liaising directly with project managers, site supervisors, and client QA teams.

The project is nearing completion of construction and preparing to enter its commissioning / close out stages.

Key Details:

• Start Date: June 2026

• Duration: Approx. 6 - 9 months, potentially ongoing

• Hours: 40+ per week

• Location: Cairns

• Rate: Negotiable hourly rate + super (ABN or casual arrangement)

Responsibilities:

• Complete project hold & witness points on behalf of the project administration team

• Carry out electrical works surveillance and maintain daily records

• Review and verify installation quality and compliance

• Coordinate with site electrical contractors, stakeholders and QA teams

• Identify and communicate non-conformances and improvements

Requirements:

• QLD Electrical Licence

• QLD Drivers Licence / Vehicle Preferred

• Post Trade 5+ years

• Strong understanding of AS/NZS 3000 and related standards

• Industrial or infrastructure project experience highly regarded

• Strong computer literacy skills, administrative experience (Microsoft office, microsoft teams, third party software/apps, photos, emails, reporting)

• QLD General Construction Induction Card

content.unEditedContent:
Want a role where a competitive salary doesn’t assume Saturday work?

Want your weekends back and still get paid overtime if Saturday work is required?

This could be the role for you!

Who We Are and What We Stand For

Vaughan Civil are one of the industry’s leading Civil Utility Infrastructure Specialists across the eastern coast with a presence in NSW and QLD. We put our steady growth and trusted reputation with our clients down to our people. Our staff, both site and office, are instrumental to our continued growth and achievements. We are looking for a Senior Project Engineer to join the Engineering Delivery team in QLD.

Competencies Required for the Role

• Demonstrated civil engineering experience.

• Experience in the water and waste sector.

• Ability to coordinate all aspects of a projects and deliver key construction requirements in line with safety, quality, budget & time.

• Knowledge of the relevant legislation, standards and codes of practice.

• Understanding contractual agreements, preparing claims and dispute management.

• Provide planning, technical advice, and support to ensure a successful project delivery.

• Expert leadership and negotiation skills.

  • Competitive Salary
  • Opportunity for Career Progression
  • No built-in Saturday work
  • Paid overtime if Saturdays are required.
  • Friendly and supportive work environment
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Company Vehicle and additional benefits

Apply today!

Please note that only successful candidates will be contacted.

We encourage applications from Australian Defence Force veterans and reservists and value the transferable skills gained through military service, including leadership, teamwork, and problem solving.

content.jobHook: Lead a thriving medical practice with competitive salary, professional development, and genuine work-life balance.
content.unEditedContent:
About the role

We are establishing a brand new, state-of-the-art medical centre in the heart of Gungahlin, one of the fastest-growing regions in Australia. This is an exciting opportunity to lead the direction of a new general practice.

What you'll be doing

  • Overseeing all administrative and operational aspects of the practice, including patient flow, staffing, budgeting, and compliance

  • Developing and implementing policies and procedures to ensure the efficient and effective delivery of patient care

  • Managing the practice's financial operations, including billing, invoicing, and financial reporting

  • Leading and motivating a team of administrative and clinical staff, providing guidance and support as needed

  • Fostering a positive and collaborative work environment that promotes high levels of patient satisfaction

  • Liaising with healthcare providers, insurers, and other external stakeholders to maintain strong relationships and support the practice's growth

  • Staying up-to-date with industry regulations, trends, and best practices, and implementing changes as necessary

What we're looking for

  • Minimum of 3 years' experience in a similar Practice Manager or senior administrative role within the healthcare industry

  • Strong understanding of medical practice operations, including patient flow, billing, and compliance requirements

  • Excellent leadership and people management skills, with the ability to motivate and develop a team

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders

  • Demonstrated problem-solving and decision-making abilities, with a focus on efficient and effective process improvement

  • Proficient in the use of practice management software and other relevant technology

  • Tertiary qualification in healthcare management, business administration, or a related field is highly desirable

What we offer

We are committed to providing a supportive and flexible work environment that enables our employees to thrive. In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a range of benefits, including:

  • Opportunities for professional development and career advancement

  • Generous leave entitlements and a focus on work-life balance

  • Subsidised healthcare and wellness initiatives

  • A collaborative and inclusive team culture

We encourage applications from candidates with a disability. If you require any adjustments or alternate formats of key information at any stage of the recruitment process, we welcome hearing from you.

Apply now to join our dynamic team as our Practice Manager.

content.jobHook: The role of Cleaning Supervisor is to establish cleaning schedules and assign Cleaners under their supervision to varying tasks and duties.
content.unEditedContent:
Riverside Christian College is a rapidly growing Prep – 12 independent Christian College located in Maryborough, Queensland providing both Day School and Distance Education. 

Riverside Christian College is a contemporary and innovative school, developing world-first educational initiatives for students. Our vision is to provide quality Christian education that develops character and empowers students to impact their community. 

The College is a supportive and respectful environment defined by its Christian ethos and values framework reflecting and encouraging behaviours aligned with our College values of Excellence, Teamwork, Respect, Faith and Community. To do this we strive to be leaders of excellence in Teaching and Learning, Faith Development, Community Engagement and Organisational rigour. 


The role of Cleaning Supervisor is to establish cleaning schedules and assign Cleaners under their supervision to varying tasks and duties, ensuring they have the right equipment and supplies to complete their work. This role will report to the College Facilities Manager to assist in maintaining high standards across the College and may include administrative duties to support reporting and quality assurance purposes.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Establish cleaning schedules for Cleaners, ensuring that tasks are carried out effectively, efficiently, and to a high standard.
  • Inspect cleaning equipment, storage areas, and supplies on a regular basis.
  • Control and monitor the usage of cleaning materials to minimise waste.
  • Provide training, guidance, and supervision to staff whilst working in a hands-on role.
  • Ensure all staff follow correct policies and procedure including reporting, hazard identification and risk management whilst actively promoting a positive and safe work environment.
  • Assist in the development, implementation and review of processes and practices in line with industry standards.
  • Inspect, monitor, and align cleaning standards with effective quality assurance practices. 
  • Build and maintain effective stakeholder relationships, both internally and externally.
  • Assist and advise in planning for term break periodicals and event support

POSITION REQUIREMENTS

  • Hold a current Blue Card or aquire prior to employment.
  • Supervisory experience with the ability to train and lead a team (essential).
  • A good understanding of WHS in the workplace.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and in a small team environment.
  • Self-motivated and the ability to work under pressure, use own initiative to prioritise work and multi-task to meet deadlines.
  • Exceptional customer service and a professional manner.
  • Highly organised with an eye for detail.

content.jobHook: Embedded within the Carborough operations team, work closely with site Superintendents supporting operational decision-making.
content.unEditedContent:
Carborough Downs underground Bord and Pillar mine is located in Queensland’s Bowen Basin, approximately 30km north-east of Moranbah and 160km from Mackay and forms part of the broader Argo Complex. This integrated mining complex includes the Ironbark Longwall Pit and Broadlea Open Cut, as well as a centralised Coal Handling and Preparation Plant (CHPP), where collaboration between our sites and teams is key to delivering safe and efficient outcomes.

WAHT THIS OPPORTUNITY ABOUT

Reporting to the General Manager (SSE), this position is is embedded within the Carborough operations team, working closely with site Superintendents to support day-to-day financial management, reports and operational decision-making. At the same time, the role is supported by the broader Complex Finance and Corporate teams providing access to wider systems and strategic guidance enabling the role to maintain a strong operational focus.

  • Monitor and analyse performance, including variance analysis, to identify trends and areas for improvement 

  • Provide management accounting support and consolidated reporting across multiple departments 

  • Lead the budgeting, reforecasting, and reporting processes for both Opex and Capex 

  • Prepare and deliver weekly KPI reports to key stakeholders 

  • Assist in the completion of audits, ensuring compliance and accuracy 

  • Lead and support ad hoc projects focused on process improvements 

  • Continuously assess and improve direct spending, balance sheet risks, opportunities, and overall profitability 

  • Facilitate monthly cost review meetings, collaborating with relevant teams to drive cost control initiatives 

  • Review and assess capital applications and out-of-budget operational requests to ensure alignment with financial goals 

  • Manage end-of-month processes, including journal entries, stock revaluation, and preparation of monthly management reports

 WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU

  • Willingness to be site-based; this position is hands-on and requires you to build strong relationships on the ground

  • Applicants who have on-site experience within the mining/construction industry will have an advantage, but if you are an experienced accountant we encourage you to apply if a site based position is your next career move!

  • Hold the relevant tertiary qualifications (CA/CPA or working towards it)

  • The ability to tailor communication to all levels of the business

  • Have strong attention to detail, a structured approach to work, and a skillset for reporting and delivering accurate financial insights

  • Strong Excel and systems skills, with the ability to efficiently extract, analyse, and interpret data

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

  • 5 / 2 / 4 / 3 roster, every second Friday off!

  • Ideally this position suits someone based in the Moranbah, Mackay, Airlie Beach areas or someone willing to relocate to them

  • Accommodation is provided and flexible based on your home location

  • Highly attractive remuneration and other benefits such as Health Insurance available

  • Carborough Downs and the broader Complex has a great site team culture with a leadership team that genuinely supports each other and wants to see everyone succeed - APPLY NOW!

content.jobHook: Part time Community Physiotherapist – Hybrid Role (Clinic + Community) - Melbourne North and West
content.unEditedContent:
Community Physiotherapist – Hybrid Role (Clinic + Community) - Melbourne North and West

PhysioFirst and Glowing Therapy Group

This excellent opportunity to join our expanding multidisciplinary team at PhysioFirst and Glowing Therapy Group would support you providing treatment options for clients across Melbourne.

The ideal candidate will have a passion helping others improve their lives through health and wellness. Experience and confidence working with all client levels in a safe manner as you will support clients to achieve their goals at home and in the community.

PhysioFirst and Glowing Therapy offers Allied Health services such as Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy, Exercise Physiology, Osteopath and Podiatry.

About the Role

We're looking for a Part time Community Physiotherapist to join our growing allied health service, delivering high quality, person centred physiotherapy across NDIS and Aged Care (Support at Home Packages), with opportunities to work with clients funded through other programs.

This is a genuinely hybrid role, designed to make community work sustainable and professionally rewarding.

Your week will include a mix of:

·         Home visits (NDIS & Aged Care clients)

·         In‑clinic appointments

·         Therapy delivered in community environments where appropriate (e.g. parks, hydrotherapy, swimming pools, schools or community venues)


You'll manage a mixed adult and paediatric caseload, including:

·         Disability (e.g. autism, cerebral palsy)

·         Neurological conditions (e.g. stroke, Parkinson's disease)

·         Age‑related conditions and post‑hospital discharge support


What We Can Offer


·         Structured onboarding and mentoring (particularly for clinicians newer to community work).

·         Flexible scheduling to support sustainable community practice.

·         Travel allowance.

·         Laptop and mobile phone provided.

·         Weekly supervision and team meetings.

·         Clinical and administrative support for NDIS report writing, care planning and funding navigation.


What You’ll Be Doing


·         Conducting comprehensive physiotherapy assessments and developing evidence based treatment plans

·         Delivering tailored physiotherapy interventions in community settings, clients’ homes and residential care facilities

·         Supporting individuals with mobility, strength, balance, pain management and functional goals

·         Working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, families and support coordinators

·         Contributing to documentation, outcome tracking and quality driven practice


REQUIREMENTS


  • Physiotherapy Degree 

  • AHPRA Registration 

  • Personal indemnity and professional liability insurance

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to establish rapport with clients

  • A desire to provide premium care options and experiences

  • Ability to work as part of a team as well as autonomously

  • Working with children check

  • Be willing to undertake a National Police check 

  • Valid Driver’s licence


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

This role starts as part-time (2–3 days per week), with a pathway to full time.

We have flexible working hours to suit your lifestyle

Excellent salary and commission structure

We look forward to meeting you!

content.jobHook: If you are looking to join a reputable and growing civil contractor where your contribution is valued, we would love to hear from you.
content.unEditedContent:
Quantum Civil is a growing civil construction company delivering high-quality commercial civil infrastructure projects across Victoria. We pride ourselves on professionalism, strong client relationships, and delivering projects safely, efficiently, and to a high standard. Due to continued growth, we are seeking an experienced and motivated Contract Administrator to join our team.

About the Role

Reporting directly to the Directors and Project Managers, you will play a key role in the commercial administration and delivery of civil construction projects from commencement through to final completion.

This role is suited to someone who has strong contract administration experience within the civil construction industry and understands the fast-paced nature of commercial projects.

Key Responsibilities

  • Contract administration and project commercial management

  • Preparing, assessing, and managing progress claims and variations

  • Reviewing subcontractor claims, invoices, and purchase orders

  • Procurement and subcontract administration

  • Cost tracking, forecasting, and budget management

  • Assisting with project programming and delivery coordination

  • Managing project documentation and contractual correspondence

  • Supporting compliance with contractual obligations and project requirements

  • Liaising with clients, subcontractors, suppliers, and consultants

About You

  • Previous experience in a Contract Administrator role within civil construction

  • Strong understanding of commercial construction contracts and project delivery

  • Experience with variations, progress claims, and subcontract management

  • Excellent communication and negotiation skills

  • High attention to detail and strong organisational skills

  • Ability to work independently and within a team environment

  • Proficient in Microsoft Office and construction management systems

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary package based on experience

  • Opportunity to work on diverse commercial civil projects

  • Supportive and professional team environment

  • Long-term career growth opportunities within a growing company

  • Immediate start available for the right candidate

If you are looking to join a reputable and growing civil contractor where your contribution is valued, we would love to hear from you.

content.jobHook: Store Manager – Town & Country Pizza & Pasta Warrnambool
content.unEditedContent:
Store Manager – Town & Country Pizza & Pasta Warrnambool

We are the local franchise owners of Town & Country Pizza & Pasta Warrnambool, and we are looking for a motivated, reliable, and hands-on Store Manager to join our team.

This is a great opportunity for someone local to Warrnambool who enjoys hospitality, leading people, and being part of a busy, community-focused business.

About the role

As Store Manager, you will help us run the day-to-day operations of our Warrnambool store and lead a team of local staff. You will be hands-on during service, support the team, maintain high standards, and help create a great experience for every customer who walks through the door or orders from us.

You will work closely with us as the franchise owners, with support from the wider Town & Country Pizza & Pasta network.

What you’ll be doing

  • Leading, training, and supporting our team

  • Managing daily store operations

  • Making sure customers receive friendly and reliable service

  • Maintaining high food quality, cleanliness, and food safety standards

  • Helping with rosters, staff performance, and team culture

  • Managing stock, ordering, and waste control

  • Working hands-on during busy periods

  • Helping grow the store within the local Warrnambool community

  • Creating a positive workplace where people enjoy coming to work

About you

We are looking for someone who is:

  • Local to Warrnambool or the surrounding area

  • Experienced in hospitality, takeaway, fast food, retail, or team leadership

  • A confident communicator who can lead by example

  • Reliable, organised, and calm under pressure

  • Hands-on and willing to jump in wherever needed

  • Customer-focused and proud of doing things properly

  • Available to work nights and weekends as part of a rotating roster

Previous pizza, takeaway, or restaurant management experience would be great, but it is not essential. We are just as interested in finding the right person with the right attitude.

What we offer

  • A full-time management role in a local Warrnambool business

  • Training and support from the Town & Country Pizza & Pasta franchise network

  • A supportive working environment with local owners who care about their team

  • Opportunity to grow with the store

  • A hands-on role where your effort will make a real difference

  • Competitive salary based on experience

About us

Town & Country Pizza & Pasta has been serving communities since 1989, and we are proud to bring the brand to Warrnambool.

As local franchise owners, we want to build a strong team, create a great workplace, and serve quality food to the Warrnambool community.

How to apply

Please apply through SEEK with your resume and a short cover letter telling us about yourself, your experience, and why you would be a great fit for our Warrnambool store.


Contact:

tncwarrnambool@gmail.com

content.unEditedContent:
Physiotherapist – Sunshine Coast Hinterland

Flexible Part-Time or Full-Time Opportunity

At Hinterland Physio Group, we believe great physiotherapy comes from clinicians who enjoy both the work they do and the life they live outside of it. We value community and lifestyle.

That’s why we’ve built a clinic environment that values:

·       Quality patient care  

·       Genuine team support

·       Professional growth

·       And the Sunshine Coast Hinterland lifestyle that drew us all here in the first place.

We are currently looking for an experienced Physiotherapist to join our growing team across our Woombye and Palmwoods clinics, with opportunities to make a big impact on people’s lives in under-serviced areas with work in our rural outreach clinics in Kenilworth and Kilkivan.

Why Choose Hinterland Physio Group

We invite you to join:

·       A team of 6 experienced physiotherapists (all with 10+ years’ experience)

·       A supportive and down-to-earth clinic culture

·       A practice focused on personalised, person-centred care

·       A growing business where clinicians are supported to pursue their interest areas and continually grow both personally and professionally


This role offers a variety across:

·       Musculoskeletal physiotherapy

·       Sports injury management

·       Sporting team coverage

·       Supporting people through Aged Care, DVA, NDIS and home visits

·       Workcover and insurance rehabilitation

·       Rural and community-based physiotherapy

What We’re Looking For

We’d love to hear from physiotherapists who:

·       Have 5+ years private practice experience

·       Enjoy building strong patient relationships

·       Are confident managing musculoskeletal conditions independently

·       Have an interest in sports, rural or community physiotherapy

·       Value teamwork, communication and high-quality care

What We Offer

·       Flexible part-time or full-time hours

·       Competitive retainer + commission structure

·       45-minute initial appointments

·       Daily admin time built into your schedule

·       Newly renovated, purpose-built clinics

·       $1,000 annual CPD allowance

·       Support to develop your clinical interests or speciality area

·       Team social events and a genuinely supportive culture

·       A roster designed to support work-life balance

Requirements:

·       Tertiary qualification in Physiotherapy

·       AHPRA Registration

·       Professional indemnity insurance

·       Valid Australians Drivers licence (required for home visits)

·       Existing working rights in Australia 

·       Ability to work one 7:30am start and one 6:00pm finish / week

Application:

content.jobHook: Permanent - Part Time, Permanent - Full Time, Fixed Term - Full Time, Fixed Term - Part Time
content.unEditedContent:
We are seeking to establish a pool of Cleaners for permanent and fixed term, full-time and part-time vacancies which may arise during the 2026 school year and up to the end of Term 2, 2027. Appointments may be offered at any time for vacancies that commence during this period.

PLEASE NOTE: Applying for this pool does not mean you are applying for a current job vacancy. If you are successful, you will be placed in the pool and may be considered for employment if a suitable position becomes available in the future.

Australind Senior High School (SHS) is located north of Bunbury with easy access to the wider Southwest region of Western Australia. We are the largest Independent Public School in the region and one of the most successful, with a strong history of outstanding success for our students in both Australian Tertiary Admission Rank (ATAR) and Vocational Education and Training (VET) pathways.

Find out more about our school by visiting www.australind.wa.edu.au or Schools Online.

The Role

Australind SHS is seeking to appoint energetic and motivated individuals to fill upcoming Cleaner roles and join their friendly team.

Suitable applicants will ideally have good attention to detail and be able to work well both individually and as part of a team to ensure a clean and safe school environment. Additionally, they should be organised, reliable and punctual and with knowledge of cleaning equipment and safe cleaning procedures, methods and practices.

Cleaners at Australind SHS carry out both internal and external cleaning duties. Internal cleaning includes the maintenance of carpets and hard floor surfaces, cleaning of furniture and fittings, windows, toilets and dusting. External duties include rubbish removal, cleaning of drinking troughs, external windows, verandas and covered areas and cobweb removal. You will also participate in vacation cleaning which includes stripping and sealing of vinyl floors, carpet shampooing, pressure cleaning of undercover areas and verandas, and other such duties as directed by the Cleaner-In-Charge.

Want to know more?

Full details of the role, selection criteria and training requirements are listed in the Job Description Form (JDF).

For more information about this opportunity, please contact Jennifer Mezger, Cleaner in Charge on (08) 9797 4400 or emailing jennifer.mezger@education.wa.edu.au.

Equity and Diversity

We are committed to an inclusive and culturally responsive workforce reflecting the diversity in our schools and the Western Australian community. We welcome and encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders, young people, people of diverse sexualities and genders, people with disability, and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

Explore our Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Plan 2021-2025 for more details.

Eligibility

To work with us, you will need to:

  • obtain a valid Working With Children Check.
  • consent to a Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check and obtain a current Screening Clearance Number issued by the Department of Education’s Screening Unit before you start.
  • be an Australian or New Zealand citizen, permanent resident or have a valid visa with relevant work rights for the term of the appointment.

Additional eligibility and training requirements are outlined in the Job Description Form (JDF).

Application Instructions

Our aim is to make it easy for you to apply!

Step 1: Prepare your application.

Your application should include the following:

  • CV/Resume detailing your work history, experience and any certificates or qualifications relevant to the position.  

Step 2: Submit your application.

Apply Online:

  • Click ‘Apply for Job’ and complete the online application.
  • Have your documents ready to attach.

Apply Directly to the School:

  • Complete the application form located at the top of this advertisement.
  • Email your application form and documents to Jessica.inman@education.wa.edu.au, or
  • Hand-deliver your application form and documents to our school reception at 12 Break O’Day Drive, Australind WA 6233

It is recommended you have your attachments ready before selecting Apply for Job.

Your application must be received before the closing date and time. Late applications will not be accepted.

For technical support submitting your application, you can call the Department of Education’s Recruitment team on (08) 9264 4127 for assistance.

Advertised Vacancy Number: IPS/SS1043319

The Department applies a ten (10) day breach period to this selection process.

Applications close: 3.30pm (AWST) on Wednesday, 17 June 2026

content.jobHook: Hiring for SAP Senior SAP SD / VMS Support Lead
content.unEditedContent:
About the Company

We are HCLTech, one of the fastest-growing large tech companies in the world and home to 219,000+ people across 54 countries, supercharging progress through industry-leading capabilities centered around Digital, Engineering and Cloud.

Role Overview

Following a major digital transformation from SAP ECC to S/4HANA, we are seeking a seasoned Senior SAP SD / VMS Consultant to lead onsite support operations in Melbourne.

This role acts as the functional heartbeat of business operations, ensuring end‑to‑end lifecycle stability across procurement, logistics, sales, and after‑sales processes, while supporting the transition from Hypercare to a scalable BAU model.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead S/4HANA post‑go‑live stabilization, ensuring alignment with business requirements and performance benchmarks

  • Manage end‑to‑end Sales & Distribution (SD), Logistics Execution (LE), and Supply Chain (SCM) processes

  • Act as Vehicle Management System (VMS) Subject Matter Expert, covering procurement, stock, sales, and after‑sales operations

  • Troubleshoot complex enhancements across the SD / MM / VMS landscape

  • Ensure smooth integration between demand planning, MRP, procurement, and fulfillment processes

  • Lead Hypercare to BAU transition and manage competing stakeholder priorities


Technical Qualifications – Core Skills

  • 12–15 years of hands‑on experience in SAP SD / MM / VMS within complex S/4HANA environments

  • Strong exposure to Procurement and MRP in both ECC and S/4HANA

  • Deep expertise in Logistics Execution (LE) and Supply Chain operations

  • Experience working in highly customised SAP landscapes

  • Strong critical problem‑solving skills, including:

  • Root cause analysis

  • PRB reduction

  • Permanent issue resolution

  • Ability to identify recurring incidents and implement systemic fixes over workarounds

  • Strong cross‑functional troubleshooting across integration, data, access, and backend layers


Why HCL

  • We are one of the fastest-growing large tech companies in the world, with offices in 50+ countries across the globe and 219,000 employees.

  • Our company is extremely diverse with 165 nationalities represented.

  • We offer the opportunity to work with colleagues across the globe.

  • We offer a virtual-first work environment, promoting a good work-life integration and real flexibility.

  • We offer comprehensive benefits for all employees.

  • We are a certified great place to work and a top employer in 17 countries, offering a positive work environment that values employee recognition and respect.


How to apply:

To apply for this role, you should have a full work right to work in Australia. Press "Apply now" button to submit your resume


HCL's enlightened approach to employee development focus on giving people whatever they need to succeed: be it a virtual assistant or talent transformation sabbaticals; expert guidance or fast track growth; inner peace or democratic empowerment.

Quarterly menu changes offer great opportunity for creativity
Be part of an independent, local, hospitality group, with a competitive salary
content.jobHook: An exciting opportunity to join the team at the region's flagship cafe and continue on the legacy.
content.unEditedContent:
Chef - The General Food Store

One of the Dandenong Ranges' most dynamic hospitality groups, The Grub Club, is looking for a Chef for its flagship cafe, The General Food Store - to take the helm and stay at the forefront of the region's cafe scene.

The General Food Store is located in the picturesque township of Emerald in the Dandenong Ranges, 45 minutes from Melbourne. No driving into the city or paying for parking, surrounded by trees and nature; you couldn't ask for a better location. It's a forward-thinking cafe with the community at its heart, a place for brunch with friends or a must-visit tourist spot on weekends.

Opened in 2011, The General Food Store has led the way in a massive shift in Hill's cafe culture over the past 15 years, and we are seeking a Chef to join the team and continue on the legacy.

About the role

This role is an opportunity for an experienced, passionate, driven chef with a creative flair who loves seasonal cooking. If you thrive on the buzz of a cafe in full swing, days will fly by as you pump out brunch for our adoring customers. The ability to self-manage and self-critique is imperative.

We remain an industry leader in our region through our seasonal-driven menus, exceptional customer service, and passion for hospitality. Our bi-monthly menu takes inspiration from a range of cuisines. We present approachable yet unique brunch dishes and enjoy the creativity that seasonal changes bring.

Key points of interest

  • 4-day shifts a week, Wednesday to Saturday

  • Local cafe. No driving into the city!

  • Menu changes quarterly

  • Focus on local, seasonal produce

  • Dietary-friendly menu

  • Great working culture

  • Small kitchen team

  • Creativity encouraged

  • Great local produce

  • Fast-paced environment

  • Working closely with the owners

  • Work alongside a motivated FOH team

  • Respectful and cooperative team

  • Established, lovely, loyal customer base

  • Honest company that looks after its team

  • Staff discount at our venues

  • All-you-can-drink coffee!

  • Salary, plus super, and phone bills paid

We know this is a tough industry to find decent working conditions in. We pride ourselves on creating a workplace that goes against the traditional work-till-you-drop, low-paid, high staff turnover environments that so many of us have experienced in our careers. It can be different, and it is at The General Food Store. Just ask our team.

This position is a long-term engagement offering excellent work-life balance.

The Grub Club is a collective of food ventures by restauranteur couple, Paul Douglas and Belinda Smullen. They are The General Food Store (2011), Incy Wincy (2017), and The Grub Club meal delivery service (2025). They employ 25 people and pride themselves on their care for their team and their love of their community.

Please apply via Seek with an addressed cover letter to Paul Douglas.

content.unEditedContent:
TLH is looking for their next Heavy Vehicle Mechanic


Started in 2021, TLH has grown to 20 employees and 16 vehicles moving various building equipment & industrial steel around Melbourne local, Sydney local and interstate routes across Melbourne, Sydney & Brisbane. 

The company started with just one truck and minimal funding and has now progressed to be a competitive player in the flat tray transport sector. 

With great team cultures and flexible working environments, we have maintained a stable and strong team morale across the company and plan to grow year by year to be one of the biggest players in Australia.

content.jobHook: Drive high‑quality, data‑driven insights that shape operational and strategic decisions across the organisation.
content.unEditedContent:
Senior Data Analyst

  • Open to Sydney / Newcastle / Brisbane / Melbourne – Hybrid Working Model
  • Lead Pacific National’s enterprise Power BI transformation
  • Safely Every Day — That’s Our Promise

Pacific National is Australia’s largest private rail freight operator, moving millions of tonnes of essential freight across the country. We’re building an enterprise‑grade data capability — and we’re looking for a Senior Data Analyst who can elevate our reporting, modelling, and insights.

What You’ll Do

Drive high‑quality, data‑driven insights that shape operational and strategic decisions across the business.

Reporting to the Manager, Business Reporting & Analytics, you will:

  • Build best‑practice Power BI dashboards, reports, and semantic data models
  • Be a trusted analytics partner to the business, turning stakeholder needs into insights that drive decisions.
  • Conduct deep‑dive analytics, predictive modelling, and scenario analysis
  • Define KPIs/metrics and promote endorsed metric frameworks
  • Manage reporting and analytics work pipelines to ensure prioritised, on‑time delivery
  • Lift organisational data literacy through training, documentation, and self‑service enablement
  • Ensure data integrity, governance alignment, and analytics standards across the business

What You’ll Bring

  • 5+ years in data analytics / BI roles
  • Expert Power BI skills including advanced DAX and semantic modelling (certs desirable)
  • Strong SQL capability and experience with data warehousing
  • Experience designing scalable data models and applying statistical/predictive techniques
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high‑quality outputs
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • Experience delivering end‑user training and enabling self‑service BI
  • Exposure to Tableau, ITIL frameworks, or asset‑intensive industries is advantageous

Why join us?

At Pacific National we value the contribution of each team member. Our values underpin our commitment to create an inclusive culture where everyone is accepted.

Some of the benefits we offer are:

  • Paid parental leave
  • Novated Leasing
  • Fitness Passport
  • Purchase leave program
  • Access to EAP program through Sonder

We live by our Values: Make it Simple, Share More, Kindness, Gratitude, Curiosity, and Own It – helping us build strong connections and do our best work every day.

Ready to deliver what matters?

Click ‘Apply Now’ and start your journey with Pacific National. Learn more at https://www.pacificnational.com.au/careers

content.jobHook: Master Drilling Australia now seek safety focused Raise Bore Drillers, Trainee Drillers and Offsiders to join our busy Raisebore team - Roster 2:2
content.unEditedContent:
About Us 

Master Drilling Australia aspires to lead the world in innovative drilling technology offering advanced, fully automated services to the mining, infrastructure and energy sectors.  We are committed to safety, environmental sustainability and operational efficiency, and have positioned ourselves as a trusted partner of choice within the global drilling industry. 

About the Role 

Master Drilling Australia continue to dominate the industry, and we are now in seek of experienced and committed Raise Bore Drillers to join our onsite team inititally in Western Australia but with continuous tendering projects in the pipeline you may find yourself interstate or abroad.

Reporting into the Project Supervisor you will be committed to the safe operations of our raise bore fleet and equipment whilst committed to the high standards of respect and safety we have set for ourselves and each other. 

Please note: This role is offered on a 2 week on and 2 weeks off, day/night shift roster and for the preferred candidate we will consider mobilisation from any Australian capital city.  

Key Responsibilities 

  • Safe operations of MDG Raise Bore Rigs ensuring all safety and compliance requirements are consistently met  

  • Conduct daily rig, light Vehicle, Integrated Tool Carrier, Telehandler and Stores Truck pre-starts are closed out in line with company policies and procedures 

  • Ability to perform basic pre-start maintenance and checks 

  • Carry out essential maintenance tasks under direct supervision if and when appropriate 

  • Lead daily pre-shift meetings with the on-site crew 

  • Set up the site and prepare the Raise boring rig in accordance with MDA's standards and protocols. 

  • Locate collar and drill pilot hole following technical guidance, monitoring progress 

  • Assemble reamer underground and carry out reaming hook-up procedures 

  • Complete the reaming of the raise bore in line with all quality compliance documentation 

  • Assemble/disassemble the drill site efficiently and promptly  

  • Carry out operator prestart maintenance and condition monitoring inspections 

  • Maintain housekeeping of drill site to company standards 

  • Maintain stock control daily to ensure stock levels are consistently met  

  • Conduct mobilisation and demobilisation. 

 About You 

  • Current experience on Atlas Copco models 71R, 72R, 73R, and 91R Drill Rigs – Advantageous  

  • Current RIINHB312 (A to D suffix) – Conduct Raise Boring Ticket - Desirable 

  • Hold RIIHAN311F – Conduct Operations with Integrated Tool Carrier - Desirable

  • Current Work at Heights ticket - RIIWHS204 - Desirable

  • RIIHAN309F – Conduct Operations with Telehandler – Desirable

  • Valid C Class Manual Drivers’ Licence - Essential 

  • Heavy Rigid Licence (HR Licence) – Desirable

  • Rigging Ticket (RB) - Minimum - Essential

  • Crane Licence (CN) – Desirable

  • Current Senior First Aid Certificate (Willing to Obtain). 

  • Knowledge of and ability to implement safe working practices. 

  • Ability to communicate effectively with a diverse range of people.  

  • Basic Microsoft Office skills are desirable. 

  Additional Requirements 

  • Unrestricted rights to work in Australia 

  • Ability to successfully complete Pre-Employment Medical including drug and alcohol  

  • Must be able to provide a valid National Police Clearance (less than 6months old) 

Why Join Master Drilling Australia?

  • Competitive market rates – Above award 

  • Performance Based Quarterly Bonus  

  • Committed to the growth and development of our employees 

  • Provide ongoing training and career advancement opportunities 

  • Remuneration and superannuation during a portion of travel time 

  • Novated Leasing – Vehicles 

  • Great Onsite Camp Facilities – Food, Accommodation, and PPE Provided 

If you want to work for a global leader and enjoy working in a collaborative team orientated environment with a strong focus on safety and operational excellence, then please submit your resume highlighting your knowledge and experience. 

We look forward to hearing from you.

content.unEditedContent:
ECi Executive is currently partnering with several well-established WA civil contractors delivering major mining infrastructure, Main Roads, urban development and bulk earthworks projects across Western Australia.

We are currently seeking experienced FIFO & Perth Metro Civil Superintendents and Civil Supervisors.

These opportunities are suited to candidates looking to join reputable contractors with strong project pipelines, supportive site teams and long-term career prospects.

The Projects

Current opportunities include involvement across:
  • Bulk earthworks packages
  • Large-scale mining infrastructure projects
  • Haul roads and access roads
  • Streetscape, landscape & minor works 
Key Responsibilities
  • Supervise crews, plant operators and subcontractors onsite
  • Coordinate daily site activities across active work fronts
  • Drive production outcomes while maintaining a strong safety culture
  • Lead pre-starts, toolbox talks and daily reporting
  • Ensure works are completed safely, efficiently and to programme
  • Liaise with engineers, client representatives and site teams
  • Monitor quality, compliance and project deliverables
About You 
  • Previous experience as a Civil Supervisor or Civil Superintendent within Australia
  • Strong background in urban civil/utilities, mining civils, bulk earthworks or road construction
  • Experience managing crews and coordinating subcontractors onsite
  • Sound knowledge of QA, safety and compliance requirements
  • S26 Statutory Supervisor qualification (essential for FIFO roles)
  • FIFO project experience within WA mining environments
  • Strong communication and leadership skills
What’s On Offer
  • FIFO roles - 2:1/10:4 rosters from Perth
  • Perth based roles - Monday-Friday 9-hour shifts 
  • Competitive salary packages based on experience
  • Long-term projects with established WA civil contractors
  • Strong project pipelines and ongoing work
  • Supportive site teams and positive working environments
  • Genuine career progression opportunities
Apply now for a confidential conversation about which opportunity suits you best.

Your enquiry will be handled with complete discretion.

Recruitment Consultant - Civil & Infrastructure

content.jobHook: An opportunity to provide leadership & management of the nursing staff &services & set strategic direction within the Dept of Medicine-Sub Acute, LGH
content.unEditedContent:
The Role:

  • Provide effective leadership and management of the nursing staff and services and set strategic direction within the Department of Medicine - Sub Acute and Ambulatory Care Service Division of the Launceston General Hospital (LGH) in consultation with the Clinical Director - Department of Medicine.
  • The role manages an interesting and diverse range of specialist services including Rehabilitation Wards, Renal Units North and Northwest, Specialist Clinics, Diabetes Centre, Hospital Aged Care Liaison Team (HALT) and Transitional Care Program (TCP), Refugee Health, Respiratory North and Northwest, Neurology, and Diabetes and Renal Research.
  • The role reports to the Executive Director of Operations and Performance and receives professional support from the Executive Director of Nursing and Midwifery. 

You will:

  • In conjunction with the Executive Director Operations & Performance lead the delivery of clinical governance systems to achieve and promote the highest standards of service delivery, quality improvement and risk management strategies.
  • Direct the operational activities of designated clinical services consistent with Agency objectives and provide effective leadership, coordination and direction for the management of the human, financial and material resources to achieve these objectives.
  • Assist in the development and application of clinical management policies, protocols and guidelines that will enable the evaluation of services against best practice standards.
  • Provide leadership and direction in the areas of research/education, continuous quality improvement and innovative redesign.
  • Manage clinical and corporate risk within the established framework while ensuring a safe environment for patients and staff.
  • Support Nurse Unit Managers to facilitate a range of initiatives to enhance the quality of patient care in all areas of responsibility by providing a learning environment through mentoring, team development, individual capability development and managing performance.

Why Tasmania:

The Department of Health Tasmania oversees various hospitals across the state, including the Royal Hobart Hospital, Launceston General Hospital, Northwest Regional Hospital, and Mersey Community Hospital, as well as district hospitals and ambulance services. Additionally, it provides community health, mental health, and primary healthcare services to the Tasmanian community through more than 300 sites.

Tasmania, Australia's only island state, offers unparalleled natural beauty and a luxurious lifestyle. Pursuing your health career in Tasmania’s public health system means building strong connections with colleagues and patients. It also means embracing a lifestyle where you can enjoy extraordinary experiences outside of work while making a significant impact on the community during work.

Details of appointment:

Permanent, full time, day worker (with on-call) position, working 76 hours per fortnight, commencing from 10 June 2026. *notwithstanding hours to be negotiated with the successful applicant.

Applicants should note that, for a period of twelve months from the date of publication, this selection process may be used to fill subsequent or similar full time, part time, and casual vacancies.

Salary: $148,470 per annum. Our Employer 12% superannuation contribution is on top of this amount.

  • Salary range is in accordance with Nurses and Midwives (Tasmania State Service) Agreement 2023.

In addition, the following allowances calculated on the salaried incremental point may be available: 

  • Post Graduate Allowance of up to 10% based on qualification type 

Salary Packaging:

You’ll have access to salary package a range of benefits including living expenses up to $9,010 + $2,650 in meal entertainment each FBT year + other benefits if eligible. 

Benefits available to eligible candidates:

  • Travel and relocation assistance support available up to $15,000 for eligible appointees from overseas, and up to $10,000 for appointees from interstate. 
  • Professional development and accelerated pathways.
  • A range of leave entitlements, including study leave and Professional Development Support.
  • Fitness Passport – You, and your family can access 40+ fitness facilities across Tasmania for just $13.95 per week per person, or $25.95 for a family.

More information about our Employee Benefits can be found here

Eligibility:

Successful applicants will be required to meet the essential criteria.

  • Registered with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia as a Registered Nurse

Applicants should note the following criteria are desirable:

  • Relevant Post Graduate Qualifications

Note: - Please refer to the Application Guide for more information of pre-employment check.

Download the Statement of Duties and any Associated Documents

We encourage you to review the Statement of Duties, Applicant Guide, prior to applying for an overview of the duties, program, selection process and application guidance.

content.jobHook: Rewarding allied health role supporting injury management in Alice Springs
content.unEditedContent:
Introduction

At Gallagher Bassett, we're there when it matters most because helping people through challenging moments is more than just our job, it’s our purpose. Every day, we help clients navigate complexity, support recovery, and deliver outcomes that make a real difference in people’s lives. It takes empathy, precision, and a strong sense of partnership—and that’s exactly what you’ll find here. We’re a team of fast-paced fixers, empathetic experts, and outcomes drivers — people who care deeply about doing the right thing and doing it well. Whether you're managing claims, supporting clients, or improving processes, you’ll play a vital role in helping businesses and individuals move forward with confidence. Here, you’ll be supported by a culture that values teamwork, encourages curiosity, and celebrates the impact of your work. Because when you’re here, you’re part of something bigger. You’re part of a team that shows up, stands together, and leads with purpose.


Overview

Gallagher Bassett (GB) is Australia and New Zealand’s premier third party claims administrator. We manage claims on behalf of insurers, brokers, government bodies and self-insured organisations. We are part of the leading global risk management and insurance group Arthur J Gallagher & Co.

Life at GB is an adventure - often fast paced, unpredictable, challenging and deeply rewarding. It is social and engaging, with our unique and positive culture underpinned by The Gallagher Way – values lived daily by our people.

In addition to flexible working options, we also offer supportive learning and career pathways and provide ongoing access to training and career development. We invest in our people through strong succession planning and have a number of mentoring and training programs available.

There are some great things happening at GB as we continue through a period of exciting period of transformation and change, including the introduction of dedicated specialist hubs within our claims functions that are truly unique to the market and our service offerings to injured workers and clients alike. And, we want YOU to be a part of it all!

We are excited to announce a new Injury Management Specialist opportunity, based in Alice Springs, offering you the work-life balance you earn! Reporting to the Team Manager, you will join a collaborative team, providing  advice, quality assurance and coaching to our Claims personnel, and contributing to our best practice injury management support.

This is a unique opportunity to bring your allied health qualifications and personal injury claims experience to a truly rewarding role.


How you'll make an impact
  • Support claims teams across injury management activities, including treatment and recovery strategies, injury management planning, treatment provider liaison, etc;
  • Provide coaching to Claims teams around best-practice injury management, feedback and training;
  • Collaborate with Claims teams and broader specialist functions, including Return to Work, Mental Health and Technical Support;
  • Participate in a range of operational projects and business initiatives.

About you
  • Previous experience as an Injury Management Specialist within an insurer setting, including workers compensation, CTP, etc;
  • Tertiary qualifications in allied health, such as exercise physiology, physiotherapy, nursing, etc;
  • Strong coaching ability, with an approachable attitude;
  • Exceptional time management and organisational skills;
  • Highly developed communication skills, with the ability to engage at all levels of organisation;
  • A strategic mindset and approach to work;
  • A strong sense of team and collaboration;
  • A resilient attitude.

Gallagher Bassett is an Equal Opportunity Employer and Indigenous Australian applicants are encouraged to apply. As a member of the Diversity Council Australia, we recognise the importance of, and embrace diversity in the workplace. We will make reasonable accommodations to known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified applicant with a disability, unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on the operation of our business.


Compensation and benefits

On top of a competitive salary, great teams and exciting career opportunities, we also offer a wide range of benefits. 

Below are the minimum core benefits you’ll get, depending on your job level these benefits may improve:

  • 4 weeks annual leave plus up to 2 weeks additional purchased Lifestyle Leave
  • Novated Leasing opportunities
  • Two paid volunteer days annually
  • Health Insurance Discounts with our Group Insurance Plan
  • Employee Stock Purchase Program
  • Paid parental leave

Other benefits include:

  • Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
  • Mental Health and Wellbeing Support for yourself and immediate family members
  • Employee Recognition Awards and Service Milestone Recognitions
  • Peer Support Program
  • Annual flu vaccinations
  • Access to Reward Gateway – discount offers at over 350 retailers!
  • And more...

We value inclusion and diversity

Inclusion and diversity (I&D) is a core part of our business, and it’s embedded into the fabric of our organization. For more than 95 years, Gallagher has led with a commitment to sustainability and to support the communities where we live and work.

Gallagher embraces our employees’ diverse identities, experiences and talents, allowing us to better serve our clients and communities. We see inclusion as a conscious commitment and diversity as a vital strength. By embracing diversity in all its forms, we live out The Gallagher Way to its fullest.

Gallagher believes that all persons are entitled to equal employment opportunity and prohibits any form of discrimination by its managers, employees, vendors or customers based on race, color, religion, creed, gender (including pregnancy status), sexual orientation, gender identity (which includes transgender and other gender non-conforming individuals), gender expression, hair expression, marital status, parental status, age, national origin, ancestry, disability, medical condition, genetic information, veteran or military status, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected (herein referred to as “protected characteristics”) by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

Equal employment opportunity will be extended in all aspects of the employer-employee relationship, including, but not limited to, recruitment, hiring, training, promotion, transfer, demotion, compensation, benefits, layoff, and termination. sections: Introduction

At Gallagher Bassett, we're there when it matters most because helping people through challenging moments is more than just our job, it’s our purpose. Every day, we help clients navigate complexity, support recovery, and deliver outcomes that make a real difference in people’s lives. It takes empathy, precision, and a strong sense of partnership—and that’s exactly what you’ll find here. We’re a team of fast-paced fixers, empathetic experts, and outcomes drivers — people who care deeply about doing the right thing and doing it well. Whether you're managing claims, supporting clients, or improving processes, you’ll play a vital role in helping businesses and individuals move forward with confidence. Here, you’ll be supported by a culture that values teamwork, encourages curiosity, and celebrates the impact of your work. Because when you’re here, you’re part of something bigger. You’re part of a team that shows up, stands together, and leads with purpose.
Overview

Gallagher Bassett (GB) is Australia and New Zealand’s premier third party claims administrator. We manage claims on behalf of insurers, brokers, government bodies and self-insured organisations. We are part of the leading global risk management and insurance group Arthur J Gallagher & Co.

Life at GB is an adventure - often fast paced, unpredictable, challenging and deeply rewarding. It is social and engaging, with our unique and positive culture underpinned by The Gallagher Way – values lived daily by our people.

In addition to flexible working options, we also offer supportive learning and career pathways and provide ongoing access to training and career development. We invest in our people through strong succession planning and have a number of mentoring and training programs available.

There are some great things happening at GB as we continue through a period of exciting period of transformation and change, including the introduction of dedicated specialist hubs within our claims functions that are truly unique to the market and our service offerings to injured workers and clients alike. And, we want YOU to be a part of it all!

We are excited to announce a new Injury Management Specialist opportunity, based in Alice Springs, offering you the work-life balance you earn! Reporting to the Team Manager, you will join a collaborative team, providing  advice, quality assurance and coaching to our Claims personnel, and contributing to our best practice injury management support.
This is a unique opportunity to bring your allied health qualifications and personal injury claims experience to a truly rewarding role.
How you'll make an impact
Support claims teams across injury management activities, including treatment and recovery strategies, injury management planning, treatment provider liaison, etc;
Provide coaching to Claims teams around best-practice injury management, feedback and training;
Collaborate with Claims teams and broader specialist functions, including Return to Work, Mental Health and Technical Support;
Participate in a range of operational projects and business initiatives.
About you
Previous experience as an Injury Management Specialist within an insurer setting, including workers compensation, CTP, etc;
Tertiary qualifications in allied health, such as exercise physiology, physiotherapy, nursing, etc;
Strong coaching ability, with an approachable attitude;
Exceptional time management and organisational skills;
Highly developed communication skills, with the ability to engage at all levels of organisation;
A strategic mindset and approach to work;
A strong sense of team and collaboration;
A resilient attitude.

Gallagher Bassett is an Equal Opportunity Employer and Indigenous Australian applicants are encouraged to apply. As a member of the Diversity Council Australia, we recognise the importance of, and embrace diversity in the workplace. We will make reasonable accommodations to known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified applicant with a disability, unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on the operation of our business.
Compensation and benefits
On top of a competitive salary, great teams and exciting career opportunities, we also offer a wide range of benefits.
Below are the minimum core benefits you’ll get, depending on your job level these benefits may improve:
4 weeks annual leave plus up to 2 weeks additional purchased Lifestyle Leave
Novated Leasing opportunities
Two paid volunteer days annually
Health Insurance Discounts with our Group Insurance Plan
Employee Stock Purchase Program
Paid parental leave
Other benefits include:
Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
Mental Health and Wellbeing Support for yourself and immediate family members
Employee Recognition Awards and Service Milestone Recognitions
Peer Support Program
Annual flu vaccinations
Access to Reward Gateway – discount offers at over 350 retailers!
And more...
We value inclusion and diversity

Inclusion and diversity (I&D) is a core part of our business, and it’s embedded into the fabric of our organization. For more than 95 years, Gallagher has led with a commitment to sustainability and to support the communities where we live and work.

Gallagher embraces our employees’ diverse identities, experiences and talents, allowing us to better serve our clients and communities. We see inclusion as a conscious commitment and diversity as a vital strength. By embracing diversity in all its forms, we live out The Gallagher Way to its fullest.

json.title: Crane Technician (Electrical, Field Service, Overhead Cranes)

bulletPoints: Sydney Metro work with a large client base. Great team culture.
Strong support team behind you, but trusted to run your own day.
Realistic $200,000+ annual package for someone who wants the hours.
content.jobHook: Get paid as soon as you leave home, new ute, monthly RDO, and serious overtime. Crane tech role across Sydney Metro with $200k+ earning potential.
content.unEditedContent:
Company & Job:

A specialist crane business is looking to expand their team with an additional Crane Technician (5 years experience) to work across industrial sites throughout Sydney.

Inspection, servicing, fault finding, breakdown response, and repair of overhead gantry cranes and hoists.

You can be based anywhere in Sydney and come with a strong package including up to a $135base, $60 to $70 per hour base rate, brand new ute, and over time, a package of $200,000 + annually. 


What you’ll be doing:
  • Service, repair, and fault-find overhead cranes, hoists, and winches across the Sydney Metro.
  • Install, wire, test, and commission crane systems and controls.
  • Get called out to breakdowns on live industrial, manufacturing, and production sites.
  • Fault-find motors, VSDs/VFDs, PLCs, limit switches, contactors, relays, brakes, drives, switchboards, and control circuits.
  • Read electrical and control drawings without needing your hand held.
  • Carry out planned maintenance, inspections, and repairs safely and properly.
  • Work to Australian Standards and WHS requirements — no cowboy stuff.
  • Manage your own day on the road, with support from the service team when needed.
  • Talk to clients on site, explain what’s going on, and help sort the problem.
  • Help apprentices or other techs when required.
  • Knock over basic service reports and job notes after each job.

About You:
  • Dual Trade background as an Industrial Electrician or Fitter.
  • You must have overhead gantry crane experience and must hold an Industrial Electrician licence.


If you would like to discuss the role further, please feel free to send your CV via this link, and we'll be in touch. For other opportunities, check out www.nextdayrecruitment.com.au     


NDR, Your People For Tomorrow. Right First Time.

content.jobHook:
Experienced Carpenter/ or Builder – Architectural Residential Construction
Huskisson, NSW
Casual / Subcontract / Or Full-Time Available
content.unEditedContent:
Experienced Carpenter/ or Builder – Architectural Residential Construction
Huskisson, NSW
Casual / Subcontract / Or Full-Time Available

We are seeking a highly experienced carpenter to join our team on high-end architectural residential projects on the South Coast of NSW.

This role is suited to an experienced carpenter or a builder with a strong understanding of residential construction across all stages of a build. We are looking for someone confident interpreting plans, working proactively onsite, problem solving efficiently, and delivering high-quality workmanship with minimal supervision.

This Position Would Suit:

  • An experienced subcontract carpenter looking for consistent subcontract work

  • A qualified builder looking for hands-on carpentry work and is capable of assisting in a leading hand / supervisor role

  • A experienced carpenter/ or builder who is looking for stable full-time employment

About the Role

You will be involved in all stages of construction on architecturally designed homes, including for example:

  • Set-out and framing

  • Complex roof carpentry

  • Structural carpentry

  • External cladding and detailing

  • Fix out and finish carpentry

  • Formwork

  • General onsite coordination and problem solving

  • Working alongside other trades

Essential Requirements

  • Extensive residential carpentry and building experience

  • Strong ability to read and interpret architectural and structural plans

  • Thorough understanding of how to build a new home from start to finish

  • Ability to work unsupervised and maintain high-quality workmanship

  • Strong attention to detail and pride in your work

  • Reliable, punctual, and professional attitude

  • White Card required

  • Own tools and transport

What We Offer

  • Immediate start available

  • Excellent rates for the right person

  • Consistent ongoing work

  • Longer hours available 7am-530pm

  • Weekend work available if desired

  • Exciting high-quality architectural projects

  • Professional and well-organised work environment

  • Long-term opportunities available for the right person

This is not a labouring position or a role suited to inexperienced carpenters. We are specifically looking for someone with genuine hands-on knowledge and experience in architectural residential construction, and add value and productivity onsite.

Project based in Huskisson, NSW.

Please apply with your experience, previous projects, availability, and contact details.

json.title: Structural Design Engineer

content.jobHook: Are you bored with designing the same thing each day. Try something new where you are exposed to new design challenges daily. Join us.
content.unEditedContent:
Do you like to be involved in design of new things with a wide style of projects and opportunities? Are you able to apply your skills and knowledge to adapt for new challenges? Can you work on small and large projects at the same time? This is the type of candidate we are looking for.

Teleo Design is a multi-disciplined Engineering Design and Project Management company. We are looking for a Structural/Civil Design Engineer to support our current and projected workload. The works include multistorey steel and composite construction structures, bridges and boardwalks, Infrastructure and transport structures along with civil foundation piling and footings design and retaining wall structures. New opportunities are also opening in WHS access structures and façade systems.

Our projects cover NSW, Queensland and Victoria with some projects extending around the world. Registration in these states will be a requirement for ongoing employment.

For this role we require:

  • Minimum 5 to 10 years civil and structural design with steel and concrete structures

  • Solid understanding of structural modelling in SpaceGass and SkyCiv.

  • Exposure to Steel/ Composite and concrete design as well as some Post tension work

  • Well developed understanding of Australian Standards. Exposure to international standards is a bonus.

  • Good understanding of the NCC for a wide range of building classes

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

  • Ability to solve problems, deliver projects on time and within budget

  • Demonstrated ability to prioritise work

  • Ability to work flexibly and demonstrate initiative

  • Rights to live and work in Australia a must

  • Strong skills in Microsoft office applications

  • Registration as a Chartered Engineer preferred, eligibility to register a must

This role provides an exciting and challenging opportunity for the right person to work in a high growth industry and develop new skills and processes in the engineering supply chain.
