json.title: Field Officer Grade 1-2 (Aboriginal Identified & Aboriginal Targeted - 2 roles)

content.jobHook: Field Officer Grade 1-2 (Two roles - Aboriginal Identified and Aboriginal Targeted)
content.unEditedContent:
• Field Officer Grade 1-2 – Two roles available, Aboriginal Identified and Aboriginal Targeted
  • Ongoing full-time opportunities based in Mundamia (Nowra West)
  • Salary relative to experience, and ranges from $58,863 to $64,620 + employer's contribution to superannuation 

 

Do you want to help support Aboriginal communities to achieve their aspirations and
work to protect the state’s environment and Aboriginal heritage?

 

About the role
National Parks and Wildlife Service has a unique opportunity for two Field Officer’s Grade 1-2 to join the South Coast team and contribute to the conservation of the natural environment, flora, fauna and Aboriginal cultural heritage. 

Field Officers assist with a diverse range of activities relating to maintenance and improvement to park assets within NPWS parks and reserves.  You will be guided by the senior field staff, in your day-to-day work including pest and weed control, routine maintenance, construction and installation of new assets and conservation works. You will operate and maintain plant and equipment, participate in fire management activities, respond to visitor enquiries and assist with compliance activities as required.

You will work as part of a team, operating vehicles, tools and equipment, helping keep parks safe and welcoming for visitors, and contributing to fire and emergency response activities with appropriate training. This role suits people who enjoy physical work, being outdoors, and learning new skills while making a practical contribution to protecting our natural and cultural heritage.

Two roles are available, the first is Aboriginal Identified and the second is Aboriginal Targeted.  A Recruitment Pool may be created for future South Coast Branch job opportunities.

NPWS is transitioning to a Field Officer Grade 1–4 classification. Successful candidates for this role will transition to the updated model as it is implemented, with progression based on satisfactory performance, demonstrated achievement of the mandatory competencies for each grade, and time in the role.

 

About You
Your fitness, enthusiasm and ability to work in small teams is crucial for you to succeed in this diverse and dynamic role.  You need to have the ability to think on your feet and enjoy working outdoors in a dynamic team.

You need to be someone who:

  • Enjoys hands‑on, physical work in outdoor environments
  • Is reliable, safety‑focused and motivated to learn new skills
  • Works well as part of a team and follows direction
  • Has a positive attitude and takes pride in a job well done
  • Is committed to protecting the natural environment and cultural heritage
  • Is comfortable interacting with park visitors and supporting a safe visitor experience


Essential requirements 

  • Current Australian Class C Drivers licence or equivalent, and ability to drive 4wd vehicles.
  • Ability to obtain and use MR License where appropriate
  • Demonstrated ability and experience to carry out all duties safely and ability to obtain relevant SafeWork NSW certification to appropriately operate and maintain a range of plant and equipment, including but not limited to conditionally registered vehicles, , lifting apparatus and minor road maintenance plant as well as the ability and willingness to obtain a First Aid certificate.
  • Certification, or ability to obtain certification within the probationary period (up to 12 months), in operating a chainsaw to crosscut or basic tree felling standard; ability to operate two-way radio.
  • Ability to carry out frontline firefighting duties and support roles including, ability to obtain and maintain certification as crew member within the probationary period (up to 12 months), and a willingness to fly in light aircraft.


This is a physically active role suited to candidates of all genders who are fit, enjoy working outdoors as part of a team, and are eager to learn and develop the skills and qualifications needed to contribute toward improving and maintaining NSW’s most precious natural places.

Field Officer applicants must meet the requirements of a firefighting medical which is inclusive of a clearance to undertake frontline firefighting roles. The applicant must pass the task-based fitness assessment to a moderate level within the probationary period (up to 12 months) and annually thereafter.

For more information read the Role Descriptions: Field Officer Grade 1-2 (Aboriginal Identified) and Field Officer Grade 1-2


Aboriginal Identified Role
Positions are specifically noted under the provisions of the NSW Anti-discrimination Act (1977).

  • This is an Identified role under Section 14d of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1977 and as such Aboriginality is an essential requirement of the role.
  • Aboriginal identified positions are developed where Aboriginal identity, cultural knowledge or connections are a genuine aspect of the role. Positions are specifically noted under the provisions of the NSW Anti-discrimination Act (1977) for Aboriginal people who meet the following criteria:
    • is of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent, and
    • identifies as an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander person, and
    • is accepted as such by the Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander community.


Aboriginal Targeted Role
Positions are Aboriginal Targeted under GSE Rule 26 and Aboriginal people are encouraged to apply. 
Role is open to all candidates that meet NSW Public Sector employment eligibility.

 

Who we are
The Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) works to protect the state’s environment and heritage. It leads the way on climate change, driving the sustainable transition to a net zero economy, powered by affordable, reliable, and clean energy.

DCCEEW conserves and protects the state’s natural environment. It manages the NSW national park estate, including its rich and diverse biodiversity and Aboriginal cultural heritage for future generations.

DCCEEW also ensures sustainable management of water resources across the state, to support the environment, communities and industry.

We acknowledge the ongoing custodial responsibilities of the Aboriginal peoples of NSW to care for Country and water and are committed to establishing meaningful partnerships with Aboriginal peoples in the management of the environment.


What we can offer you
NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service is a great place to expand your career and grow your skills and knowledge.

  • Accrued days off in addition to Annual Leave
  • Corporate wellbeing programs, including the Fitness Passport
  • Learning and development opportunities, including in-house training.


What we do 
About NSW National Parks & Wildlife Service 
Visit a park 
South Coast Branch Overview

To Apply
Submit your application, including a copy of your resume (maximum 4 pages) and one page cover letter expressing your interest and suitability for the role.  

To be eligible for an ongoing role in the NSW Public Sector you need to be an Australian Citizen, New Zealand Citizen or Permanent Resident. For temporary and casual roles, you need to hold a valid visa giving you permission to work in Australia as required by the role.


Applications close: Tuesday 9 June 2026 at 11:55pm 

For further information about the role please contact Kim Waterhouse, Senior Field Supervisor via kim.waterhouse@dcceew.nsw.gov.au or on 0427 405 640.

A recruitment pool may be created for ongoing and temporary opportunities of the same role or role type that may become available over the next 18 months. 


Our goal is to build a workforce that not only represents but also understands and serves the diverse communities of New South Wales. We are committed to making our state a vibrant and inclusive place to live, work, and thrive for everyone. Our workforce represents people of all ages and genders, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people with disabilities, the LGBTQI+ community, and people from diverse ethnic and cultural backgrounds. 

 

Looking for more information or assistance in applying? 

  • Our commitment to a diverse and inclusive workplace. 
  • How we encourage and support people with disability  
  • Information and adjustments for individual needs for the recruitment process and the workplace. 


If you require an adjustment for your application process, please contact our Talent Acquisition Team by emailing dcceew.ta@dpie.npws.gov.au or contacting Kylie Miller on 0459 877 821 (please mention reference number 550391 or 550393).  

If you are an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander use our Aboriginal applicants guide to assist with applying for roles or our Aboriginal Career pathways team at AEX@dcceew.nsw.gov.au for a yarn. 


Find us on Facebook, Instagram, X (Twitter), YouTube and LinkedIn.

content.jobHook: Tell us what flexibility means to you! We welcome diverse backgrounds to enable our residents to get the best clinical care.
content.unEditedContent:
We are seeking experienced casual Registered Nurses available for morning, afternoon and night duty shifts to join our dedicated team at our Care Home in Knoxfield VIC.

Casual pool employees are considered for permanent shifts as they become available.

If you are a compassionate, flexible, and reliable Registered Nurse with a minimum of 12 months experience in aged care looking to make a difference, we would love to hear from you.

Shortlisted candidates will be required to complete a video assessment as part of the application process.

The Role

At Infinite Aged Care, the role of a Registered Nurse is highly visible and plays a vital role in meeting our residents’ daily needs and delivering high quality, person centric care to residents and families.

Our nurses are responsible for the total care of the resident, including physical, emotional wellbeing and safety. They are given the autonomy and space they need to make decisions and enjoy the support of the personal care, lifestyle, and Hospitality teams.

In addition to this, they act as role models by adhering to safe practice measures in medication management, providing leadership to others and by doing so promote a harmonious team environment aligned with our values. The attached position description outlines duties and accountabilities for this role.

 About You

You have the ability to “think on your feet” as well as the ability to communicate effectively, build rapport and maintain professional relationships with residents and co-workers alike.

We hire on attitude and aptitude, so you do not need experience in the aged care sector. You do however need to be aligned with our philosophy and values, have strong communication skills, and a commitment to resident wellbeing as well as

  • Minimum of 12 months experience as a Registered Nurse in an aged care setting
  • Being a "caring centric" person is your superpower!
  • There is a higher purpose for coming to work and enabling our residents to live life to the fullest.
  • You thrive in variety and diversity in clinical care settings and commit to following compliant practices for the elderly.
  • A Bachelor of Nursing degree
  • AHPRA Registration with no restriction
  • Being a positive team colleague, shows initiative and delivers quality work is your daily world!
  • A valid NDIS Workers Screening Clearance (or have the ability to get one)
  • Enjoys working with other nursing, personal care workers, lifestyle and hotel services to create the "Best place to work" for everyone's happiness and safety.

Who are we?

We are a rapidly growing leader in residential aged care with facilities in Queensland, NSW, and South Australia. We take pride in our ability to provide an environment which encourages and enables residents to remain independent.

We offer our employees the opportunity to broaden their skills and achieve their potential whilst at the same time create a home away from home for our residents and their loved ones.

Employee Benefits - Why work for us?

  • FREE mandatory & self-paced training modules throughout your employment.
  • Earn extra income via Carefriends employee referral program (*unlimited referrals)
  • Earn extra income via weekly shift bidding for extra shifts in your week.
  • Discounted retail, fuel and technology items via Employee discounts provider – Flare.
  • Fitness Passport to access discounted exercise, wellness and sporting facilities e.g aquatic centres
  • FREE Employee Assistance Program for family, financial and wellbeing support services.
  • Ability to cross-skill into hospitality and resident engagement teams.
  • Ability to span your career across our 17 homes nationally.
  • Dedicated and structured workplace induction plan with an assigned buddy for your initial shifts.
  • Companywide safety-first workplaces for our residents, families and staff.

Infinite Care accepts the Ausmed Passport, which is a free, digital certificate for the Australian aged care workforce that recognises their completion of eight, sector-wide, core mandatory training topics.

Our care roles are busy! Alot of bending, lifting, pushing and squatting to perform your duties safely. All candidates will be required to complete an online medical assessment to maintain personal and workplace safety standards.

content.jobHook: The Tasmanian Health Service is seeking interest from suitable applicants for Registrar and Fellow vacancies in Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine
content.unEditedContent:
The Tasmanian Health Service is seeking interest from suitable applicants for Registrar and Fellow vacancies in Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine at the Royal Hobart Hospital (RHH).

The RHH Department of Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine (DDHM) is fully accredited for ANZCA Advanced Certificate of Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine training, subject to the applicant meeting ANZCA requirements. The positions are also accredited by the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine, Royal Australian College of General Practitioners, and the Australian College for Rural and Remote Medicine for advanced training as a Special Skills Category A term, and are approved by the South Pacific Underwater Medicine Society for the SPUMS Diploma of Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine.

  • All applicants must be fit to dive as per AS/NZS 2299.1 or AS/NZS 4774.2.
  • The SPUMS Diploma is suitable for registrars at any level of training.
  • The ANZCA Advanced Certificate program requires candidates to be in their Fellowship year or Post-Fellowship.

Applications can be accepted from Anaesthesia, Emergency Medicine, Intensive Care Medicine, General Practice, Rural & Remote Medicine, or other training programs.

The DDHM is the State referral centre for diving emergencies and is the only medical recompression facility in Tasmania.  The facility recently entered an exciting new phase, moving into a world class dual-function, triple-lock, multiplace Hyperbaric/Hypobaric chamber complex in the new RHH redevelopment – which is the only one of its kind in the Southern Hemisphere.

Tasmania has a population of approximately 25,000 active divers of which 2,000 are professional divers.  The hyperbaric facility conducts over 2,000 patient treatments annually and manages approximately 20-30 cases of decompression illness and 60-80 acute non-decompression emergencies.  The RHH hyperbaric facility has full critical care capability.  

Hyperbaric medical, nursing and technical staff are involved in a number of international collaborative research projects and multi-centre randomised trials and will provide support to successful applicants in undertaking research projects.  Protected time is provided for teaching and attendance at specialty training programs in addition to support to attend the short courses in Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine held each year at either the Fiona Stanley Hospital in Perth or HMAS Penguin in Sydney.

Specialists at the DDHM have close links with Tasmanian professional diving industries. There are opportunities for field visits to professional and offshore diving operations whilst working at the facility.

Salary

$134,930 to $189,005 per annum

Salary range is in accordance with the Medical Practitioners Agreement 2022

Classification

Medical Practitioner Level 5-11 (Registrar/Senior Registrar)

Award

Medical Practitioners (Tasmanian State Service) Award

Period of Employment

Fixed term, full-time day work (with on-call), working 76 hours per fortnight (+10 hours protected training time per fortnight, pro rata) commencing 1 February 2027 until 7 February 2028.

NOTE:

Six- or twelve-month appointments may be considered. For 6-month appointments (suitable for the SPUMS DipDHM), a matching 6-month term is required in the applicant’s primary specialty training program, for example Anaesthesia, Emergency Medicine, Intensive Care Medicine. A separate application should also be made to the applicant’s primary speciality training program to facilitate integration of the two six-month positions.

The 12-month appointments (suitable for the ANZCA AdvCertDHM) can be made on a stand-alone basis.

Applicants should note that, for a period of twelve months from the date of publication, this selection process may be used to fill subsequent or similar full time, part time and casual vacancies.

Location

 

 

Department of Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine, Ward K3 East
Royal Hobart Hospital

Make It Tasmania | Move for a great lifestyle

Tasmanian | The quiet pursuit of the extraordinary

Duties

Under the direction and supervision of the Medical Director, Supervisor of Training, and DDHM specialist medical staff, the successful applicants will -

  • Be responsible for the day-to-day management of public and private Diving and Hyperbaric inpatients and outpatients within the Hospital.
  • Provide after-hours emergency cover at the hospital in accordance with the DDHM roster (supported by on-call specialists).
  • Undertake the research requirements associated with the SPUMS DipDHM.
  • Undertake the training requirements of the ANZCA Advanced Certificate of Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine (12-month appointments only).

Essential Requirements

  • General or limited registration with the Medical Board of Australia
  • Current Tasmanian Working with Children Registration (where applicable and as determined by individual position requirements).

The Head of the State Service has determined that the person nominated for this job is to satisfy a pre‑employment check before taking up the appointment, on promotion or transfer.  The following checks are to be conducted:
1.  Conviction checks in the following areas:
a)  Crimes of Violence
b)  Sex Related Offences
c)  Serious Drug Offences
d)  Crimes involving dishonesty
2.  Identification check
3.  Disciplinary action in previous employment check

Download the Statement of Duties and Associated Documents

  •  Generic Registrar-Senior Registrar MP5-11 (June 2024) CSU.pdf
  •  Generic Registrar-Senior Registrar MP5-11 (June 2024) CSU.docx
  •  0. Department of Health - Applicant Guide Sep 2024.pdf
  •  0. Department of Health - Applicant Guide Sep 2024.docx

How do I submit my application?

Please submit an online application.  Please click the blue "Apply now" button.

You are NOT required to address the selection criteria within the Statement of Duties.

Please ensure your application includes:

  • A current CV
  • A cover letter/statement outlining your career goals and suitability for the position.
  • Copy of your Qualifications

 

Attachments must be in Microsoft Word or PDF format.
Please note, hard copy applications will not be considered for this recruitment campaign.

NOTE:  Applications submitted by an Agent on behalf of an applicant will not be considered for this recruitment.

For further information regarding these positions please contact –

Dr Lizzie Elliott
Acting Head of Department - Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine
Phone: (03) 6166 8322
Email: elizabeth.elliott@ths.tas.gov.au

Should you require further information regarding the application process please contact

Marita Eccles
Medical Staffing Unit
Email:  medical.recruitment@ths.tas.gov.au

Better health and quality of life around Tasmania.
Visit us at www.ths.tas.gov.au

What it is like working at the Department of Health? 

Compassion, Accountability, Respect, Excellence are the key values to work in Department of Health. Listen to some of the lived experiences from within the department through some of our wonderful staff and hear about their journey in relocating to Tasmania!

Respecting diversity is the foundation of everything that Department of Health do. This allows us to instil trust and collaborate through honest and fair communication and helps cultivate an environment of growth and innovation. We strongly encourage applicants from key communities including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders, LGBTIQA+ people, and people living with disabilities.

Important Information  

The email account you provide when submitting job applications will be used in correspondence to you.  It is important that this is kept up to date and monitored regularly. To update your email address (or contact number), log in to www.jobs.tas.gov.au and look for “Existing applicant login” where you can update your details. 

The Department of Health values workforce diversity and recognises the value each person offers which is shaped by their unique characteristics, background, experiences, knowledge, skills, values and perspectives.

json.title: Continuing Care Coordinator

content.jobHook: Make a real difference in addiction recovery. Supportive culture, professional development & competitive salary in Tennant Creek.
content.unEditedContent:
About the role


Reporting to the Executive Manager Client Pathways, this full-time Continuing Care Coordinator role is an exciting opportunity to join the BRADAAG' team in Tennant Creek, NT. In this vital position, you will play a key part in coordinating the ongoing care and support for clients accessing BRADAAG's alcohol and other drug services.

What you'll be doing

  • Coordinate and monitor the ongoing care and support for clients, including developing individualised care plans and facilitating access to appropriate services

  • Maintain regular contact with clients to provide support, monitor progress and address any emerging issues

  • Liaise with a range of internal and external stakeholders, such as other service providers, to ensure coordinated and holistic care for clients

  • Provide comprehensive case notes and maintain accurate client records

  • Contribute to the evaluation and continuous improvement of BRADAAG's programs and services

  • Participate in team meetings and professional development opportunities


What we're looking for

  • Relevant tertiary qualification in a health or social services field, such as nursing, social work or community services

  • Demonstrated experience in case management or care coordination, preferably in the alcohol and other drugs or mental health sectors

  • Minimum of 1-2 years experience in case management or care coordination

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build rapport and engage effectively with a diverse range of clients

  • Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage a complex caseload

  • Commitment to person-centred, trauma-informed and culturally responsive practice

  • Ability to work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary team

  • Australian citizenship or permanent residency required


What we offer

  • Competitive salary and salary packaging options

  • Ongoing professional development and training opportunities

  • Supportive and inclusive organisational culture

  • Employee assistance program and wellbeing initiatives


About BRADAAG'


BRADAAG' is a not-for-profit organisation providing a range of alcohol and other drug services in Tennant Creek and the Barkly region of the Northern Territory. With a strong focus on harm reduction and recovery, we are committed to supporting our clients on their journey to improved health and wellbeing.

Apply now, applications close 10pm on Sunday, 31 May 2026 unless filled sooner.

For more information or a copy of the job description email: hr@bradaag.org.au

content.jobHook: Join a growing team of allied health professional supporting individuals return to work after injury!
content.unEditedContent:
Pinnacle Rehab is an award-winning workplace rehab provider, with the goal of achieving quality recovery and return-to-work outcomes for individuals who have been injured at work, our dedicated consultants support these individuals to regain their confidence and independence.  

Our people are at the forefront of the business, we are committed to staff development and training. The collaborative team culture, extensive induction and onboarding into the business will support you to build a solid foundation into the industry of occ rehab. 
  • Certified ‘Great Place to Work’ and #2 Best workplaces in Healthcare and Social Assistance in Australia, Best workplaces for Women 
  • Structured induction, and individually tailored onboarding program 
  • Flexibility to organise your own calendar with appointments, office days and work-from-home 
  • Ongoing support in a collaborative and fun team environment 
The Opportunity: 
    
Driven by ongoing growth across our Same Employer Division, we are offering a unique opportunity to be part of our expanding success. As a New Graduate or experienced Occupational Therapist you will have a chance to further develop your clinical reasoning skills and play a key role in supporting effective return to work plans. 
 
You will be involved within a structured and hands-on induction, shadowing opportunities and classroom sessions in your first week, followed by ongoing remote learning modules to provide clear understanding of the workers' compensation framework. 
  
Ongoing individual support and team meetings with Team Leader, peer mentor sessions to help you develop the skills to drive and achieve the best possible outcomes for your clients.  
 
Looking after a client portfolio, your day will include:  
  • Manage a portfolio of clients with a physical injury providing return-to-work services and  
  • One off - Activities of Daily Living (ADL) assessments and making recommendations 
  • Complete initial assessments to better understand the injury, recovery timeframes and return to work goals 
  • Visiting workplace to assess environment and duties within the role, identify with employer of any suitable duties while recovering 
  • Providing support through recommendations for community assistance or additional support through the insurer 
  • Working within a multidisciplinary team to provide complex stakeholder management to support the recovery of an injured worker 
  • Document case notes as part of reporting and compliance requirements, applying your clinical judgement to support and guide your clients to a safe return to work goal 
What is on offer: 
  • Excellent remuneration on offer plus achievable bonus 
  • All travel reimbursed at $0.99 per km, including tolls and parking expenses 
  • Structured induction and onboarding with buddy system, including ongoing weekly and monthly team meetings to support your learning 
  • Professional development opportunities – internal training programs for leadership and management 
  • Latest technology with laptop and iPhone provided  
  • Regular seasonal social events throughout the year 
  • Annual Christmas party 
  • Opportunity to participate in our Emerging Leaders Program for career development opportunities 
Your Wellbeing our Heartbeat - Our employee benefits program   
  • Wellbeing Support - Employee Assistance Programs 
  • Employee Connection - Social entertainment budgets 
  • Life Balance - Unplug agreement, flexible working arrangements 
  • Paid Parental Leave - entitlements to support your growing family 
  • Learning and Development - Group supervision sessions, quarterly formal professional development and monthly bites and insights
About You     
  • General Registration with AHPRA 
  • Tertiary degree in Occupational Therapy
  • Car and valid Driver’s license 
  • Satisfactory police check or willingness to obtain prior to commencement
  • Ability to build strong stakeholder relationships 
  • Ability to work in autonomously and as part of a team 
Pinnacle Rehab is an equal opportunity employer who encourages applications from suitably qualified candidates from all cultures, ages, religions and genders. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. 
 
Next Steps 
 
Opportunities like this won’t stick around long! If this sounds like your next rewarding role, feel free to reach out directly for a chat or apply through the "Apply" button, and we’ll be in touch to discuss further. 

careers@pinnaclerehab.com.au or call Ash 0455 118 755
  
Applications close on 14th June, 2026.

Permanent part time | Marrickville at Willandra Aged Care
content.jobHook: Provide and monitor the person-centred care of our residents alongside a welcoming, experienced clinical team.
content.unEditedContent:
Bolton Clarke is Australia's largest independent, not-for-profit aged care provider shaping the future of positive ageing. With RSL Queensland and the Royal District Nursing Service at the heart of our DNA, we have been caring for Australians since 1885. Today, our exceptional teams support more than 130,000 people to live independently at home and across our 43 retirement living communities and 88 residential aged care homes. Everything we do is dedicated to enabling, celebrating and supporting older Australians to live and age positively.

About The Role
As a Registered Nurse, you'll provide a range of clinical care and support services for our residents, assisting them to experience a greater level of independence and ensuring their health and wellness are supported. These include:
  • Providing and monitoring the care of residents
  • Using a systematic approach to clinical decision-making
  • Developing appropriate therapeutic and caring relationships
  • Collaborating with the health care team to achieve resident outcomes
  • Participating in the development of a supportive environment with the team

To be successful, you will have
  • Relevant qualifications and AHPRA registration
  • Minimum of 12 months experience as a Registered Nurse (desirable in-charge)
  • Valid working rights in Australia (Passport, Birth Certificate etc)
  • NDIS Workers Screen and or a National Police check (or willingness to obtain) prior to commencement
  • Ability to communicate effectively with residents, families and all levels of staff
  • Strong passion for working with the elderly and dedication to professional growth
  • Work for an organisation committed to resident respect and dignity, where you will receive a competitive salary and benefits.

About this location:

Located in Marrickville, the multi-cultural hub of Sydney's inner-west, Willandra provides high-quality aged care in a friendly, secure and comfortable residential environment.

What We Can Offer

Our culture is both supportive and collaborative, where you can make your role your own. In return you'll get:

  • A work culture that truly values you and invests in your career.
  • Salary packaging & tax benefits up to $15,900 tax free & additional $2,650 entertainment
  • Up to 10 weeks parental paid leave, 1 additional public holiday per year nominated by Bolton Clarke, up to 2 days a year infectious illness leave
  • A range of employee discounts and benefits.
  • Free seasonal flu vaccinations
  • Ongoing professional development and career opportunities.
  • Mental Health Programs (EAP).

Our residential aged care communities are supported by specialised teams who care deeply about our residents' individual needs. Together with residents, healthcare partners and families, our teams deliver best practice care with the highest standards of safety, clinical practice and governance.

Apply Now: Our application process takes 10 minutes to apply, please follow the below link to start your application.

Our commitment to diversity: At Bolton Clarke we expect our staff to respect and value differences in age, disability, race, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity, intersex status and family or marital status.

Appointment to this position and ongoing employment is subject to your commitment to supporting diversity and inclusion.

content.jobHook: Create fun, safe experiences for children at Camp Australia! Enjoy great benefits, job security, & career growth while making a real impact every day.
content.unEditedContent:
Camp Australia is on the hunt for a passionate, Permanent Educator to join our team in Marlow Lagoon If you're excited about building meaningful connections with children, their families, and the local school community, we want YOU!

As an educator with us, you will get the job security of a permanent contract and you’ll be at the heart of all the fun and excitement—whether it’s before school, after school, or during school holidays. In this role, you’ll help design a safe, engaging, and compliant program, leading exciting daily activities to help primary-aged children. Plus, you’ll get to prepare and serve delicious, healthy snacks to keep everyone energised to learn and grow.

 

OUR VALUES 

Our values, Courage, Gratitude, Respect, Joy, and Belonging, guide everything we do and ensure a culture where everyone thrives.

 

BENEFITS

  • We’ve been approved to offer the ECEC Worker Retention Grant. This means you’ll receive an increase on top of your award hourly rate.
  • Partnered with Flare Benefits for exclusive savings on fuel, groceries, tech, fashion, dining, entertainment, and more!
  • Enjoy Competitive rates on a permanent contract with no weekend work
  • Receive split shift allowances when working Before School Care & After School Care, or attending team meetings outside of shifts
  • Take advantage of career growth opportunities through internal promotions and study pathways, plus access subsidised Diploma qualifications for eligible staff
  • Get paid for your onboarding and ongoing professional training and development

 

ABOUT YOU

  • Enthusiastic, engaging approach to childcare with strong relationship-building skills.
  • You have completed a childcare-related Certificate III, Diploma or equivalent.
  • Valid Working with Children Check Ochre Card (or willingness to obtain).
  • National Child Safety Training (or willingness to obtain)
  • Valid First Aid, CPR, Anaphylaxis, and Asthma certificates (or willingness to obtain).
  • Availability between 6:30 am - 8:30 am & 2:15 pm - 6:00 pm, Monday to Friday (28.75 hour per week contract).

 

At Camp Australia, child safety and wellbeing are our highest priorities.
We are a child safe organisation, committed to creating inclusive, supportive environments where every child feels safe, respected and empowered. We have zero tolerance for any form of child abuse or harm, and all our staff share the responsibility of upholding our strong child safeguarding culture.

 

WANT TO KNOW MORE ABOUT US?

Visit us at www.campaustralia.com.au or email talentacquisition@campaustralia.com.au to learn more!

content.jobHook: Play a Key role in completing Inland Rail's I2S project - One of Australia's most significant nation-building infrastructure program.
content.unEditedContent:
Rail Delivery & Engineering Professionals (Civil | Track | Structures)

About the opportunity

Inland Rail - Illabo to Stockinbingal (I2S) Greenfield | Active Construction Phase | Immediate needs 14:7 roster | FIFO or DIDO | Project Specified contracts


Roles / Disciplines:

  • Construction Manager
  • Senior Project Engineer - Civil
  • Senior Project Engineer - Track
  • Senior Project Engineer - Civil/Structures
  • Project Engineer - Civil
  • Project Engineer - Track
  • Project Engineer - Civil/Structures
  • Supervisor / Site Surveillance - Civil x 2
  • Supervisor / Site Surveillance - Track x 2

Why join Inland Rail now:

This is your opportunity to be part of one of Australia's most significant nation‑building infrastructure programs-join us now and play a critical role in completing Inland Rail's I2S Project.



About the Project

The Illabo to Stockinbingal (I2S) Greenfield section is a ~39km new rail corridor in regional NSW, creating a more efficient route by bypassing local townships and the steep, winding Bethungra Spiral section.

Construction is ramping up and we're recruiting experienced rail delivery & engineering professionals to support corridor delivery across civil (including structures/culverts, earthworks), rail and road related work packages.


What you'll be working on:
Site-based delivery across packages including bulk earthworks, structures, culverts, track formation rail system interfaces on a 14:7 roster


About you

You are a capable and collaborative construction professional experienced in delivering major rail or linear infrastructure projects, with strong technical capability, clear communication skills, and a proactive, solutions-focused mindset.

What we're looking for:

  • Proven delivery experience on major rail or linear infrastructure projects

content.jobHook: Come join the Macmahon Underground Team and be a key part of our exciting Project!!!
content.unEditedContent:
Join the Macmahon Underground team as an experienced Underground HD Mechanic and be responsible for daily service and repairs to the light and heavy vehicle fleet to maintain the safety and reliability standards according to the manufacturer's specifications and requirements.

About the role

  • Residential option for Bendigo, VIC and surrounds
  • 2:2 roster (Days and Nights Roster)
  • Interstate FIFO flights covered from any capital city

About you

  • Previous experience in a similar role, preferably within a mine site environment
  • Australian recognised Trade Certificate (Cert III in Mobile Plant)
  • Demonstrated experience working on Sandvik Drill rigs (ideal)
  • Proven experience in the repairs and maintenance of heavy earthmoving equipment underground
  • Breakdown repairs and servicing of heavy mining equipment
  • Diagnostic fault finding on mechanical systems
  • Maintain maintenance data on a daily basis
  • Sound planning and organisational skills

Employee benefits

  • Ongoing career development opportunities - Challenge. Develop. Grow.
  • Dedicated lifestyle, financial and mental health support
  • Salary sacrifice options for flights, vehicles, airport parking and A LOT more
  • Access to a wide range of employee discounts with Macmahon retail, vehicle, insurance and banking partners

Across Macmahon's team, you will find positive stories of people embracing opportunities to develop and grow their careers going on to celebrate impressive career milestones that contribute to our success. Macmahon is a leading Australian contract mining company with projects throughout Australia and Southeast Asia. Delivering a comprehensive range of surface and underground mining, civil design and construction, performance enhancement, and mine site maintenance and rehabilitation services to the resources sector.

Successful applicants must pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening, as well as criminal history and qualification checks. Proof of working rights in Australia (valid passport, birth certificate, citizenship certificate, or current visa grant notification) is also required.

Macmahon is an equal opportunity employer and strongly encourages suitably qualified women and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders to apply.

Macmahon Winning Values
United | Integrity | Courage | Pride

content.jobHook: Are you wanting to upgrade your Electrical Apprenticeship and find an employer who cares? power up your future with real industry skills through FHR!
content.unEditedContent:
Frontline HR South Australia are looking for electrical apprentices to continue their apprenticeship. The opportunities are based across Adelaide, offering a broad range of projects for you to gain real industry experience.

As a registered Group Training Organisation (GTO), we give you the opportunity to work with a vast number of Host Employers throughout your apprenticeship. This allows you to gain a broad range of electrical experience and get the most out of your Apprenticeship. You will work full time whilst completing a Certificate III in Electrotechnology.

Responsibilities will vary between host employers, but can include:

  • Rough in and fit off electrical cabling and equipment
  • Installing cable tray
  • Assisting with the installation of power and lighting circuits
  • Installing of power points and light fittings
  • Wiring and labelling electrical sub panels and enclosures
  • Final test check, fault finding and troubleshooting
  • Building and fabrication of switchboards
  • Installation of conduits
  • Wiring and installing data cabling and equipment
  • Commercial solar installation



The successful Apprentices will be:

  • Safety conscious, consistently adhering to OH&S regulations
  • A team player with a good attitude towards work
  • Able to show initiative and work autonomously
  • Ready to ask questions and learn
  • Reliable and punctual



Requirements:

  • Minimum 6 months experience as an electrical apprentice
  • Current Driver's License
  • Willing to undertake a Police Check and/or Medical
  • Australian working rights



What you will receive:

  • Ongoing mentoring & support
  • Comprehensive PPE and footwear
  • Additional training opportunities for tickets and licenses
  • Potential to work on major infrastructure projects


This in an amazing opportunity to undergo an Apprenticeship where you will gain experience in numerous fields across the Electrical industry. This is an opportunity not to be missed! Please note: only successful applicants will be contacted.


If this sounds like the job for you, apply today!

To be eligible for an apprenticeship or traineeship you must be an Australian Citizen, Permanent Resident or have full working rights in Australia.

content.jobHook: Lead landscape projects with BluScape in Adelaide.
content.unEditedContent:
🌿 Project Manager – BluScape Landscaping


Location: Adelaide, SA
Employment Type: Full-Time


Build landscapes. Lead projects. Create impact.

BluScape Landscaping is a leader in delivering high-quality, sustainable landscape construction projects across South Australia. With a strong reputation for excellence, innovation, and environmentally responsible practices, we are seeking a driven and experienced Project Manager to join our growing team.

At BluScape, we don’t just build landscapes — we create outdoor environments that enhance communities and stand the test of time. If you’re passionate about delivering exceptional projects while leading teams and driving performance, we want to hear from you.


🌱 About the Role

As a Project Manager, you will take ownership of multiple landscape construction projects, ensuring they are delivered safely, on time, within budget, and to the highest quality standards. Working closely with the Landscape Manager, you will play a key role in contract administration, project delivery, and team leadership.

🔧 Key ResponsibilitiesProject Delivery & Performance
  • Lead and manage projects across all phases – from planning to completion
  • Ensure projects meet safety, quality, time, and profitability targets
  • Develop construction programs, budgets, and cash flow forecasts
  • Manage labour, plant, and materials allocation across projects
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, subcontractors, and stakeholders
Contract Administration
  • Administer contracts, variations, and extensions of time (EOTs)
  • Prepare progress claims, reports, and final contract documentation
  • Review and approve subcontractor and supplier claims
  • Prepare subcontract documentation and manage subcontractor performance
  • Identify and manage commercial and contractual risks
Safety, Quality & Environment
  • Implement BluScape’s WHS, Quality, and Environmental systems
  • Promote and enforce safe work practices and environmental awareness
  • Develop and implement Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS), quality plans, and environmental management plans
  • Conduct site audits, toolbox talks, and monitor compliance
  • Investigate and resolve non-conformances
Leadership & Development
  • Mentor and develop junior team members
  • Support recruitment, performance reviews, and team development
  • Foster a positive and collaborative team culture aligned with BluScape values
✅ About You

You are a motivated and detail-oriented professional with a passion for landscape construction and project excellence.

You will bring:

  • Proven experience as a Project Manager in construction or landscaping
  • Strong understanding of contract administration and project financials
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
  • Knowledge of WHS, environmental, and quality systems
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and leadership skills
  • A proactive approach to problem-solving and risk management
🌏 Why Join BluScape?
  • Work with a respected industry leader in landscape construction
  • Be part of projects that prioritise sustainability and “green construction”
  • Supportive team environment with strong leadership
  • Opportunities for growth, training, and career progression
  • Competitive salary package aligned with experience
🚀 Apply Now

If you’re ready to take the next step in your career and contribute to award-winning landscape projects, we’d love to hear from you.

Join BluScape Landscaping and help shape the environments where people live, work, and thrive.

  • C#, .NET Core
  • APIs and Microservices
  • Event-driven and Distributed Systems
  • Azure

  • Modern Design Patterns
  • SOLID principles

We are currently seeking experienced Electricians for immediate starts across a range of commercial installation, maintenance, and upgrade projects throughout Brisbane.

These positions offer long-term ongoing work, consistent hours, and the opportunity to work across well-established commercial environments with a strong pipeline of upcoming projects.


What’s on Offer
  • $55 - $60/hr + Super
  • Ongoing casual role with long-term opportunities
  • Immediate starts available
  • Stable Monday to Friday work
  • 6:00am – 3:00pm shifts
  • Variety of commercial installation and maintenance work
Key Duties
  • Commercial Construction
  • Solar inspections
  • Lighting upgrades and replacements
  • General electrical installation and maintenance
  • Preventative & reactive maintenance
  • Fault finding, diagnosis, and repairs
  • Switchboard and small upgrade works
  • Testing, commissioning, and compliance checks
  • Supporting minor projects and site upgrades
About the Role

You’ll be working across a variety of commercial sites completing a mix of:
  • Reactive breakdown and maintenance work
  • Planned preventative maintenance
  • Small to mid-sized upgrade projects
We are also interested in speaking with Electricians who have experience in estimating and project scoping, particularly for small to medium commercial works.

This role would suit tradespeople who can work autonomously, communicate well on site, and enjoy a varied workload.

If interested please apply within or get in contact with Kristian from Intro Recruitment

Kristian Luppes

Hybrid role - run your own diary!
content.jobHook: Are you frustrated in your current role... Are you looking to work within a collaborative & professional environment!
content.unEditedContent:
Pinnacle Rehab is an award-winning workplace rehab provider, with the goal of achieving quality recovery and return-to-work outcomes for individuals who have been injured at work, our dedicated consultants support these individuals to regain their confidence and independence.  

Our people are at the forefront of the business, we are committed to staff development and training. The collaborative team culture, extensive induction and onboarding into the business will support you to build a solid foundation into the industry of occ rehab.  
  • Certified ‘Great Place to Work’ and #2 Best workplaces in Healthcare and Social Assistance in Australia, Best Workplace for Women  
  • Structured induction, and individually tailored onboarding program  
  • Flexibility to organise your own calendar with appointments, office days and work-from-home  
  • Ongoing support in a collaborative and fun team environment  
What is on offer:  
  • Excellent remuneration on offer plus achievable bonus  
  • All travel reimbursed at $0.99 per km, including tolls and parking expenses  
  • Structured induction and on-boarding with buddy system, including ongoing weekly and monthly team meetings to support your learning  
  • Professional development opportunities  
  • Latest technology with laptop and iPhone provided   
  • Regular seasonal social events throughout the year  
  • Annual staff company wide party  
  • Opportunity to participate in our Emerging Leaders Program for career development opportunities    
Your Wellbeing our Heartbeat - Our employee benefits program    
  • Wellbeing Support - Employee Assistance Programs 
  • Employee Connection - Social entertainment budgets 
  • Life Balance - Unplug agreement, flexible working arrangements 
  • Paid Parental Leave - Entitlements to support your growing family 
  • Learning and Development - Group supervision sessions, quarterly formal professional development and monthly bites and insights
The Opportunity 
  
Your new role as a Employment Consultant will see you managing a portfolio of clients who are in the job seeking phase of their rehabilitation. 
  
Within this role you will be travelling to different hubs within your region to have face to face meetings with your clients and attend the office for team catch-ups on a monthly basis.  
  
This role requires a people oriented professional with a positive, forward thinking caring attitude and the desire to help others secure new employment. 
  
Within your new role you will; 
  • Providing support for clients, preparing them for new employment  
  • Contacting prospective businesses to discuss staffing solutions & incentives for job trials/placements 
  • Assisting clients with resume drafting 
  • Delivering job seeking training (specific training modules) 
  • Career planning, job matching  
  • Developing local relationships with prospective employers 
  • Post placement check-in support 
  About You 
  • 1 + years’ experience in a similar role  
  • Recruitment background assisting individuals with barriers secure new employment 
  • Car and valid Driver’s license 
  • Exceptional time management and attention to detail 
  • Ability to build strong stakeholder relationships 
  • Ability to work autonomously and as part of a team 
  • Confidence over the phone and ability to strong network with potential employers 
  • Police check or willingness to obtain a police check prior to commencement 
Pinnacle Rehab is an equal opportunity employer who encourages applications from suitably qualified candidates from all cultures, ages, religions and genders. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. 
  
If you are looking for the next step in your career, apply today. 
  
Next Steps! Apply now or contact Ash via email: ashk@pinnaclerehab.com.au or phone: 0455 118 755  for more information. 

Applications close 14th June, 2026.

json.title: Mechanical Automation Technician - Night Shift

content.jobHook: Join SSI SCHAEFER as we expand operations under a new contract with a high-profile beverage and FMCG company.
content.unEditedContent:
About the Roles

Are you a skilled tradesperson or technician looking for an exciting new challenge? SSI SCHAEFER has expanded its operations at an existing site in Mentone Victoria as part of a new contract with a high-profile beverage and FMCG company. You'll work with state-of-the-art automated warehouse systems and play a key role in helping SSI SCHAEFER successfully transition the site successfully.

This is a unique opportunity to join SSI SCHAEFER as we expand our customer portfolio. Be part of a dynamic team supporting operations now under SSI SCHAEFER management.

Australian citizens and permanent residents are eligible to apply for these positions.

Who we're looking for

RM Technicians - Mechanical & Electrical

Shift: 12hr Night Shifts 6pm-6am, even time Panama Roster. 2 on, 2 off, 3 on, 2 off, 2 on, and 3 off.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Provide technical support during breakdowns, shutdowns, and all preventative/corrective maintenance

  • Complete CMMS work orders accurately and on time

  • Ensure maintenance and repairs meet OEM standards

  • Liaise with SSI SCHAEFER international helpdesk and R&D for technical support and improvements

  • Update CMMS with repair notes, spare parts usage, and improvement recommendations

  • Support site KPIs, continuous improvement initiatives, and team efficiency

  • Promote a safe and collaborative work environment

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Hands-on experience diagnosing and resolving mechanical/electrical/mechatronic issues

  • Familiar with automated warehouse machinery

  • Ability to interpret technical drawings and manuals

  • Experience with CMMS software

  • Strong organisational, teamwork, and customer focus skills

Qualifications / Certifications:

  • Electrical: Unrestricted electrical license, PLC & VSD fault finding/programming, Pneumatics & Hydraulics advantageous

  • Mechanical: Mechanical Trade Certificate

  • Working at Heights & Rescue certifications, First Aid + CPR

  • Exposure to automated warehouse environments and continuous improvement advantageous

  • Minimum 2 years in the automation industry

Why Join Us?

Become part of our success story!

The SSI SCHAEFER Group is a leading global solution provider for all areas of intralogistics.  With innovative technologies and software, the family-owned company empowers customers to increase the efficiency and sustainability of their storage, picking and transport processes.  From full automated warehouses, with individual service and maintenance offers, to manual and semi-automated systems, SSI SCHAEFER offers cost effective intralogistics solutions from a single source, for small and medium-sized businesses as well as large companies. SSI SCHAEFER has also become one of the largest vendors of software for internal material flow control and offers all possibilities for sustainable resource management with modern real-time analyses, smart data processing and optimisation algorithms. With SSI SCHAEFER Plastics, the company is also an expert in sustainable container systems and customized constructive packaging, as well as solutions for wase and recycling management.

SSI SCHAEFER employes more than 8,800 people at is international headquarter in Neunkirchen (Germany) and in approximately 80 operating companies globally, including seven production facilities on six continents. In fiscal year 2024, the company generated a revenue of EUR 2.0 billion.

Our commitment to Work Health and Safety

We have a strong focus on and commitment to health and safety and expect all workers to:

  • Comply with relevant WHS legislation

  • Follow company policies and procedures

  • Proactively report hazards and incidents

  • Contribute to a safe working environment for all, including psychological and psychosocial safety

Ready to make your mark in the world of industrial automation? Apply now!

No agencies please

json.salary: Estimated full time equivalent $160,000+ per year

content.jobHook: Part-time Physiotherapist role in Burwood, managing WorkCover & CTP clients within a supportive multidisciplinary medical centre.
content.unEditedContent:
Job Location: Burwood

About Us

Our medical centre is a dedicated multidisciplinary clinic specialising in themanagement of Workers’ Compensation and Compulsory Third Party (CTP) cases. Our team of experienced General Practitioners works closely with allied health and specialist providers to deliver high quality, patient centred care with a strong focus on functional recovery and return to work outcomes.

We take a collaborative, coordinated approach to care and maintain strong professional relationships with rehabilitation providers, insurers, and employers to ensure the best possible outcomes for our patients.

Why Join Us

This is an exciting opportunity for an independent contractor to work alongside an engaged and supportive GP team within a growing, purpose-driven practice. At our medical centre, you will benefit from consistent referral opportunities and a well-established clinical network, while retaining flexibility and autonomy in how you structure your work.

Our model is designed to minimise administrative burden so you can focus on delivering quality clinical care. Dedicated administrative staff manage bookings, billing coordination, insurer correspondence, and report follow-ups, allowing you to spend your time where it matters most, with patients.

You will also be supported by an established multidisciplinary network that includes physiotherapists, chiropractors, psychologists, counsellors, occupational therapists, dietitians, return to work rehabilitation providers, and medical and surgical specialists, enabling a comprehensive and coordinated approach to care.

BENEFITS

·Strong referral opportunities from an engaged GP team

·Flexible working arrangements - one to two days per week initially, with scope to grow

·Fully equipped rooms with all equipment and consumables supplied

·Dedicated marketing support to help promote and develop your career

·Supervision and mentoring provided by a senior physiotherapist

·Remuneration well above industry average. With scope for progression as your skills, experience, and competencies develop.

We offer contractors the opportunity to build a sustainable caseload (no expectations on KPIs!) within a supportive, professional environment while making a meaningful impact on patient recovery and return to function. We are seeking a part-time physiotherapist for 1–2 days per week, with the opportunity to increase days. Estimated full-time equivalent income is $160k+ per annum.

JOB DETAILS:

Key responsibilities include:

·Manage a varied caseload of Workcover and CTP clients, combining musculoskeletal rehabilitation, exercise-based care, and injury prevention.

·Consistently deliver high-quality service by applying evidence-based treatment approaches and facilitating early and safe return to work.

·Maintaining accurate documentation, records, and preparing reports.

·Proactively engaging with injured workers, Insurance Case Manager, employers, NTDs (Nominated Treating Doctors), and other stakeholders to drive prompt and positive outcomes.

ABOUT YOU

To succeed in this role, you will have:

·Current AHPRA Physiotherapy registration

·SIRA provider number

·2+ years of experience as a physiotherapist

·Professional indemnity insurance

·Confidence in managing your own caseload

·Strong communication and interpersonal skills

·A collaborative mindset and passion for quality care

·English, Mandarin and/or Cantonese speaking applicants preferred

·Pilates experience is advantageous

Ready for Your Next Step?

If you’re looking for a role where your skills are recognised, your income reflects your value, and your work-life balance is respected, apply now.

content.jobHook: If you enjoy the diversity of work, working on a variety of high-end projects & having fun along the way, we welcome your application.
content.unEditedContent:
PROJECT MANAGER 

GE Hughes Construction Co is a family owned business based in the Adelaide Hills at Lobethal. 

As one of South Australia’s most unique and diverse companies, we offer a large variety of work and opportunities.

 We are looking for accomplished, driven and team-oriented Project Manager / Construction Manager with an exceptional eye for detail and well-developed time management skills. 

 We are proud to work in all facets of the building industry from residential, civil, commercial and renewable works and manage most trades in house – earthworks, concreting, brickwork, carpentry, cabinetmaking, steelwork and transport.

Due to this diversity, we offer unmatched variety in your role and a broad range of career advancement opportunities. 

 About the role:

·         High level of communication. 

·         Manage incoming enquiries, quoting and project evaluation.

·         Liaise between clients, architects, building designers, interior designers, suppliers and sub-contractors.

·         Collate quotes from sub-contractors and suppliers for all building works.

·         Prepare and present estimates/quotes to management.

·         Manage and source of materials.

·         Provide project tender documentation and variations to clients and project delivery.

·         Develop and deliver on project schedules.

·         Costings for materials, workers and machinery to meet project deadlines and budgets.

·         Engage Suppliers and contractors to meet project demands.

·         Company vehicle supplied

 If you enjoy working on a wide variety of projects, big or small and having fun along the way, apply today! 

 If you have the right attitude, we can teach you to be multi-skilled in a dynamic business environment.

About the business



Morris Cohen Glen & Co is a Australian Financial Review Top 100 firm of Chartered Accountants based in Camberwell with a focus on providing a high level of service, advice and expertise to our varied and interesting client base.


An exciting opportunity is available for an Accountant position, where you will join our team of young professionals, where the skills you have the opportunity to learn have lasting value and will form the foundation of your career.


Our team is dedicated to providing our clients with high standard of service using the latest technology with a particular focus on cloud based accounting.


Our Firm takes great pride in the work we do and as a result we have high standards. We aim to provide a polished and professional service to our clients – giving the same high-quality service that we would like to receive.




About the role

 

The successful candidate will become a part of a team that looks after a varied and interesting client base including:


  • Business clients across various industries including construction, professional services and property development.

  • Tax affairs on international companies operating in Australia- foreign branch or subsidiary.

  • Set up and processing of Payroll for the clients.

  • Investor clients with substantial holdings in property and equities.

  • Reviewing junior staff work (ITRs, BAS/IAS and basic companies & trusts)

  • Preparation of financials & tax returns for multi-entity structures



The team works collaboratively together to assist client needs, improve their skills and drive excellent commercial outcomes for clients. We support one another to solve problems and help clients each and every day.


Initially working in the Senior Accountant role, your duties will include but are not limited to:

  • Accurate, efficient and timely preparation of financial statements, tax returns and BAS’s for individuals, partnerships, companies and trusts and management reporting.

  • Be a first point of contact for clients, coordinating their requests and ensuring deadlines are met.

  • Reviewing work prepared by other team members and clients Bookkeepers.

  • Working directly with the Partner in high-level and complex consulting engagements.



We would expect and work with the successful candidate to ensure that they will continue grow and learn and move into more senior and challenging roles (Supervisor / Manager) with the team and the firm & Morris Cohen Glen & Co.



Benefits and perks

 

Our firm does not believe in our team working unnecessary long and extended hours, we have standard 36.25 hours per week.


Whilst we work hard and give high quality service to our clients this can be done without the long hours of many big firms.


And we have a full A4 page of wonderful benefits including yearly salary increases, progression pathways and a long list of thoughtful social perks.


We offer the successful applicant:


  • Direct contact with Partners to help develop you

  • Strong training support to supplement your skills

  • We will train and guide you in all major tax and accounting areas

  • A healthy work life balance

  • Free office and on street car parking and office just two minutes walk from the nearby train station

  • Support for Visa / Permanent Residency (PR)

  • Modern inner-East Melbourne Offices 

  • Progressive, fun and energetic youthful environment 

  • Opportunity to grow and enhance your skillset



Skills and experience

 

  • We are candidates that that possess the following:

  • Studied Accounting major at university

  • CA / CPA or close to completing

  • 1+ years accounting or payroll experience, ideally gained within a public practice or professional services firm

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

  • Strong attention to detail

  • The ability to multi-task and meet deadlines

  • Strong dedication to teamwork, a willingness to work hard, learn and develop new skills using the latest technology

  • The right to work in Australia. Our Company has the ability to sponsor candidates and will consider this on a case by case basis.


 


If this sounds like the role for you, please submit your CV outlining why you believe you are the right hire for Morris Cohen Glen & Co, using the apply now function below.


If you have queries that you would like to discuss before submitting your CV, please contact Harish Budhiraja at harish@morco.com.au

content.jobHook: Lead end-to-end delivery across a high-impact national reform program, driving complex workstreams in a fast-paced, hybrid environment.
content.unEditedContent:
EL1 Project Manager, Aged Care Reform

Your new company

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced EL1 Project Manager with experience in Federal or State based reform projects to contribute to a major transformation program reshaping how aged care is regulated across Australia.

The organisation undergoing significant change as part of broader government reform - including new regulatory models, strengthened oversight, and enhanced digital and operational systems. This program sits at the centre of that transformation.

You'll be working on a critical workstream focused on improving how access, processes, and systems are structured across the organisation, ensuring the Commission can operate effectively in a more modern, responsive regulatory environment.


Your new role

Reporting to the Program Manager, you will take ownership of end-to-end project delivery across key workstreams within the program.

You'll operate at the centre of delivery - bringing structure to complexity, aligning stakeholders, and ensuring outcomes are delivered in a coordinated and controlled way.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Developing and managing detailed project plans, including scope, milestones, and dependencies
  • Driving day-to-day delivery across complex, interdependent workstreams
  • Managing risks, issues, and change in a structured program environment
  • Preparing high-quality reporting, briefs, and updates for governance forums
  • Facilitating steering committees, workshops, and working groups
  • Coordinating stakeholders across policy, operations, and digital teams
  • Supporting implementation and change activities as new frameworks and systems are rolled out

You'll play a key role in ensuring the program delivers practical, scalable outcomes - not just plans on paper.


What you'll need to succeed

You are a confident, delivery-focused Project Manager with a track record of operating in government or large-scale program environments.

You will bring:

  • Proven experience delivering projects end-to-end, ideally within reform based projects (not an IT/ICT)
  • Government experience essential, healthcare experience highly beneficial (however desirable only)
  • Strong skills in planning, scheduling, and project coordination
  • Experience working within formal governance frameworks in a government setting
  • Ability to manage multiple stakeholders and competing priorities
  • Strong written communication skills, with the ability to produce high-quality reports and briefings
  • A proactive, solutions-driven mindset

Experience within regulatory, reform, or transformation programs will be highly regarded.

What you'll get in return

  • Work on a high-impact national reform initiative
  • Gain exposure to senior stakeholders and government decision-makers
  • Join a collaborative, delivery-focused program environment
  • Competitive EL1 salary ($118,588 - $135,251 + super)
  • Hybrid working based in Parramatta

Key details

  • Initial contract through to December 2026 with very high potential for extension
  • Full-time hours (37.5 per week)
  • Australian Citizenship required
  • Mix of office-based and remote working


What you need to do now

If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.

If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion on your career.

content.jobHook: Join our maintenance team at Duketon South Gold mining project - 2:1 roster - maintain our Epiroc T45 and CAT MD5150 drills
content.unEditedContent:
The Role & Project

MACA Mining are seeking experienced and skilled Drill Fitters to join our team. Your focus will be maintaining our fleet of Epiroc T45 Drill Rigs as well as our Caterpillar MD5150's

The Duketon Gold project is located in the Northeastern Goldfields of Western Australia approximately 130 kilometres north of Laverton.

Build your future with one of WA's most trusted contractors.

As a proud Thiess company, MACA is a trusted integrated contracting services group specialising in mining, civil construction, infrastructure, and mineral processing.

We strive to be the best by investing in our people, understanding our clients' needs, and having a relentless focus on continuous improvement. Our social responsibility is what drives us, and we make an impact through contributions and support we give our communities.

To be Successful in this Role, You Will Possess:

  • Australian Trade Certificate
  • Extensive surface mining drill rig experience - Epiroc, CAT preferred
  • HR Driver Licence (preferred)
  • Problem-solving ability, diagnostic and troubleshooting skills whilst being able to repair and maintain.
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Highly motivated with the ability to work independently
  • Good knowledge and ability to follow Work Health & Safety procedures and policies.

What we will offer you:

  • FIFO 2:1 roster (7days,7nights,7r&r)
  • Full time and casual rates available.
  • Superannuation paid on all hours worked.
  • Paid maternity leave.
  • Competitive rates and access to a range of corporate discounts and cashback offers from over 350 popular retailers.
  • Access to a dedicated online employee Wellbeing Centre providing education, support and tools to help you live a healthier life.
  • Access to salary sacrificing benefits.
  • Refer and earn program allowing you to earn up to $2,500 for referring new employees to MACA positions.
  • $3000 sign on bonus (T&C's apply)
  • Save up to 10% on your Health Insurance with BUPA, HBF or HCF.

There are many long-term opportunities available across our business, and more on the horizon. There is always room to grow and develop into the professional you want to be with MACA!

Make your mark.

If you want to come with us on our journey apply with us today

We're ready when you are.

MACA is an equal opportunity employer and strongly encourages all females and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants.

content.jobHook: Join a high-end residential builder. Great opportunity for an apprentice carpenter to learn all aspects of carpentry and construction. Immediate Start
content.unEditedContent:
🛠️ Apprentice Carpenter – High-End Residential Builds. Immediate Start.

📍 Shoalhaven Area
🔨 Full-Time Apprenticeship
🏡 Architectural Projects | Hands-On Training | Career Growth

Hatchway Constructions is a well-established residential building company specialising in high-end, architecturally designed homes. We're currently looking for Apprentice Carpenters to join our team full-time.

About the Role

You’ll work closely with a licensed, award-winning builder on a bespoke residential project.

This is a hands-on role that offers valuable exposure to all aspects of high-end residential construction — from foundations, framing and structural work through to detailed interior fit-outs.

What We’re Looking For

We’re after someone who:

  • Has a genuine interest and passion for carpentry and construction

  • Takes pride in quality workmanship and has an eye for detail and craftsmanship

  • Is reliable, motivated, and eager to learn, with the ability to follow instructions

  • Communicates well and brings a strong work ethic and positive attitude

  • Holds a White Card, car license and has reliable transport and basic tools

  • Is a 2nd, 3rd, or 4th-year apprentice (Mature-age apprentices welcome to apply, (may consider for the right person)

  • Can start immediately

What We Offer

  • The opportunity to work on architectural, one-of-a-kind homes

  • One-on-one training and mentorship from a highly experienced and award-winning builder

  • Full support towards completing your Certificate III in Carpentry

  • A positive team environment focused on skill development and career growth

📞 Apply now via Seek, or contact Jason directly on 0415 233 492 to find out more about this opportunity.
