content.jobHook: Join one of Australia’s leading dermatology organisations as a Cosmetic Nurse within a brand-new Dermatologist Led, Nurse Delivered Cosmetic Clinic.
content.unEditedContent:
Company: Skin Health Institute | Carlton, Melbourne

Position: Cosmetic Nurse

Employment type: Part Time (2 Days, Must be available Fridays)

The One Clinic Agency is proud to partner with The Skin Health Institute in the search for an experienced Cosmetic Nurse to establish a new Dermatologist Led, Nurse Delivered Cosmetic Clinic.

With a 39-year history in medical dermatology, the Skin Health Institute is recognised as one of Australia’s leading centres of excellence in dermatology and skin health. Home to 22 clinics, 6 day-surgery theatres, and a multidisciplinary network of dermatologists, plastic surgeons, nurses, and allied health, this is a unique opportunity to be part of the Institute’s first formal expansion into cosmetic and aesthetic dermatology.

This is more than just a Cosmetic Nurse role; it is an opportunity to help build and shape a new division within one of Australia’s most respected dermatology organisations.

The Role

We are seeking a dynamic, experienced, and entrepreneurial Cosmetic Nurse (RN) who is excited by the opportunity to lead, grow, and help establish a new aesthetic offering within the Institute.

Working within a Dermatologist-led, nurse-delivered model, this role will be hands-on, focused on cosmetic injectables, laser treatments, and other aesthetic therapies, while also playing a key role in driving the service forward operationally and commercially.

This position would suit a confident injector who enjoys autonomy, has strong interpersonal and business development skills, and is excited by the opportunity to grow something from the ground up with the backing of an established medical institution.

The successful candidate will work closely with dermatologists and medical specialists, with doctor-led scripting and clinical oversight available via in-person and telehealth support.


About the Opportunity

  • Attractive revenue-share incentives with a guaranteed hourly rate (+ salary sacrificing)

  • Opportunity to build and grow your own patient base within the Institute

  • Flexible arrangement: ideally 2 days per week initially, with the scope to build

  • Opportunity to help shape the future direction of the cosmetic clinic

  • Strong internal referral pathways from dermatologists, plastic surgeons, and nurses

  • Opportunity to join a prestigious centre of excellence in dermatology.

Key Responsibilities

  • Deliver safe and evidence-based cosmetic treatments, including anti-wrinkle injections, laser therapies, light-based treatments, and other aesthetic procedures within the scope of practice

  • Conduct comprehensive patient consultations, assessments, treatment planning, informed consent, and clinical documentation

  • Monitor patient outcomes and provide exceptional post-treatment care and follow-up

  • Build strong patient relationships while driving patient experience, retention, and clinic growth

  • Recognise and appropriately manage adverse events or treatment complications

  • Maintain the highest standards of infection control, patient safety, and clinical care

  • Work collaboratively with dermatologists and the wider clinical team to support integrated patient care and treatment planning

  • Support the establishment, growth, and ongoing success of the cosmetic clinic

  • Participate in clinical governance, quality improvement initiatives, and multidisciplinary discussions

  • Provide patient education regarding treatment options, expectations, risks, aftercare, and outcomes

  • Contribute to the implementation of new technologies, treatment protocols, and cosmetic services

  • Ensure all treatments and care are delivered in accordance with AHPRA guidelines, NMBA professional standards, and clinic policies and procedures

  • Stay up to date with emerging technologies, techniques, and best practice standards within cosmetic and aesthetic medicine

Requirements

  • Registered Nurse with current AHPRA registration

  • Minimum 3 years’ experience in cosmetic nursing and aesthetic treatments

  • Proven experience performing anti-wrinkle injections and other cosmetic injectable treatments

  • Experience with laser and light-based therapies highly regarded

  • Strong consultation, assessment, and treatment planning skills

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to build rapport and trust with patients

  • High level of professionalism, clinical confidence, and attention to detail

  • Strong understanding of patient safety, infection control, and clinical governance principles

  • Ability to work independently while also collaborating within a multidisciplinary team environment

  • Experience working alongside dermatologists, cosmetic physicians, or specialist medical teams highly regarded

  • Leadership qualities with the ability to contribute to clinic growth, mentoring, and service development

  • Passion for aesthetics, patient care, and ongoing professional development

  • Business acumen, initiative, and a proactive approach to growing patient relationships and clinic success

  • Commitment to delivering treatments in line with AHPRA guidelines, NMBA standards, and best practice cosmetic medicine protocols


Why Join Us?

  • Join one of Australia’s most respected dermatology organisations

  • Be part of an exciting new venture from the very beginning

  • Work alongside leading dermatologists and plastic surgeons

  • Strong clinical governance and medical support structure

  • Opportunity to help shape and grow a new cosmetic division

  • Flexible contractor arrangement with excellent earning potential

  • Collaborative, innovative, and highly respected medical environment

Ready to Apply?

If you are an experienced Cosmetic Nurse looking for an opportunity to combine clinical excellence, autonomy, and business growth within a highly respected medical organisation, we would love to hear from you.

content.unEditedContent:
Are you a Mechanic looking to get off the tools and change your direction. Maybe a Service advisor who has had enough of the 7:30 to 5:30 days, as well as being stuck behind a desk dealing with retail customers. This is an opportunity for you!

Are you a Mechanic looking to get off the tools and change your direction? We are currently seeking a permanent full time Workshop Equipment Sales Specialist to join our team based in Woodville, to provide exceptional customer service to our SA customers through advising and guiding them through our range of equipment products.

content.jobHook: Hands-on leadership role maintaining fleet, vehicles and parade floats, keeping operations running smoothly behind the scenes.
content.unEditedContent:
Team Leader Auto Electrician – Fleet & Mechanical
Full Time Salary
Movie World, Oxenford, Gold Coast

The Opportunity
Join a team that thrives on fast fixes, smart planning, and show-ready results, keeping vehicles, floats, and equipment ready for action.

As a hands-on Team Leader Auto Electrician – Fleet & Mechanical, you’ll lead a tight-knit team while keeping our fleet in top shape, ensuring everything from utility vehicles to parade floats is ready to roll.

From vehicle diagnostics and electrical systems to themed vehicles and parade floats, you’ll play a key role in keeping everything running smoothly.

If you enjoy variety, problem-solving, and leading from the front, this is your opportunity to make a real impact where no two days are the same.

Key Responsibilities
Behind every seamless operation is a team making sure everything keeps moving. You’ll be:
• Leading and supporting a small team of mechanics, driving high-quality work, safety, and performance.
• Managing fleet maintenance and servicing schedules to keep all vehicles, plant, and equipment running safely and efficiently.
• Carrying out hands-on diagnostics, fault finding, and repairs across a range of electrical systems, including themed vehicles and parade floats.
• Responding to breakdowns and troubleshooting issues to minimise downtime and keep operations moving.
• Maintaining accurate service records and coordinating parts, materials, and external providers to support maintenance activities.

What We’re Looking For
An energetic, hands-on leader who thrives on solving problems and supporting their team! You’ll bring:
• Trade qualifications in Automotive Electrical Technology (Auto Electrician) is required
• Current driver’s license (MR desirable)
• Experience with fleet management systems (desirable)
• Proven leadership or supervisory experience, with the ability to support and develop a small team.
• Solid understanding of fleet maintenance, including managing servicing schedules and programs.
• Strong problem-solving, organisational, and time management skills.
• Confident communicator who can work effectively across multiple teams and stakeholders.
• Experience with maintenance systems (SAP or Mobaro desirable).

Your backstage pass to fun, friends and unforgettable memories!
• Unlimited free entry to our amazing theme parks!
• Earn complimentary passes to share with family and friends!
• Enjoy discounts on food & beverage, retail and animal experiences across our parks!
• Exclusive employee deals through our Village Employee Benefits App, partnered with 65+ major retailers!
• Unique team events and awards, celebrating our people is part of the fun!
• Reward and recognition programs with prizes for outstanding contributions
• Wellbeing support with our on-site team and 24/7 Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
• Professional development opportunities with internal training, we love to grow our talent!

At Village Roadshow Theme Parks, our purpose is simple: create joy and memories that last a lifetime. Every day, our team brings this to life across our iconic properties , from Warner Bros. Movie World and Sea World, to Wet’n’Wild, Paradise Country, Topgolf, Sea World Resort, Australian Outback Spectacular, and Village Roadshow Studios.

Working here isn’t just a job, it’s being part of a team that loves what they do, in a vibrant, fun, and supportive environment. You’ll meet amazing people, develop new skills, and help create unforgettable experiences for our guests.

We value everyone’s unique contributions and encourage candidates of all backgrounds, abilities, and experiences to apply. Apply today to join one of the most exciting tourist attractions on the Gold Coast and start creating memories, for our guests, your team, and your career!

content.jobHook: Build the future with Google - flexible, scalable cloud services
content.unEditedContent:
At Google, we have a vision of empowerment and equitable opportunity for all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and commit to building reconciliation through Google’s technology, platforms and people and we welcome Indigenous applicants. Please see our Reconciliation Action Plan for more information.
Note: By applying to this position you will have an opportunity to share your preferred working location from the following: Canberra ACT, Australia; Sydney NSW, Australia.

Minimum qualifications:
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 2 years of experience with software programming in C++, Java, Python or Go.
  • Successful candidates will be required to hold and maintain the Australian Government Security Vetting Agency (AGSVA) Negative Vetting 1 (NV1).
Preferred qualifications:
  • Master's degree in Computer Science or a related technical field.
  • 2 years of experience with data structures and algorithms.
  • Experience developing accessible technologies.
About the job
Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

The Google Australia Sovereign Cloud team builds, delivers and operates secure private cloud services. We aim to provide flexibility, reliability and scalability for an end to end capability to enable operation in complex environments. We deliver and operate these private cloud deployments for the most critical Australian Federal Government customers, helping scale, secure and maintain the deployment whilst working closely with Google product teams to continually improve the technology.Google is an engineering company at heart. We hire people with a broad set of technical skills who are ready to take on some of technology's greatest challenges and make an impact on users around the world. At Google, engineers not only revolutionize search, they routinely work on scalability and storage solutions, large-scale applications and entirely new platforms for developers around the world. From Google Ads to Chrome, Android to YouTube, social to local, Google engineers are changing the world one technological achievement after another.

Responsibilities
  • Write product or system development code.
  • Review code developed by other developers and provide feedback to ensure best practices (e.g., style guidelines, checking code in, accuracy, testability, and efficiency).
  • Contribute to existing documentation or educational content and adapt content based on product/program updates and user feedback.
  • Triage product or system issues and debug/track/resolve by analyzing the sources of issues and the impact on hardware, network, or service operations and quality.
  • Participate in, or lead design reviews with peers and stakeholders to decide amongst available technologies.
Google is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. See also Google's EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing our Accommodations for Applicants form.

content.unEditedContent:
Join a leading national mid-tier law firm recognised for its outstanding culture, long-standing team stability, and reputation for excellence across the insurance and disputes market.

With six offices nationally, this firm offers the best of both worlds, the warmth, loyalty and collaboration of a close-knit practice combined with the capability, resources and sophisticated work of a large national firm. Many of the lawyers and partners have worked together for years, with several teams having moved firms together over the course of their careers, a rare reflection of the strength of the leadership, culture and working environment.

The Opportunity
An exciting opportunity exists for a Defendant Insurance Lawyer to join the highly regarded Casualty team in Brisbane.

Working closely with two respected Partners and supported by a well-resourced team of more than 15 lawyers, paralegals and administrative staff, you will gain exposure to a broad and interesting portfolio of liability matters acting for major insurers and corporate self-insured clients.

Your work will include:
  • Public liability
  • Product liability
  • Personal injury defence
  • Property damage disputes
  • Indemnity disputes
  • Catastrophic injury claims
Importantly, this team does not handle institutional or historical abuse matters, making it one of the few defendant insurance teams in Brisbane where lawyers can focus entirely on broader casualty and liability work.

You will be encouraged to take genuine carriage of matters with appropriate Partner support while continuing to develop your technical skills, client management capability and long-term career progression.

About You
To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:
  • 1+ years’ PAE within defendant insurance or liability
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills
  • A practical, commercial and proactive approach
  • Lawyers currently working in historical abuse matters who are looking to transition into broader casualty and liability work are strongly encouraged to apply!
Why This Firm?
This firm is genuinely known for its supportive and people-focused culture, with flexibility, wellbeing and professional development seen as priorities rather than afterthoughts.

Benefits include:
  • Flexible working arrangements, including regular WFH options and flexibility around hours
  • Modern, light-filled offices with excellent facilities
  • Strong administrative and paralegal support
  • Monthly CPD and structured professional development programs
  • Postgraduate study support and leadership development initiatives
  • Significant investment in AI and legal technology innovation
  • Private health discounts, wellbeing initiatives and wellness programs
  • Regular team breakfasts, social events and firm-funded functions
  • Inclusive parental leave and flexible workplace policies
  • This is an exceptional opportunity for a lawyer seeking high-quality insurance and casualty work within a genuinely supportive, stable and collaborative team environment.
Express Your Interest
Law Staff makes your career move discreet and straightforward. Connect with us for a no-pressure conversation by phone, video, or in our CBD office to share your goals. We will transparently match you with suitable opportunities.
To apply:

We know timing is everything. If you're intrigued but not quite ready, please still reach out. We're happy to keep you in the loop on future openings that fit your career path.

content.unEditedContent:
The opportunity for a Structural Engineer who is:
  • Passionate about working in a consultancy driven to provide quality design
  • Looking to work on a wide variety of challenging, architecturally led projects
  • Seeking a long-term opportunity where you will be rewarded – through career development to achieve your full potential and financially with a competitive salary & quarterly bonus
  • Build your name in a company where your career path could, in the long-term lead to being a future director
The Company

Medium sized, multi-disciplinary consultancy with firm position in the Australian market. Australian owned, led by hands on, approachable Directors who have a genuine passion for Engineering which emanates throughout the company culture.

This is a consultancy driven foremost by quality design and innovative engineering practices. Established over 30 years ago, my client put their success to date as a direct reflection of the great team of people in the business.
  
The Culture

My client invest in their employees, ensuring a clear career path, a quarterly profit share to all employees highlights that valuing their people is at the heart of this consultancy. This is a consultancy where you genuinely feel a part of the business and its success. High staff retention in this competitive market is testimony to the great culture.  
  
The Work

Diverse and challenging work, a wide variety of projects, architecturally acclaimed projects and ranging in size and complexity. From high end residential, schools and universities through to heritage and institutional, the projects have an architecturally. This is a rare opportunity to join the team as they grow their Sydney office.
  
The Position
  
A degree qualified Structural Design Engineer from Mid to Senior level. As you learn and develop, you will be encouraged to run your own projects through design and delivery and manage your own clients - this is a great place to work if you enjoy autonomy whilst having the support of technically accomplished and reputable Senior Engineers.
  
Key Qualities for the role:
  • Passion – for engineering and doing a quality job every time
  • Communication -  You will be confident to communicate with a  range of stakeholders, liaising with architects, clients and your peers.
  • Design Experience - You will have design experience ideally in some of the following: steel, reinforced concrete, post-tensioned concrete, masonry, and timber.
  • Software’s - knowledge of Structural design software’s, including Spacegass, RAM Concept, RAPT, Strand7 and Inducta would be beneficial. 

Get in Touch or Apply Now

This is an exciting opportunity to join a leading Australian Consultancy and play a key role in the growth of their Sydney Team.

Apply now or for a confidential chat please get in touch with Anna Roberts email:

  • Anna@cooksonandroberts.com.au
  • Mobile 0468546555

content.jobHook: Kidscape Erly Leanring Centre is looking for an amazing Centre Director
content.unEditedContent:
• Lead an established childcare service with a strong support team and large-scale operations

  • Competitive salary up to $120K + KPI incentives, birthday leave, childcare discount, relocation assistance

  • Build a thriving community, manage meaningful events, and shape high-quality early learning experiences

About Kidscape Early Learning Centre

Kidscape Early Learning Centre Two Rivers is a high-quality family owned early education provider for children aged 0–6 years, 5 rooms, 84 Place service. Our meals are prepared onsite by a qualified chef in line and families stay connected via our online parent portal. With a team of experienced educators and a strong focus on wellbeing, creativity, and early learning outcomes, Kidscape delivers a rounded start to every child’s education journey.

If you’re ready to lead a passionate and well-resourced team with the autonomy to drive impactful change, this is the role for you.

For more information, please visit our website: www.kidscapeearlylearning.com.au

About the Opportunity

Kidscape Early Learning Centre is looking for a full-time Centre Director based in Buronga, New Sout Wales. The servcie is located on the edge of the Victorian town Mildura.

You are responsible for overseeing the operational, educational, and leadership functions of the Centre whilst drawing on your creative abilities to market and stategise.

More specifically, your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Overseeing staffing levels, routines, recruitment, and professional development of educators
  • Ability to Build Occupancy
  • Managing events ranging from open days to seasonal activities with community involvement
  • Ensuring high-quality educational programming aligned with laws and regulations
  • Driving family engagement, inclusive practices, and a safe, nurturing learning environment
  • Coordinating compliance with all relevant regulations and reporting procedures
  • Showcasing the centre’s personality and achievements through hands-on social media and local marketing
  • Leading quality improvement planning and achieving operational and financial targets

To read the full position description, please click here

About You

To qualify, you will need at least a Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care and 3 years of experience (Preferred) as a Director or Supervisor/2IC in an early childhood setting.

You must also hold:

  • First Aid qualification in an Education and Care Setting
  • Anaphylaxis and Asthma Management certification
  • Valid Working with Children Check
  • Accredited Child Protection Training
  • Child Safety Training

As our ideal candidate, you will be an energetic, professional leader who can connect authentically with families, staff, and the broader community. You’ll have excellent communication skills, thrive under pressure, and be driven to build and manage a service that aligns with high educational and operational standards.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone confident, organised, warm, and who thrives in a dynamic leadership role. You will be empowered to lead and have the desire to create lasting connections with the community. You will be supported by a Management team and a very supportive Approved Provider. The service also has long standing team members.

About the Benefits

In return for your skills and passion, Kidscape Early Learning Centre is offering a competitive salary of up to $120K, along with an attractive range of benefits, including:

  • KPI-based incentives
  • Birthday leave
  • Childcare discount for immediate family
  • Above Award Rate
  • ECEC Wage Subsidy
  • Paid Professional Development
  • Paid First Aid/ CPR

If you’re looking for a leadership opportunity where you’ll be supported, valued, and given the autonomy to succeed, then this is your chance to make a real difference.

json.title: HI-FOG Service Technician

content.jobHook: Experienced Marine HI-FOG Technician wanted for offshore and industrial installations, commissioning, and service across Australia.
content.unEditedContent:
HI-FOG® Marine Installation, Commissioning & Service Technician

Location: Australia (Offshore, Marine, and Remote Land-Based Projects)
Employment Type: Full-Time
Experience Required: 3–6 Years Minimum

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly motivated, technically skilled, and safety-focused HI-FOG® Marine Installation, Commissioning & Service Technician to join our growing operations team. This role is ideal for an experienced field technician with a strong background in offshore oil and gas, marine systems, and industrial mechanical or hydraulic installations who is looking to advance their career within a specialized fire suppression and safety systems environment.

The successful candidate will be responsible for the installation, commissioning, maintenance, troubleshooting, inspection, servicing, and repair of HI-FOG® fire suppression systems across offshore platforms, marine vessels, shipyards, ports, FPSOs, drilling facilities, refineries, and land-based oil and gas installations. The position involves significant travel to offshore and remote locations throughout Australia and potentially internationally.

This role requires extensive hands-on experience utilizing mechanical, hydraulic, and electrically operated installation machinery and equipment. The technician must be capable of working independently in demanding environments while maintaining exceptional safety standards and technical accuracy.

Candidates with prior experience in hydraulic pipework installation, marine fire suppression systems, offshore mechanical systems, and confined space or working-at-height operations will be highly regarded.

The ideal applicant will possess strong troubleshooting abilities, excellent communication skills, and a professional work ethic with the ability to represent the company positively while on client sites and offshore facilities.

Key Responsibilities

Installation Duties

  • Install HI-FOG® marine fire suppression systems on offshore vessels, marine facilities, FPSOs, drilling rigs, and land-based industrial sites.

  • Interpret and work from engineering drawings, piping schematics, P&IDs, installation diagrams, and technical specifications.

  • Perform mechanical installation of pumps, valves, manifolds, nozzles, hydraulic assemblies, stainless steel tubing, pipework, and support structures.

  • Carry out hydraulic pipework fabrication, assembly, routing, mounting, and testing.

  • Utilize hydraulic, pneumatic, and electrically powered installation equipment safely and efficiently.

  • Install system control panels, instrumentation, pressure monitoring devices, and associated mechanical equipment.

  • Conduct alignment, fitment, and mounting of system components in accordance with engineering tolerances and project requirements.

  • Coordinate with shipyard personnel, offshore supervisors, project engineers, and client representatives during installation activities.

  • Perform structural mounting and bracket fabrication where required.

  • Ensure all installation work complies with company procedures, marine regulations, offshore standards, and client specifications.

  • Assist with mobilization and demobilization activities for offshore projects.

  • Operate elevated work platforms, lifting equipment, torque tools, hydraulic tooling, and pipe installation machinery.

  • Ensure all work is completed within project schedules while maintaining quality and safety standards.

Commissioning Responsibilities

  • Perform pre-commissioning inspections and system verification checks.

  • Conduct flushing, hydrostatic pressure testing, leak testing, and functional testing of high fog systems.

  • Verify correct operation of pumps, valves, sensors, alarms, control systems, and suppression components.

  • Assist with system startup and commissioning activities on offshore and marine assets.

  • Diagnose commissioning faults and rectify installation or operational deficiencies.

  • Complete commissioning reports, test documentation, and quality assurance records.

  • Interface with client representatives during FAT (Factory Acceptance Testing) and SAT (Site Acceptance Testing).

  • Validate system performance against technical specifications and regulatory requirements.

  • Support integration testing with vessel or platform alarm and shutdown systems.

  • Ensure commissioning activities are completed in accordance with safety and permit-to-work systems.

  • Provide technical feedback to engineering and project management teams regarding commissioning outcomes and field improvements.

Service & Maintenance Duties

  • Conduct routine inspections, preventative maintenance, and breakdown servicing of HI-FOG® systems.

  • Troubleshoot mechanical, hydraulic, and basic electrical faults within fire suppression systems.

  • Replace defective components including pumps, valves, actuators, sensors, and control devices.

  • Perform periodic testing and certification activities in compliance with marine and offshore standards.

  • Respond to emergency call-outs and critical equipment failures when required.

  • Prepare detailed service reports and maintenance records.

  • Identify system improvements and recommend corrective actions.

  • Maintain service tools, test equipment, and company assets in good working condition.

  • Participate in shutdowns, turnarounds, and planned maintenance campaigns.

  • Conduct onboard vessel servicing and offshore platform maintenance under varying operational conditions.

  • Maintain high standards of housekeeping in workshops, offshore facilities, and project sites.

Technical Requirements

The successful candidate must possess strong practical field experience involving:

  • Mechanical installation systems

  • Hydraulic systems and hydraulic pipework

  • Industrial piping systems

  • Offshore oil and gas equipment

  • Marine mechanical systems

  • Fire suppression systems

  • High-pressure systems

  • Industrial commissioning activities

  • Rotating equipment

  • Mechanical maintenance and servicing

  • Stainless steel tubing installation

  • Pipe bending and tube fitting

  • Use of hydraulic tooling

  • Use of electrically operated installation machinery

  • Technical fault finding

  • Industrial equipment servicing

Required Experience

Applicants must demonstrate:

  • Minimum 3 to 6 years of relevant field experience in offshore oil and gas, marine, industrial environments, data centres and land based oil and gas.

  • Previous experience working on offshore platforms, drilling rigs, marine vessels, FPSOs, shipyards, or refineries.

  • Proven installation and commissioning experience involving mechanical or hydraulic systems.

  • Experience utilizing mechanical, hydraulic, and electrically powered installation machinery and equipment.

  • Experience reading technical drawings and engineering documentation.

  • Familiarity with permit-to-work systems and isolation procedures.

  • Strong understanding of safe work practices in hazardous industrial environments.

  • Exposure to remote work conditions and offshore rosters.

  • Experience working within multidisciplinary project teams.

  • Ability to complete technical documentation and reporting accurately.

Preferred Experience

The following experience will be highly regarded:

  • HI-FOG® fire suppression systems experience

  • Marine fire protection systems

  • Deluge systems

  • Water mist systems

  • Hydraulic pipework installation

  • Stainless steel tube fitting

  • Offshore commissioning

  • Marine vessel maintenance

  • Shipyard construction projects

  • Fire suppression inspection and testing

  • Experience with marine classification societies

  • Oil and gas shutdown experience

  • Mining or heavy industrial maintenance experience

  • Confined space operations

  • Working at heights experience

  • Hazardous area work experience

  • Experience operating EWPs and lifting equipment

Essential Skills & Competencies

The successful applicant should possess the following personal and professional qualities:

Technical Skills

  • Strong mechanical aptitude

  • Ability to troubleshoot field issues independently

  • Competence using installation and commissioning equipment

  • Knowledge of hydraulic systems and components

  • Ability to safely operate power tools and machinery

  • Understanding of industrial safety systems

  • Mechanical assembly and fabrication skills

  • Basic electrical knowledge preferred

Communication Skills

  • Strong verbal communication

  • Ability to communicate professionally with clients and supervisors

  • Good written reporting skills

  • Ability to follow technical instructions accurately

Personal Attributes

  • Strong work ethic

  • Reliable and punctual

  • Safety-focused mindset

  • Professional presentation

  • Ability to work under pressure

  • Adaptable to changing project conditions

  • Self-motivated and proactive

  • Team-oriented approach

  • High attention to detail

  • Commitment to quality workmanship

Electrical Knowledge

Basic electrical knowledge is preferred but not mandatory. Candidates with experience involving:

  • Basic electrical fault finding

  • Control panel familiarity

  • Alarm systems

  • Instrumentation wiring

  • Sensor replacement

  • Electrical isolation procedures

will be viewed favorably.

However, this role is primarily mechanically and hydraulically focused, and applicants with strong mechanical backgrounds are encouraged to apply even if electrical experience is limited.

Safety Requirements

Due to the nature of offshore and industrial work environments, the successful candidate must maintain strict adherence to all workplace health and safety standards.

Candidates should possess experience or familiarity with:

  • Permit-to-work systems

  • Job safety analysis (JSA)

  • Take-5 risk assessments

  • Lockout/tagout procedures

  • Confined space entry procedures

  • Working at heights protocols

  • Hazard identification and risk mitigation

  • Offshore emergency response procedures

  • PPE compliance

  • Manual handling techniques

  • Industrial site safety requirements

Mandatory Requirements

Applicants must meet the following mandatory criteria:

  • Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident

  • Current unrestricted Australian driver’s licence

  • Ability to travel extensively throughout Australia

  • Ability to travel offshore and to remote locations

  • Physically fit for offshore and industrial work

  • Ability to pass offshore medical assessments

  • Ability to pass drug and alcohol screening

  • Ability to obtain relevant site inductions and certifications

  • Own reliable work vehicle preferred (SUV or Ute highly desirable)

Preferred Certifications & Tickets

The following certifications are highly desirable but not mandatory:

  • Working at Heights

  • Confined Space Entry

  • White Card

  • Forklift Licence

  • EWP Licence

  • Basic Fire Training

  • First Aid Certificate

  • Offshore Survival Training (BOSIET or equivalent)

  • Gas Testing Atmospheres

  • MSIC Card

Candidates willing to obtain required certifications may also be considered.

Work Environment

This position involves work in a variety of challenging industrial environments including:

  • Offshore oil and gas platforms

  • Marine vessels

  • Shipyards

  • Ports and harbors

  • Remote industrial facilities

  • Refineries

  • LNG facilities

  • Construction sites

  • Heavy industrial workshops

Work conditions may involve:

  • Extended offshore rosters

  • Shift work

  • Remote travel

  • Climbing ladders and structures

  • Confined space access

  • Exposure to harsh weather conditions

  • Physically demanding tasks

The successful candidate must be comfortable operating in these environments while maintaining a strong commitment to safety and professionalism.

Summary

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced mechanical or hydraulic technician seeking a challenging and rewarding position within the offshore oil and gas and marine industries. The role offers exposure to specialized high fog fire suppression systems across some of the most demanding industrial environments in Australia.

If you possess strong mechanical installation experience, offshore industry exposure, hydraulic pipework capability, and a commitment to safety and technical excellence, we encourage you to apply for this exciting opportunity.

Carry out hydraulic pipework fabrication, assembly, routing, mounting, and testing.
Utilize hydraulic, pneumatic, and electrically powered installation equipment safely and efficiently.
Install system control panels, instrumentation, pressure monitoring devices, and associated mechanical equipment.
Conduct alignment, fitment, and mounting of system components in accordance with engineering tolerances and project requirements.
Coordinate with shipyard personnel, offshore supervisors, project engineers, and client representatives during installation activities.
Perform structural mounting and bracket fabrication where required.
Ensure all installation work complies with company procedures, marine regulations, offshore standards, and client specifications.
Assist with mobilization and demobilization activities for offshore projects.
Operate elevated work platforms, lifting equipment, torque tools, hydraulic tooling, and pipe installation machinery.
Ensure all work is completed within project schedules while maintaining quality and safety standards.
Commissioning Responsibilities
Perform pre-commissioning inspections and system verification checks.
Conduct flushing, hydrostatic pressure testing, leak testing, and functional testing of high fog systems.
Verify correct operation of pumps, valves, sensors, alarms, control systems, and suppression components.
Assist with system startup and commissioning activities on offshore and marine assets.
Diagnose commissioning faults and rectify installation or operational deficiencies.
Complete commissioning reports, test documentation, and quality assurance records.
Interface with client representatives during FAT (Factory Acceptance Testing) and SAT (Site Acceptance Testing).
Validate system performance against technical specifications and regulatory requirements.
Support integration testing with vessel or platform alarm and shutdown systems.
Ensure commissioning activities are completed in accordance with safety and permit-to-work systems.
Provide technical feedback to engineering and project management teams regarding commissioning outcomes and field improvements.
Service & Maintenance Duties
Conduct routine inspections, preventative maintenance, and breakdown servicing of HI-FOG® systems.
Troubleshoot mechanical, hydraulic, and basic electrical faults within fire suppression systems.
Replace defective components including pumps, valves, actuators, sensors, and control devices.
Perform periodic testing and certification activities in compliance with marine and offshore standards.
Respond to emergency call-outs and critical equipment failures when required.
Prepare detailed service reports and maintenance records.
Identify system improvements and recommend corrective actions.
Maintain service tools, test equipment, and company assets in good working condition.
Participate in shutdowns, turnarounds, and planned maintenance campaigns.
Conduct onboard vessel servicing and offshore platform maintenance under varying operational conditions.
Maintain high standards of housekeeping in workshops, offshore facilities, and project sites.
Technical Requirements
The successful candidate must possess strong practical field experience involving:
Mechanical installation systems
Hydraulic systems and hydraulic pipework
Industrial piping systems
Offshore oil and gas equipment
Marine mechanical systems
Fire suppression systems
High-pressure systems
Industrial commissioning activities
Rotating equipment
Mechanical maintenance and servicing
Stainless steel tubing installation
Pipe bending and tube fitting
Use of hydraulic tooling
Use of electrically operated installation machinery
Technical fault finding
Industrial equipment servicing
Required Experience
Applicants must demonstrate:
Minimum 3 to 6 years of relevant field experience in offshore oil and gas, marine, industrial environments, data centres and land based oil and gas.
Previous experience working on offshore platforms, drilling rigs, marine vessels, FPSOs, shipyards, or refineries.
Proven installation and commissioning experience involving mechanical or hydraulic systems.
Experience utilizing mechanical, hydraulic, and electrically powered installation machinery and equipment.
Experience reading technical drawings and engineering documentation.
Familiarity with permit-to-work systems and isolation procedures.
Strong understanding of safe work practices in hazardous industrial environments.
Exposure to remote work conditions and offshore rosters.
Experience working within multidisciplinary project teams.
Ability to complete technical documentation and reporting accurately.
Preferred Experience
The following experience will be highly regarded:
HI-FOG® fire suppression systems experience
Marine fire protection systems
Deluge systems
Water mist systems
Hydraulic pipework installation
Stainless steel tube fitting
Offshore commissioning
Marine vessel maintenance
Shipyard construction projects
Fire suppression inspection and testing
Experience with marine classification societies
Oil and gas shutdown experience
Mining or heavy industrial maintenance experience
Confined space operations
Working at heights experience
Hazardous area work experience
Experience operating EWPs and lifting equipment
Essential Skills & Competencies
The successful applicant should possess the following personal and professional qualities:
Technical Skills
Strong mechanical aptitude
Ability to troubleshoot field issues independently
Competence using installation and commissioning equipment
Knowledge of hydraulic systems and components
Ability to safely operate power tools and machinery
Understanding of industrial safety systems
Mechanical assembly and fabrication skills
Basic electrical knowledge preferred
Communication Skills
Strong verbal communication
Ability to communicate professionally with clients and supervisors
Good written reporting skills
Ability to follow technical instructions accurately
Personal Attributes
Strong work ethic
Reliable and punctual
Safety-focused mindset
Professional presentation
Ability to work under pressure
Adaptable to changing project conditions
Self-motivated and proactive
Team-oriented approach
High attention to detail
Commitment to quality workmanship
Electrical Knowledge
Basic electrical knowledge is preferred but not mandatory. Candidates with experience involving:
Basic electrical fault finding
Control panel familiarity
Alarm systems
Instrumentation wiring
Sensor replacement
Electrical isolation procedures
will be viewed favorably.
However, this role is primarily mechanically and hydraulically focused, and applicants with strong mechanical backgrounds are encouraged to apply even if electrical experience is limited.
Safety Requirements
Due to the nature of offshore and industrial work environments, the successful candidate must maintain strict adherence to all workplace health and safety standards.
Candidates should possess experience or familiarity with:
Permit-to-work systems
Job safety analysis (JSA)
Take-5 risk assessments
Lockout/tagout procedures
Confined space entry procedures
Working at heights protocols
Hazard identification and risk mitigation
Offshore emergency response procedures
PPE compliance
Manual handling techniques
Industrial site safety requirements
Mandatory Requirements
Applicants must meet the following mandatory criteria:
Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident
Current unrestricted Australian driver’s licence
Ability to travel extensively throughout Australia
Ability to travel offshore and to remote locations
Physically fit for offshore and industrial work
Ability to pass offshore medical assessments
Ability to pass drug and alcohol screening
Ability to obtain relevant site inductions and certifications
Own reliable work vehicle preferred (SUV or Ute highly desirable)
Preferred Certifications & Tickets
The following certifications are highly desirable but not mandatory:
Working at Heights
Confined Space Entry
White Card
Forklift Licence
EWP Licence
Basic Fire Training
First Aid Certificate
Offshore Survival Training (BOSIET or equivalent)
Gas Testing Atmospheres
MSIC Card
Candidates willing to obtain required certifications may also be considered.
Work Environment
This position involves work in a variety of challenging industrial environments including:
Offshore oil and gas platforms
Marine vessels
Shipyards
Ports and harbors
Remote industrial facilities
Refineries
LNG facilities
Construction sites
Heavy industrial workshops
Work conditions may involve:
Extended offshore rosters
Shift work
Remote travel
Climbing ladders and structures
Confined space access
Exposure to harsh weather conditions
Physically demanding tasks
The successful candidate must be comfortable operating in these environments while maintaining a strong commitment to safety and professionalism.
Summary

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced mechanical or hydraulic technician seeking a challenging and rewarding position within the offshore oil and gas and marine industries. The role offers exposure to specialized high fog fire suppression systems across some of the most demanding industrial environments in Australia.

If you possess strong mechanical installation experience, offshore industry exposure, hydraulic pipework capability, and a commitment to safety and technical excellence, we encourage you to apply for this exciting opportunity.

bulletPoints: Access salary sacrifice to increase take home pay +super + casual loading
A passion for community life in a unique part of the world.
Access free wellbeing support via our Employee Assistance Program
content.jobHook: We are seeking reliable and motivated casual Health Ancillary Workers to provide efficient and effective support services at Cleve Hospital.
content.unEditedContent:
• Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, Cleve
  • WHD2 | Casual (up to 30 June 2027), working over a 7 day roster
  • Salary: $31.70 - $32.27 per hour + 25% casual loading + 12% Superannuation and Salary Sacrifice Benefits 

 

Join Our Support Services Team

Cleve Hospital is seeking reliable and motivated Health Ancillary Workers to join our team on a casual basis.

This role plays an important part in supporting the smooth operation of the hospital and health service by delivering high-quality catering, cleaning, laundry and housekeeping services in a safe and professional manner.

If you enjoy working in a team environment and take pride in providing excellent service, we would love to hear from you.

About the Role

As a Services Assistant, your duties may include:

  • Cleaning and housekeeping duties across the health service
  • Laundry duties including washing, folding, ironing and linen management
  • Assisting with food preparation, plating and meal delivery
  • Supporting patients with menu selections
  • Maintaining safe food handling and infection control standards
  • Receiving and storing supplies and stock
  • Supporting a clean, safe and welcoming environment for patients, residents and staff

You may also assist across multiple service areas depending on operational needs.

About You

You are a flexible and dependable team player with a strong work ethic and a commitment to customer service.

Essential Skills & Experience:

  • Ability to work effectively within a team environment
  • Good communication and interpersonal skills
  • Flexible approach to work and rostering
  • Ability to work across catering, cleaning and laundry services
  • Basic understanding of workplace safety and infection control practices
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and professionalism

Desirable:

  • Previous experience in housekeeping, catering, cleaning or laundry services
  • First Aid Certificate
  • Experience working in healthcare or aged care settings

Apply Now

If you are looking for a rewarding casual opportunity and want to make a difference in your local community, apply today.

About Us

With its ancient outback landscapes, boutique vineyards, oyster farms and Australia’s best-kept-secret surf coast, Eyre and Far North will inspire and energise you.

The Eyre and Far North Local Health Network (EFNLHN) is responsible for the planning and delivery of hospital and health services over 337,626 square kilometres, taking in the Eyre Peninsula, western part of South Australia and north to Coober Pedy.  We are one of the largest LHNs by area in Australia and communities include Ceduna, Cleve, Coober Pedy, Cowell, Cummins, Elliston, Kimba, Oodnadatta, Port Lincoln, Streaky Bay, Tumby Bay and Wudinna.

Services include acute care, medical, accident and emergency, surgery, birthing and midwifery, specialist consultancy, renal dialysis, chemotherapy, transfusions, rehabilitation, residential and community aged care, respite care, transitional care packages, Aboriginal health, mental health, allied health, community health, community nursing, palliative care, community home support packages and home modifications.

Click here to learn more about living and working in Eyre and Far North Local Health Network.

Why Join Us

  • Make a real difference and feel like an important part of the community. Being part of Eyre & Far North means you will be supported both personally and professionally, can take advantage of education and training opportunities, will have access to flexible working hours and be part of an inter-professional approach to holistic health care.
  • Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) up to $9,010 each FBT year + $2,650 for Meal Entertainment expenses each FBT year Click here more information
  • Wellbeing and counselling support: support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program
  • Relocation support: relocation reimbursement of up to $15,000 may be available to people relocating for this opportunity. More information available from SA Health Careers - Relocation support.
  • Employee recognition: supportive and collaborative work environment where your contributions are valued and recognised.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and/or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

Applicant Information

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

Check(s)

  • National Police Certificate (NPC) for employment involving unsupervised contact with vulnerable groups required for this position (E.g. aged care employment or work involving vulnerable clients)
  • Immunisation Risk for this position is - Category B (indirect contact with blood or body substances)

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

For more information about the role please refer to the role description provided below. Job Ref: 938741

Enquiries

Rachel Russell
Position: Catering & Utility Team Leader
Phone: 8629 3000
E-mail: Rachel.Russell@sa.gov.au

Application Closing Date: 30 June 2027 - 11:55PM

Refer to the SA Health Career Website - How to apply for further information.

Eligibility: Open to Everyone

json.title: General Practice Nurse

content.jobHook: Flexible work arrangement with competitive salary. Join our supportive team delivering exceptional patient care.
content.unEditedContent:
We are establishing a brand new, state-of-the-art medical centre in the heart of Gungahlin, one of the fastest-growing regions in Australia. This is an exciting opportunity to lead the nursing direction of a new general practice if you're an experienced nurse, or work within a fresh team in a mordern GP practice if you're a graduate nurse. We have several opportunities available and will be conducting interviews on a rolling basis until positions are filled.

Essential qualities:

  • A desire to build ongoing relationships with patients

  • Incredibly positive attitude

  • Kindness and compassion

  • A collaborative team member

  • Previous experience in coordinating and reviewing Chronic Disease Management plans in a GP setting

  • Passion and experience in supporting elderly patients in their health journey by undertaking Health Assessments, including home visits.

  • Able to use initiative to manage own workload and optimise bookings

  • Strong work ethic and able to commit to permanent role within the clinic. 

  • Enthusiastic  for continued learning and teaching.

  • Strong communication skills including accurate and comprehensive documentation.

  • The ability to cover annual leave and take on additional shifts as required is essential

  • Current AHPRA registration, Police Clearance, CPR certificate, SA child/vulnerable person clearance

Core skills (not a requirement):

  • Health Assessment and Care Planning

  • Wound care management

  • Immunisation (children, adults), and knowledge cold chain storage and vaccine management

  • ECG, spirometry, ear syringing, iron infusions.

  • Assisting in minor surgery clinics and women’s contraceptive procedures 

  • It is expected that you will contribute to the recall system and development of our clinical protocols, working towards ongoing accreditation, and summation of medical records

  • In addition, at busy times to help in other areas of the business such as reception/admin duties

content.jobHook: Utilise your OT skills and knowledge to complete assessment, modifications and recommendations to help people recover after injury at work
content.unEditedContent:
Pinnacle Rehab is an award-winning workplace rehab provider, with the goal of achieving quality recovery and return-to-work outcomes for individuals who have been injured at work, our dedicated consultants support these individuals to regain their confidence and independence.  

Our people are at the forefront of the business, we are committed to staff development and training. The collaborative team culture, extensive induction and onboarding into the business will support you to build a solid foundation into the industry of occ rehab. 
  • Certified ‘Great Place to Work’ and #2 Best workplaces in Healthcare and Social Assistance in Australia, Best workplaces for Women 
  • Structured induction, and individually tailored onboarding program 
  • Flexibility to organise your own calendar with appointments, office days and work-from-home 
  • Ongoing support in a collaborative and fun team environment 
The Opportunity: 
    
Driven by ongoing growth across our Same Employer Division, we are offering a unique opportunity to be part of our expanding success. As a New Graduate or experienced Occupational Therapist you will have a chance to further develop your clinical reasoning skills and play a key role in supporting effective return to work plans. 
 
You will be involved within a structured and hands-on induction, shadowing opportunities and classroom sessions in your first week, followed by ongoing remote learning modules to provide clear understanding of the workers' compensation framework. 
  
Ongoing individual support and team meetings with Team Leader, peer mentor sessions to help you develop the skills to drive and achieve the best possible outcomes for your clients.  
 
Looking after a client portfolio, your day will include:  
  • Manage a portfolio of clients with a physical injury providing return-to-work services and  
  • One off - Activities of Daily Living (ADL) assessments and making recommendations 
  • Complete initial assessments to better understand the injury, recovery timeframes and return to work goals 
  • Visiting workplace to assess environment and duties within the role, identify with employer of any suitable duties while recovering 
  • Providing support through recommendations for community assistance or additional support through the insurer 
  • Working within a multidisciplinary team to provide complex stakeholder management to support the recovery of an injured worker 
  • Document case notes as part of reporting and compliance requirements, applying your clinical judgement to support and guide your clients to a safe return to work goal 
What is on offer: 
  • Excellent remuneration on offer plus achievable bonus 
  • All travel reimbursed at $0.99 per km, including tolls and parking expenses 
  • Structured induction and onboarding with buddy system, including ongoing weekly and monthly team meetings to support your learning 
  • Professional development opportunities – internal training programs for leadership and management 
  • Latest technology with laptop and iPhone provided  
  • Regular seasonal social events throughout the year 
  • Annual Christmas party 
  • Opportunity to participate in our Emerging Leaders Program for career development opportunities 
Your Wellbeing our Heartbeat - Our employee benefits program   
  • Wellbeing Support - Employee Assistance Programs 
  • Employee Connection - Social entertainment budgets 
  • Life Balance - Unplug agreement, flexible working arrangements 
  • Paid Parental Leave - entitlements to support your growing family 
  • Learning and Development - Group supervision sessions, quarterly formal professional development and monthly bites and insights
About You     
  • General Registration with AHPRA 
  • Tertiary degree in Occupational Therapy
  • Car and valid Driver’s license 
  • Satisfactory police check or willingness to obtain prior to commencement
  • Ability to build strong stakeholder relationships 
  • Ability to work in autonomously and as part of a team 
Pinnacle Rehab is an equal opportunity employer who encourages applications from suitably qualified candidates from all cultures, ages, religions and genders. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. 
 
Next Steps 
 
Opportunities like this won’t stick around long! If this sounds like your next rewarding role, feel free to reach out directly for a chat or apply through the "Apply" button, and we’ll be in touch to discuss further. 

careers@pinnaclerehab.com.au or call Ash 0455 118 755
  
Applications close on 15th June, 2026.

content.jobHook: Due to exciting growth across the business our Psych Division is expanding we are hiring Prov Psych's and Exp Rehab Consultants across our Teams!
content.unEditedContent:
Inhouse Provisional Psychologist Program:  
 
As a Provisional Psychologist, understanding the pathway to General Registration can be overwhelming, which is why Pinnacle Rehab have carefully designed a tailored psychological internship program to support you on your registration journey, whether you are currently completing your Masters studies and looking to work in the psychological field (AWOP) or have entered into your internship year (5+1). 
 
Within the Psychological Division you will be exposed to the key learning objectives of psychological practice, board approved supervision, professional development and understanding the assessment tasks which will prepare you for the National Psychology Exam. 

About Us 

Pinnacle Rehab is an award-winning workplace rehab provider, with the goal of achieving quality recovery and return-to-work outcomes for individuals who have been injured at work, our dedicated consultants support these individuals to regain their confidence and independence.  

Our people are at the forefront of the business, we are committed to staff development and training. The collaborative team culture, extensive induction and onboarding into the business will support you to build a solid foundation into the industry of occ rehab. 
  • Certified ‘Great Place to Work’ and #2 Best workplaces in Healthcare and Social Assistance in Australia, Best workplaces for Women 
  • Structured induction, and individually tailored onboarding program 
  • Flexibility to organise your own calendar with appointments, office days and work-from-home 
  • Ongoing support in a collaborative and fun team environment 
The Opportunity: 
    
Due to growth across the business and our expanding Psych Division we currently have a new opportunity for a Master of Psychology Graduate or experienced Rehabilitation Counsellor looking for more exposure to complex psych claims to join our Team! 
 
Full induction, training, and buddy system provided to set you up for success. Including weekly and monthly team meetings targeted at developing your exposure to different psychometrics assessments and interventions. 
    
In your new role you will manage a portfolio of clients with a psychological injury, creating and monitoring rehabilitation plans which aim to gradually return your clients back to work.   
    
You will develop the skills needed to conduct motivational interviews with clients as well as influencing stakeholders to achieve the best possible outcomes for your clients.  
 
Looking after a client portfolio, your day will include:  
  • Completing initial psychological assessments which will provide a comprehensive look into an injured workers biopsychosocial barrier’s 
  • Providing a tailored intervention approach to recovery and developing appropriate return to work plans 
  • Conducting vocational assessments, rehabilitation and vocational counselling and motivational interviewing techniques 
  • Providing support through recommendations for community assistance or additional support through the insurer 
  • Working within a multi-disciplinary team to provide complex stakeholder management to support the recovery of an injured worker 
  • Document case notes as part of reporting and compliance requirements, applying your clinical judgement to support and guide your clients to a safe return to work goal.
What is on offer: 
  • Excellent remuneration on offer plus achievable bonus 
  • All travel reimbursed at $0.99 per km, including tolls and parking expenses 
  • Structured induction and on-boarding with buddy system, including ongoing weekly and monthly team meetings to support your learning 
  • Professional development opportunities – internal training programs for leadership and management 
  • Latest technology with laptop and iPhone provided  
  • Regular seasonal social events throughout the year 
  • Annual Christmas party 
  • Opportunity to participate in our Emerging Leaders Program for career development opportunities 
Your Wellbeing our Heartbeat - Our employee benefits program   
  • Wellbeing Support - Employee Assistance Programs 
  • Employee Connection - Social entertainment budgets 
  • Life Balance - Unplug agreement, flexible working arrangements 
  • Paid Parental Leave - entitlements to support your growing family 
  • Learning and Development - Group supervision sessions, quarterly formal professional development and monthly bites and insights 
About You     
  • General Registration with AHPRA or ASORC 
  • Tertiary degree as a Psychology (Hons) or Masters in Psychology 
  • Car and valid Driver’s license 
  • Police check or willingness to obtain a police check prior to commencement 
  • Ability to build strong stakeholder relationships 
  • Ability to work in autonomously and as part of a team 
Pinnacle Rehab is an equal opportunity employer who encourages applications from suitably qualified candidates from all cultures, ages, religions and genders. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. 
 
Next Steps 
 
Opportunities like this won’t stick around long! If this sounds like your next rewarding role, feel free to reach out directly for a chat or apply through the "Apply" button, and we’ll be in touch to discuss further. careers@pinnaclerehab.com.au or call Tara 0429370805 
  
Applications close on 14th June 2026.

content.jobHook: Skilled carpenter performing decking, fencing, retaining walls, pergolas and outdoor construction for landscaping projects.
content.unEditedContent:
FDSS Landscaping and Building Services Pty Ltd

Position Summary

FDSS Landscaping and Building Services Pty Ltd is seeking a skilled and motivated Carpenter to join our growing landscaping and construction team. The successful applicant will perform a wide range of carpentry and landscaping construction duties across residential and commercial projects.

The role involves constructing outdoor structures, retaining walls, decking, fencing, pergolas, formwork, and other landscape-related building works while ensuring all work is completed safely, efficiently, and to a high standard.

Key Responsibilities

  • Construct and install timber and structural landscaping features

  • Build retaining walls, decking, pergolas, fences, screens, and outdoor structures

  • Carry out formwork and concreting preparation works

  • Measure, cut, shape, and assemble timber and other materials

  • Read and interpret plans, drawings, and specifications

  • Operate carpentry tools, machinery, and equipment safely

  • Perform repairs, maintenance, and modifications to existing structures

  • Coordinate with supervisors, landscapers, and other trades onsite

  • Ensure works are completed in accordance with Australian Standards and workplace safety requirements

  • Maintain a clean and safe work environment

  • Assist with general landscaping and construction duties when required

Skills and Experience

  • Relevant trade qualification in Carpentry

  • Minimum 2 years relevant experience preferred

  • Experience in landscaping and outdoor construction works advantageous

  • Ability to read plans and specifications

  • Strong knowledge of construction methods and materials

  • Ability to work independently and within a team environment

  • Good communication and problem-solving skills

  • Strong attention to detail and workmanship

Licence and Requirements

  • White Card (Construction Induction Card)

  • Driver Licence preferred

  • Ability to perform physically demanding work

  • Commitment to workplace health and safety

Employment Details

  • Full-time position

  • Minimum 38 hours per week

  • Annual salary and conditions in accordance with applicable Australian workplace laws and industry standards

content.unEditedContent:
The Opportunity: 
    
Due to growth across the business and our expanding New Employer Division we currently have a new opportunity for a Master of Psychology Graduate, Rehabilitation Counsellor or Psychology (Hons) looking for more exposure to complex psych claims to join our Team! 
 
Full induction, training, and buddy system provided to set you up for success. Including weekly and monthly team meetings targeted at developing your exposure to different psychometrics assessments and interventions. 
    
In your new role you will manage a portfolio of clients with an injury who are unable to return to their pre-injury role to find meaningful employment with a new organisation. This involves creating and monitoring rehabilitation plans which aim to gradually return your clients back to work.  
  
You will develop the skills needed to conduct motivational interviews with clients as well as influencing stakeholders to achieve the best possible outcomes for your clients.  
 
Looking after a client portfolio, your day will include:  
  • Manage a portfolio of clients with a psychological or physical injury working towards finding new employment 
  • Complete initial & psychometric assessments which will provide a comprehensive overview of the injury and biopsychosocial barriers 
  • Conducting vocational assessments to identify skills and capabilities, rehabilitation and vocational counselling and motivational interviewing to provide ongoing support to overcome barriers 
  • Providing support through recommendations for community assistance or additional support through the insurer 
  • Working within a multi-disciplinary team to provide complex stakeholder management to support the recovery of an injured worker 
  • Document case notes as part of reporting and compliance requirements, applying your clinical judgement to support and guide your clients to a safe return to work goal 
What is on offer: 
  • Excellent remuneration on offer plus achievable bonus 
  • All travel reimbursed at $0.99 per km, including tolls and parking expenses

content.jobHook: Hiring Now! Have you recently graduated and looking to start your career with a supportive and collaborative team?
content.unEditedContent:
Fantastic opportunity to start your career as a New Graduate or make a change in your career to become a rehab consultant and facilitate outcomes within occupational rehab. 
 
This opportunity is working with an award-winning workplace rehab provider, providing exceptional support and assisting clients recover from injury, return to work and regain their confidence and independence with the support from specialised consultants. 
 
At Pinnacle Rehab we are committed to staff development and training, our people are our business. We recognise this by providing a supportive and collaborative team culture, we have an extensive induction program for all new employees and regular staff training sessions. We also coordinate regular team social events and an annual company conferences and awards night. 
 
Providing exceptional support and rehab to our clients is our passion and we are proud of our achievements.

What is on offer...
  • Excellent remuneration on offer plus achievable bonus 
  • All travel paid at $0.99 per km 
  • Structured induction and onboarding with buddy system 
  • Professional development opportunities, internally and externally 
  • Truly flexible - manage your own diary 
  • Latest technology with laptop and iPhone provided  
  • Regular seasonal social events throughout the year 
  • Annual staff company wide conference 
  • Opportunity to participate in our Emerging Leaders Program for career development opportunities  
  • Certified Great Place to Work
  • Ranked 2nd "Best Workplaces in Healthcare & Social Assistance"
The Opportunity... 
   
This is a new Psychology (Hons) Graduate or Rehabilitation Counsellor opportunity available - Full induction, training, and buddy system provided to set you up for success. 
 
As a Rehabilitation Consultant you will manage a portfolio of clients with a psychological disorder, completing vocational assessments and reports.
   
You will develop the skills needed to conduct motivational interviews with clients as well as influencing stakeholders to achieve the best possible outcomes for your clients.
 
Within your role, you will...  
  • Manage a portfolio of clients with a psychological or physical injury 
  • Complete initial assessments and identify suitable goals 
  • Identify barriers preventing clients from returning to work 
  • Organise appropriate intervention with stakeholders  
  • Providing vocational counselling  
  • Conduct Vocational Assessments 
  • Attend medical appointments with your clients  
  • Complete reports after assessments and meetings  
  • Communicate with medical professionals regarding diagnoses and treatment 
  • Facilitate a safe and timely graduated return to work  
  • Document case notes as part of reporting and compliance requirements 
Your Wellbeing our Heartbeat - Our employee benefits program...

content.unEditedContent:
Pinnacle Rehab is an award-winning workplace rehab provider, with the goal of achieving quality recovery and return-to-work outcomes for individuals who have been injured at work, our dedicated consultants support these individuals to regain their confidence and independence.  

Our people are at the forefront of the business, we are committed to staff development and training. The collaborative team culture, extensive induction and onboarding into the business will support you to build a solid foundation into the industry of occ rehab. 
  • Certified ‘Great Place to Work’ and #2 Best workplaces in Healthcare and Social Assistance in Australia, Best workplaces for Women 
  • Structured induction, and individually tailored onboarding program 
  • Flexibility to organise your own calendar with appointments, office days and work-from-home 
  • Ongoing support in a collaborative and fun team environment 
The Opportunity: 
    
Driven by ongoing growth across our Same Employer Division, we are offering a unique opportunity to be part of our expanding success. As a New Graduate or experienced Occupational Therapist you will have a chance to further develop your clinical reasoning skills and play a key role in supporting effective return to work plans. 
 
You will be involved within a structured and hands-on induction, shadowing opportunities and classroom sessions in your first week, followed by ongoing remote learning modules to provide clear understanding of the workers' compensation framework. 
  
Ongoing individual support and team meetings with Team Leader, peer mentor sessions to help you develop the skills to drive and achieve the best possible outcomes for your clients.  
 
Looking after a client portfolio, your day will include:  
  • Manage a portfolio of clients with a physical injury providing return-to-work services and  
  • One off - Activities of Daily Living (ADL) assessments and making recommendations 
  • Complete initial assessments to better understand the injury, recovery timeframes and return to work goals 
  • Visiting workplace to assess environment and duties within the role, identify with employer of any suitable duties while recovering 
  • Providing support through recommendations for community assistance or additional support through the insurer 
  • Working within a multi-disciplinary team to provide complex stakeholder management to support the recovery of an injured worker 
  • Document case notes as part of reporting and compliance requirements, applying your clinical judgement to support and guide your clients to a safe return to work goal

  • Excellent remuneration on offer plus achievable bonus 
  • All travel reimbursed at $0.99 per km, including tolls and parking expenses

content.jobHook: Join Cairns and Hinterland Hospital and Health Service!  Work in the beautiful Cassowary Coast, providing vital care in a supportive, community-focuse
content.unEditedContent:
About us:

Cairns and Hinterland Hospital and Health Service provide an extensive range of health services at more thatn 30 regional, rural and remote facilities across a geographical area of 142,900 square kilometres. The Health Service is 95 percent self-sufficient with only a small number of high- level acute services being provided in Townsville and Brisbane. 

Innisfail Hospital serves as a major rural healthcare facility, delivering emergency, perioperative, medical, surgical, maternity, and medical imaging services. It also offers a wide range of outpatient care to support the health needs of its population of over 7,000.

An exciting opportunity is available for a Registered Midwife to join the Midwifery Group Practice (MGP) in Innisfail. This role focuses on providing continuity of midwifery care across the full maternity journey, including antenatal, intrapartum, and postnatal care. The position involves working collaboratively within a caseload model, supporting women and their families through pregnancy, birth, and the early parenting period. Midwives in this role are responsible for delivering safe, high-quality, and evidence-based care, while fostering strong therapeutic relationships and promoting informed choice.

About your role:

  • Manage a defined caseload of women within the MGP model
  • Provide comprehensive antenatal, labour, birth, and postnatal care
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and community services
  • Support culturally safe care, particularly for rural and diverse populations

For more information about this role, please refer to the attached Role Description.

Vaccine Preventable Diseases (VPD) evidence as required for your employment in accordance with legislation/government policy and Directives.

What we offer:

Cairns and Hinterland Hospital and Health service offer a number of workplace benefits. Besides attractive remuneration, generous superannuation, salary packaging and career development opportunities, we value a healthy work/life balance that allows you take advantage of the sunshine, hiking tracks, swimming spots, reef and rainforest. 

Learn what it's like to work with us, in an inclusive and supportive work environment.

Discover our dynamic and culturally diverse region through community and lifestyle.

Listen to what some of our staff have to say about working in our regions.
