content.unEditedContent:
The Early Childhood Centre Cleaner is responsible for cleaning a centre according to our robust cleaning practices and procedures, to ensure we maintain our stringent hygiene, health & safety requirements.

  • Enjoy a permanent part-time position with daily start time after the centre has closed each day.
  • Be proud of the work you do to maintain a safe and hygienic Early Education Centre for the children and staff.
  • Your attention to detail to the centre’s cleanliness will have a big impact on customer satisfaction and the children’s health and wellbeing.
Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate will possess a commitment to maintaining high standards of cleanliness and hygiene, along with effective communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively within a team.

  • Essential: Current Working with Children Check & experience in cleaning or a similar role 
  • Desirable: First Aid Certificate
  • Strong decision-making and time management skills
  • Ability to critically evaluate work practises and suggest improvements

Join our Team and Grow with Us!

If you are ready to take on a challenging and rewarding role that makes a real difference in the community, apply now to join our team at Sutherland Shire Council!

  • Apply by responding to our online application questions and submitting your resume outlining why we are a great fit!
  • Applicants will be contacted as opportunities arise. Previous applicants need not apply.
  • Hourly Rate: $27.70 gross per hour plus 12% superannuation.
  • Package: $54,763 gross p.a. (salary paid pro-rata for part time) plus 12% superannuation. The Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) Worker Retention Allowance will be applied to this role in addition with Federal Government guidelines. 
  • Hours of work: Permanent part-time role. Working - Monday - Friday, 3 hours per night. Start time at 6pm.
  • To benefit your wellbeing you will have access to fitness passport, employee assistance program, annual flu shots, health and wellbeing programme and novated lease options.

Suitable candidates are subject to pre-employment screening which includes Reference Checks, Work Rights Verification, Identity and Functional/Medical History Checks, and will also include a Criminal History, Qualification and Working with Children Check. Employment is subject to clearance of all these checks.

Reach out to Jessica Chappell, Business Administration Supervisor, JChappell@ssc.nsw.gov.au for any job specific enquiries.
Jodi Johnson, Talent Acquisition Business Partner, JJohnson@ssc.nsw.gov.au can assist with any recruitment related enquiries.

Manage a...
content.unEditedContent:
Company Description

Are you ready to be a big part of something big? 

At carsales, we’re all about making buying and selling a great experience. Since 1997, we’ve been evolving with the new economy to help people choose how they move today and tomorrow.

When it comes to your career, we want to offer meaningful opportunities that empower you to make a lasting impact. But for that to happen, we strive to feel small, small enough to stay agile, learn across teams, and connect authentically with each other.

With a vision to be the global leader in online vehicle marketplaces, we’re transforming how people buy and sell across the world. We discover new ideas and bring them to life. We continue to grow, and we continue to evolve and we’re not afraid to take bold steps to get there.

This role sits within our visual media team, a customer‑facing group focused on showcasing vehicles through high‑quality imagery. The team works closely with dealership clients, combining creative expertise with strong relationship management to deliver consistent, high‑impact results while living our values of ownership, curiosity, and collaboration.

We embrace hybrid working combining the flexibility of remote work with the energy and connection of in-person collaboration. We champion flexibility and offer a range of policies and leave options to support your wellbeing.

What’s on offer

  • Recognition as one of Australia’s Best Workplaces™ by Great Place to Work®, a Family Friendly Workplace, a WORK180 endorsed employer.
  • A highly engaged, collaborative team where you’ll learn from exceptional talent.
  • 24 weeks paid parental leave for primary caregivers, four weeks for secondary caregivers, and six weeks paid gender-affirming care leave.
  • Regular hackathons, continuous learning opportunities, and wellbeing initiatives that support your mental, emotional, and physical health.

Job Description

What you will do:

  • Understand and share expertise in photography. You will photograph a variety of vehicles that are advertised by our dealership clients.
  • Manage a portfolio of clients, who you will visit regularly to capture their vehicles and assist with any enquiries.
  • Work in a variety of locations, both indoors and out.

Qualifications

What we are looking for

  • Demonstrated inclusive and interpersonal attributes that connect you to our behaviours (we change the game, we own it, we step in, we are curious, we don’t take ourselves too seriously).
  • Must haves: own SLR camera kit with an 18-70mm lens as a minimum, an iPhone (preferred), a computer and photo editing software (Adobe Photoshop is preferred), a reliable form of transport, and a valid driver’s licence.
  • A creative flair and passion for photography and videography! An interest in the automotive industry is a bonus.
  • Flexible availability from Monday to Friday.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with clients and internal stakeholders.

As part of your application please submit your resume along with 20 images of a car of your choice detailing the best angles and features of the car. Be sure to include interior and exterior photographs.  Photos will need to be submitted via PDF format. Alternatively, you can include a link to your work. Please note that there is an upload limit of 2MB.

Additional Information

A few other things we want you to know...

  • As an equal opportunity employer, carsales welcomes applications from individuals of all backgrounds, identities, abilities, and life experiences. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and supported.
  • If you have a disability or require adjustments to participate fully in the recruitment process, please let us know - we’re here to support you.
  • We understand the importance of work-life balance and offer flexible working arrangements, including part-time options. If you’d like to explore this, just ask during the process.
  • We’re also a proud Circle Back Initiative employer, which means we commit to responding to every applicant.
  • Successful candidates joining the carsales team will need to complete a National Police Record check and must have full-time Australian working rights.

So come join us - because every role plays a vital part in our journey toward something big!

Senior Product Manager - Platforms

Permanent 

This is a fully remote role, though we have a strong preference for someone who can easily pop into our Melbourne or Sydney hubs for the occasional huddle.

Not all heroes wear capes — but plenty of them use toilet paper 

Want to challenge yourself at a purpose-led scale up AND make a difference in the world? Come join the revolootion!

Funny name, serious business

We are a leading eco-friendly household essentials business and we donate 50% of our profits to help everyone gain access to clean water and a toilet. As of June 2024, we’ve contributed over $18 million AUD to this mission. Basically, we’re really good at making it easy to do good.

We operate scaling businesses in the UK, US, Australia, and Canada. Our amazing team of 250+ people is spread across the globe, all aiming to make the biggest possible impact for people and the planet. Over the next 5-10 years, we’re hoping to increase our annual donation tenfold. That’s a lot of toilet paper, and a lot of lives changed.

A bit about the role

In Digital Product, we have squads that own the front door and the subscriber relationship. This role owns the building they both operate inside. As the Senior PM you define the platform strategy, technical foundations, and data flows that determine what is possible for our entire DTC business.

You will be the architect of our internal systems, ensuring they are designed with the same rigour as our customer-facing products. You'll systematically remove the "technical ceilings" that create manual workarounds, allowing our value streams to move faster and scale further.

If you worked here this past month, here are some things you might have been involved in:
  • Shopify Markets Consolidation: Leading the charge on our highest-leverage platform initiative—scoping and sequencing the move toward a consolidated global architecture.
  • Subscription Strategy: Partnering with our engineering leads to structure the evaluation of our subscription platform to decide if we stay, customise, or migrate.
  • Designing the Internal Experience: Mapping how our internal teams interact with our tools from Shopify to our ERP, to identify and eliminate friction points.
  • AI Prototyping: Mapping our own product workflows and using AI to remove manual hurdles, creating a repeatable methodology for the rest of the business.
  • Data Pipelines: Ensuring our squads have the behavioural data and analytics instrumentation they need to make informed decisions.
  • Build vs. Buy: Evaluating new tools and vendor changes to ensure our technical ecosystem remains strategically coherent.
Let’s talk about you

You are a systems thinker who sees how platforms, integrations, and team workflows connect as one ecosystem. You aren't just managing migrations; you are designing experiences for the people who use our systems every day.

What you'll bring to the team:

  • Product Seniority: Very skilled in product management with a focus on platform strategy or complex systems-level delivery. You've led at least one complex platform migration or systems consolidation end-to-end, and you can talk clearly about what you traded off and why.
  • Technical Fluency: You are comfortable navigating Shopify APIs, vendor evaluations, and data infrastructure.
  • Commercial Logic: You can articulate the trade-offs between migration costs and the long-term capability they unlock.
  • Practical and Collective AI Innovation: You don’t just use AI tools for your own productivity; you are passionate about moving beyond individual usage to build a shared, repeatable methodology. You want to ensure we aren’t all just using AI differently in silos, but rather creating a "lead domino" effect that improves the whole business.
  • Collaborative Spirit: You enjoy pairing and mentoring others to help elevate the craft of the entire product team.
You give a crap

Do you want your work to make the world a better place? Do you want to work with other people who feel the same way? What a coincidence — us too!

Why should you work with us?

First off, as a certified B Corp™, we work to make a difference every day while maintaining the highest standards of social and environmental impact. With our most recent score of 125.5, we’re in very good company with other exceptional B Corps around the world.

We also believe that helping to make the world a better place should be rewarded accordingly – that’s why we offer competitive, market-informed salaries, meaningful support towards healthcare for our team around the world, generous paid leave, tailored learning and development opportunities, and free toilet paper (yes, you read that right).

Our engagement surveys tell us that our team is really proud (95%) to work for Who Gives A Crap and, well, we couldn’t be more proud of that.

Have you made it this far?

If you’re still reading, we think there’s a strong chance you might be our kind of person. Here’s the thing, though — research suggests that 60% of women and underrepresented folks might have already talked themselves out of applying. Even if you don’t check every box above, we want to encourage you to introduce yourself. We believe a diversity of perspectives and experiences makes a team stronger — and the stronger our team, the closer we are to delivering toilets and clean water for all.

A bit about the role

You’ll be the navigator for our financial future, turning complex data into a clear map that guides our strategic decision-making. By maintaining our financial engines while our current manager is on parental leave, you’ll ensure we stay on course to hit our goals and keep making a huge impact.

This is a 6-month Fixed Term Contract, and while we are a global business, this role is Remote Australia based. You aren't just "keeping the lights on"—you'll have a primary focus on our global Supply Chain, ensuring our logistics and inventory are as efficient as they are impactful.

If you worked here this past month, here are some things you might have been involved in:
  • Steering the Ship: Leading the mid-year re-forecasting process and setting budgets to ensure we stay on track.
  • Supply Chain Deep-Dives: Quantifying the size of supply chain initiatives to make sure we’re focusing our energy where it creates the most value.
  • Monthly Storytelling: Crafting month-end management reporting packs that explain the "why" behind the performance.
  • Risk Scouting: Proactively identifying budget variances and huddling with team leads to build mitigation plans.
  • Finance for Non-Finance: Facilitating conversations with stakeholders across the business to elevate our collective financial literacy.
  • Systems Tinkering: Leveraging our operating systems (NetSuite experience is a massive bonus here!) to improve our source of truth.
Let’s talk about you

You are a strategic thinker who sees how a ripple in one area of the business affects the entire P&L. You’re a steady hand during transitions, comfortable with ambiguity, and someone who digs into discrepancies to implement permanent fixes.

What you'll bring to the huddle:

  • Planning Prowess: Solid FP&A with a strong experience in forecasting and budgeting.
  • Supply Chain Savvy: You understand the financial flow of goods from A to B.
  • Stakeholder Diplomacy: You are a pro at managing expectations and partnering with leaders to drive commercial outcomes.
  • Tech Edge: You love a good ERP; if you’ve used NetSuite, we definitely want to hear about it.

We also believe that helping to make the world a better place should be rewarded accordingly – that’s why we offer competitive, market-informed salaries, meaningful support towards healthcare for our team around the world, generous paid leave, tailored learning and development opportunities, and free toilet paper (yes, you read that right).

Our engagement surveys tell us that our team is really proud (95%) to work for Who Gives A Crap and, well, we couldn’t be more proud of that.

Have you made it this far?

If you’re still reading, we think there’s a strong chance you might be our kind of person. Here’s the thing, though — research suggests that 60% of women and underrepresented folks might have already talked themselves out of applying. Even if you don’t check every box above, we want to encourage you to introduce yourself. We believe a diversity of perspectives and experiences makes a team stronger — and the stronger our team, the closer we are to delivering toilets and clean water for all.

content.unEditedContent:
Pinnacle Rehab is an award-winning workplace rehab provider, with the goal of achieving quality recovery and return-to-work outcomes for individuals who have been injured at work, our dedicated consultants support these individuals to regain their confidence and independence.  

Our people are at the forefront of the business, we are committed to staff development and training. The collaborative team culture, extensive induction and onboarding into the business will support you to build a solid foundation into the industry of occ rehab.  

  • Certified ‘Great Place to Work’ and #2 Best workplaces in Healthcare and Social Assistance in Australia, Best Workplace for Women  
  • Structured induction, and individually tailored onboarding program  
  • Flexibility to organise your own calendar with appointments, office days and work-from-home  
  • Ongoing support in a collaborative and fun team environment  
What is on offer:  
  • Excellent remuneration on offer plus achievable bonus  
  • All travel reimbursed at $0.99 per km, including tolls and parking expenses  
  • Structured induction and on-boarding with buddy system, including ongoing weekly and monthly team meetings to support your learning  
  • Professional development opportunities  
  • Latest technology with laptop and iPhone provided   
  • Regular seasonal social events throughout the year  
  • Annual staff company wide party  
  • Opportunity to participate in our Emerging Leaders Program for career development opportunities    
Your Wellbeing our Heartbeat - Our employee benefits program    
  • Wellbeing Support - Employee Assistance Programs 
  • Employee Connection - Social entertainment budgets 
  • Life Balance - Unplug agreement, flexible working arrangements 
  • Paid Parental Leave - Entitlements to support your growing family 
  • Learning and Development - Group supervision sessions, quarterly formal professional development and monthly bites and insights
The Opportunity 
  
Your new role as a Employment Consultant will see you managing a portfolio of clients who are in the job seeking phase of their rehabilitation. 
  
Within this role you will be travelling to different hubs within your region to have face to face meetings with your clients and attend the office for team catch-ups on a monthly basis.  
  
This role requires a people oriented professional with a positive, forward thinking caring attitude and the desire to help others secure new employment. 
  
Within your new role you will; 
  • Providing support for clients, preparing them for new employment  
  • Contacting prospective businesses to discuss staffing solutions & incentives for job trials/placements 
  • Assisting clients with resume drafting 
  • Delivering job seeking training (specific training modules) 
  • Career planning, job matching  
  • Developing local relationships with prospective employers 
  • Post placement check-in support 
  About You 
  • 1 + years’ experience in a similar role  
  • Recruitment background assisting individuals with barriers secure new employment 
  • Car and valid Driver’s license 
  • Exceptional time management and attention to detail 
  • Ability to build strong stakeholder relationships 
  • Ability to work autonomously and as part of a team 
  • Confidence over the phone and ability to strong network with potential employers 
  • Police check or willingness to obtain a police check prior to commencement 
Pinnacle Rehab is an equal opportunity employer who encourages applications from suitably qualified candidates from all cultures, ages, religions and genders. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. 
  
If you are looking for the next step in your career, apply today. 
  
Next Steps! Apply now or contact Ash via email: ashk@pinnaclerehab.com.au or phone: 0455 118 755  for more information. 

Applications close 14th June, 2026.

content.jobHook: We care about people and the world. We seek out areas of social need and policy failure and make transformational change using research, design and...
content.unEditedContent:
About Portable

We care about people and the world. We seek out areas of social need and policy failure and make transformational change using research, design and technology. Our clients are as passionate as we are — working in government agencies and socially-minded businesses, as well as Australia's most recognised tech companies. Ever wondered what it’s like to work in a high performing engineering team at a start-up? This role gives you exposure to the culture and practices but with a mature and supported team.There are currently 65+ of us working as technology consultants, researchers, strategists, designers and producers towards our mission from our head office in Collingwood, and remotely from co-working spaces and homes across Australia.

Technology consultants with a difference

This role sits within our embedded consulting practice, which is called “Midnyte”. The team is a closely knit group of technology experts that work directly inside our client organisations to provide technology leadership, technical uplift and problem solving for periods between three months to over a year in some cases. Our clients are typically well known technology companies or mature start-ups and our team is highly regarded in the industry - we just won AWS partner of the year because of our unique approach. The work is genuinely complex: large-scale cloud infrastructure, high-availability systems, and real engineering problems that matter. You'll be employed by Portable, connected to our broader team and culture, and embedded with a client where you'll do some of the best technical work of your career.

Then there's you

A highly experienced technologist with deep expertise and the judgment that comes from years of solving hard infrastructure problems across different industries and environments. You may have designed global-scale networks and landing zones, built CI/CD pipelines that actually hold up under pressure, and guided clients through complex cloud migrations without losing sight of security, cost, or reliability. 

You're past the point of needing to prove yourself technically. What drives you now is doing the work well — architecting things properly, sharing what you know, and leaving systems (and teams) in better shape than you found them. However, fundamentally you’re a problem solver who can step into spaces and add value. 

We are looking for someone who:
  • Has deep, hands-on AWS expertise — ideally holding AWS Professional or Specialist certifications
  • Has designed and implemented cloud landing zones, multi-account architectures, and global-scale infrastructure
  • Is highly proficient with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, AWS CDK, or similar) and treats it as standard practice, not a nice-to-have
  • Has built and maintained CI/CD pipelines for complex, production-grade systems
  • Has strong Linux and Windows systems knowledge
  • Understands cloud economics at a practical level
  • Brings experience with database performance, scalability assessment, and working across SQL and cloud-native data patterns
  • Has worked in regulated or security-conscious environments and applies secure-by-default thinking
  • Can work closely with client engineering teams — communicating clearly, building trust quickly, and operating with a high degree of autonomy
  • Is a Principal/engineering manager-level  practitioner: technically excellent, adaptable across stacks, and comfortable working without a people management brief
  • Brings curiosity and generosity — you share knowledge, engage seriously with problems, and make the teams around you better

Please note! We are also interested in hearing from people who are interested in embedded consultant roles, but also have a background in related areas like observability, site reliability engineering and complex software development. 

An example of what a week might look like:
  • Working embedded in a client's engineering team, leading the design and implementation of a new AWS landing zone or infrastructure migration
  • Conducting a performance and scalability assessment — analysing execution plans, identifying bottlenecks, and delivering clear, evidence-based recommendations
  • Pairing with a client or Portable developer on a tricky infrastructure problem and helping them see a cleaner path through it
  • Contributing to an internal Portable Deep Dive session on a cloud or DevOps topic you've been working with
  • Collaborating with a producer and client stakeholders to scope upcoming work, shape architecture decisions, and keep delivery on track
How we remunerate and support our team

The salary range for this role is $138,000–$200,000 plus superannuation.

Here's what else you can look forward to:

  • Meaningful work: Clients who are building things that matter, and problems worth solving properly
  • Flexible work arrangements: Hybrid and remote options, flexible hours, and personalised start/finish times. You can expect to be in either Portable’s local office or the client you are embedded with 3-4 days a week. 
  • Enhanced leave: Bonus annual leave based on tenure, purchasable additional leave, paid volunteering leave, and paid mental health days with no explanation required
  • Growth and development: $2,000 annual professional development allowance plus two working days, structured career pathways, twice-yearly salary reviews, and access to our Emerging Leaders program
  • Wellbeing support: Up to 4 counselling sessions per year through our EAP with The Mindroom
  • Financial incentives: Profit-sharing bonus, employee share plan options, and salary sacrificing
  • Family-friendly policies: Enhanced parental leave and flexible arrangements around family commitments
How to apply

We are committed to building a diverse and equal team. People from groups which are typically underrepresented in technology leadership are strongly encouraged to apply.

Please send us:

  • Your resume
  • A short cover letter (max. 1 page) answering:
    • What's attracted you to this role and why do you think it would be a good fit for you?
    • Tell us about a time you navigated a technically complex or ambiguous environment and delivered a strong outcome — what was your approach and what did you learn?
    • What does a commercial mindset mean to you?
sections: About Portable

We care about people and the world. We seek out areas of social need and policy failure and make transformational change using research, design and technology. Our clients are as passionate as we are — working in government agencies and socially-minded businesses, as well as Australia's most recognised tech companies. Ever wondered what it’s like to work in a high performing engineering team at a start-up? This role gives you exposure to the culture and practices but with a mature and supported team.There are currently 65+ of us working as technology consultants, researchers, strategists, designers and producers towards our mission from our head office in Collingwood, and remotely from co-working spaces and homes across Australia.
Technology consultants with a difference

This role sits within our embedded consulting practice, which is called “Midnyte”. The team is a closely knit group of technology experts that work directly inside our client organisations to provide technology leadership, technical uplift and problem solving for periods between three months to over a year in some cases. Our clients are typically well known technology companies or mature start-ups and our team is highly regarded in the industry - we just won AWS partner of the year because of our unique approach. The work is genuinely complex: large-scale cloud infrastructure, high-availability systems, and real engineering problems that matter. You'll be employed by Portable, connected to our broader team and culture, and embedded with a client where you'll do some of the best technical work of your career.
Then there's you

A highly experienced technologist with deep expertise and the judgment that comes from years of solving hard infrastructure problems across different industries and environments. You may have designed global-scale networks and landing zones, built CI/CD pipelines that actually hold up under pressure, and guided clients through complex cloud migrations without losing sight of security, cost, or reliability.

You're past the point of needing to prove yourself technically. What drives you now is doing the work well — architecting things properly, sharing what you know, and leaving systems (and teams) in better shape than you found them. However, fundamentally you’re a problem solver who can step into spaces and add value.
We are looking for someone who:
Has deep, hands-on AWS expertise — ideally holding AWS Professional or Specialist certifications
Has designed and implemented cloud landing zones, multi-account architectures, and global-scale infrastructure
Is highly proficient with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, AWS CDK, or similar) and treats it as standard practice, not a nice-to-have
Has built and maintained CI/CD pipelines for complex, production-grade systems
Has strong Linux and Windows systems knowledge
Understands cloud economics at a practical level
Brings experience with database performance, scalability assessment, and working across SQL and cloud-native data patterns
Has worked in regulated or security-conscious environments and applies secure-by-default thinking
Can work closely with client engineering teams — communicating clearly, building trust quickly, and operating with a high degree of autonomy
Is a Principal/engineering manager-level  practitioner: technically excellent, adaptable across stacks, and comfortable working without a people management brief
Brings curiosity and generosity — you share knowledge, engage seriously with problems, and make the teams around you better
Please note!

We are also interested in hearing from people who are interested in embedded consultant roles, but also have a background in related areas like observability, site reliability engineering and complex software development.
An example of what a week might look like:
Working embedded in a client's engineering team, leading the design and implementation of a new AWS landing zone or infrastructure migration
Conducting a performance and scalability assessment — analysing execution plans, identifying bottlenecks, and delivering clear, evidence-based recommendations
Pairing with a client or Portable developer on a tricky infrastructure problem and helping them see a cleaner path through it
Contributing to an internal Portable Deep Dive session on a cloud or DevOps topic you've been working with
Collaborating with a producer and client stakeholders to scope upcoming work, shape architecture decisions, and keep delivery on track
How we remunerate and support our team
The salary range for this role is $138,000–$200,000 plus superannuation.
Here's what else you can look forward to:
Meaningful work:
Clients who are building things that matter, and problems worth solving properly
Flexible work arrangements:
Hybrid and remote options, flexible hours, and personalised start/finish times. You can expect to be in either Portable’s local office or the client you are embedded with 3-4 days a week.
Enhanced leave:
Bonus annual leave based on tenure, purchasable additional leave, paid volunteering leave, and paid mental health days with no explanation required
Growth and development:
$2,000 annual professional development allowance plus two working days, structured career pathways, twice-yearly salary reviews, and access to our Emerging Leaders program
Wellbeing support:
Up to 4 counselling sessions per year through our EAP with The Mindroom
Financial incentives:
Profit-sharing bonus, employee share plan options, and salary sacrificing
Family-friendly policies:
Enhanced parental leave and flexible arrangements around family commitments
How to apply
We are committed to building a diverse and equal team. People from groups which are typically underrepresented in technology leadership are strongly encouraged to apply.
Please send us:
Your resume
A short cover letter (max. 1 page) answering:
What's attracted you to this role and why do you think it would be a good fit for you?
Tell us about a time you navigated a technically complex or ambiguous environment and delivered a strong outcome — what was your approach and what did you learn?
What does a commercial mindset mean to you?

content.jobHook: In this role, locally known as Associate Principal, you will lead the delivery of Cleveland District State High School’s strategic plan, driving...
content.unEditedContent:
Two temporary Head of Campus opportunities are available while the Executive Principal undertakes coaching during Term 3 and possibly part of Term 4.

In this role, locally known as Associate Principal, you will lead the delivery of Cleveland District State High School’s strategic plan, driving improvement in teaching, learning and student outcomes.

These temporary full-time roles are for Term 3, from 13 July to 18 September 2026, unless otherwise determined.

About the Department

Working for the Queensland Department of Education means joining an organisation that values its people and promotes leadership and innovation. Be part of an environment that respects professionalism and diversity, offers training and development opportunities and embraces flexible careers and work-life balance. Find out more about working with us.

About the School

Cleveland District State High School is a high performing secondary school located in the heart of the Redlands which is a short drive East of Brisbane. It is a school with a strong academic focus and a clear continuous improvement agenda. All staff are accountable for ensuring optimal achievement for every student.

About the Role

The Head of Campus position is locally known as Associate Principal.  This vital leadership role delivers the vision of the department and the strategic outcomes of the school.

As Associate Principal, you will improve the educational achievement, belonging and engagement of students.

You will also develop the quality of teaching and learning and nurture positive relationships between students, teachers and stakeholders.

Please refer to the attached role description for any mandatory requirements for this position.

Interested? To Apply

  • Attach a brief resume including contact details for 2 referees (referees should understand your relevant work history).
  • Attach a written response (2-page maximum) addressing Key Capabilities as per Role Description 'How you will be assessed' section. 
  • Attach a copy of your mandatory requirements outlined in the Role Description.

We welcome all applicants to share any support needed to ensure our recruitment process is inclusive.

Applications remain current for 12 months from the closing date and may be considered for appointment to identical or similar vacancies within the Department.

Applications from recruitment agencies will not be accepted.

content.unEditedContent:
At Zeus Street Greek, we believe in bold flavours, legendary hospitality, and the power of food to bring people together. As a Restaurant Manager, you will take full ownership of your restaurant and lead the charge in delivering exceptional food, service and team culture.


You will inspire and develop your leadership team, drive performance through people, and manage your restaurant’s P&L. This is a hands-on leadership role where you will maintain the highest standards of quality and safety, while living and breathing the Zeus Street Greek values and lightning bolt energy.


What’s in it for you?
So much! Here’s what you can look forward to:

  • Competitive salary + bonus opportunities
  • Flexible rosters and employment stability – let’s talk about what work-life balance means to you
  • Career progression – level up to Regional Restaurant Manager and Area Manager and beyond
  • Comprehensive training and ongoing support to set you up for success
  • Heavily discounted Zeus Street Greek meals
  • Free ZSG uniforms and exclusive merchandise
  • Cultural celebrations and brand moments
  • Opportunities to grow into head office

About You
We value diverse experience, but ideally you’ll bring:

  • Demonstrated leadership experience in a fast-paced, high-energy environment
  • Strong financial and commercial acumen, with the ability to identify sales and P&L opportunities and partner with your team on solutions
  • A proven track record of achieving and driving KPIs
  • Outstanding customer service capability
  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills

If you’re ready to take ownership of a restaurant and lead with lightning bolt energy, we’d love to hear from you.

content.jobHook: Sutherland Shire Council is seeking ISS Support Workers to join our Early Education & Child Protection Team. In this role, you’ll help children...
content.unEditedContent:
Sutherland Shire Council is seeking ISS Support Workers to join our Early Education & Child Protection Team. In this role, you’ll help children with higher support needs fully participate in early childhood education by providing extra care and encouragement in a safe, nurturing environment.

You’ll work alongside educators to support play-based learning activities tailored to each child’s interests and abilities. Your role is vital in creating an inclusive space where all children can learn, grow and build positive relationships.

What You’ll Do:
  • Assist children with additional support needs during daily routines such as meals, rest, and hygiene. 
  • Support children’s participation in play and learning activities, adapting to their individual needs. 
  • Encourage positive interactions, respect, and fairness among all children. 
  • Work closely with families and educators to support each child’s development. 
What You'll Bring:
  • NSW Working with Children Check.
  • Commitment to undertake First Aid and Child Protection training. 
  • Experience working in early childhood education and care settings. 
  • Experience supporting children with additional or high support needs. 

Join our Team and Grow with Us!

If you are ready to take on a challenging and rewarding role that makes a real difference in the community, apply now to join our team at Sutherland Shire Council!

  • Apply by responding to our online application questions and submitting your resume outlining why we are a great fit!
  • Applicants will be contacted as opportunities arise. Previous applicants need not apply.
  • Hourly Rate: $29.62 gross per hour plus 12% superannuation. 
  • Package: $58,545 gross p.a. (salary paid pro-rate for part time roles) plus 12% superannuation. The Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) Worker Retention Allowance will be applied to these roles in addition with Federal Government guidelines. 
  • Hours of work: Temporary Part Time - multiple roles available across our 11 centres. Applicants must be able to work a range of shifts from 6am - 7pm to support the operational requirements of the centres.  
  • To benefit your wellbeing you will have access to fitness passport, employee assistance program, annual flu shots, health and wellbeing programme and novated lease options.

Suitable candidates are subject to pre-employment screening which includes Reference Checks, Work Rights Verification, Identity and Functional/Medical History Checks, and will also include a Criminal History, Qualification and Working with Children Check. Employment is subject to clearance of all these checks.

Reach out to Jessica Chappell, Business Administration Supervisor JChappell@ssc.nsw.gov.au for any job specific enquiries.
Jodi Johnson, Talent Acquisition Business Partner, JJohnson@ssc.nsw.gov.au can assist with any recruitment related enquiries.

Click on the link to check out the Position Description

content.jobHook: Livingstone Shire Council is seeking a passionate and experienced professional to lead the delivery of sustainability and natural resource...
content.unEditedContent:
The Role

Livingstone Shire Council is seeking a passionate and experienced professional to lead the delivery of sustainability and natural resource management outcomes across the region.

This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in shaping a sustainable future for our community by driving strategic initiatives, leading environmental programs, and providing expert advice within a dynamic local government environment. You will work across Council to ensure strong alignment with legislative requirements, corporate priorities, and long-term environmental outcomes

What You Will Do

  1. Lead and coordinate sustainability functions across Council to ensure compliance with legislation and alignment with strategic priorities.
  2. Deliver sustainability programs and projects, including initiatives such as Reef Guardian and climate resilience programs.
  3. Provide expert advice on sustainability matters, including development proposals, planning schemes, and environmental management.
  4. Develop and implement sustainability strategies, operational plans, and continuous improvement initiatives, including carbon reduction opportunities.
  5. Engage with stakeholders and the community to promote sustainability awareness and behavioural change.
  6. Support and build a high-performing team, ensuring effective project delivery and organisational outcomes.

What You Will Bring

You are a motivated and knowledgeable sustainability professional with strong technical and stakeholder engagement capability.

We are looking for someone who has:

  • Strong expertise in sustainability, environmental management, legislation, and climate change (including carbon accounting).
  • Experience developing and delivering sustainability strategies, policies, and programs within a planning or local government context.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to engage stakeholders and deliver clear, professional advice.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical skills, including experience with relevant systems (e.g. GIS, corporate systems, MS Office).
  • Demonstrated leadership capability, including building and supporting high-performing teams.

Mandatory requirements:

  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in environmental science, sustainability, or a related discipline (or equivalent experience).
  • Current Queensland “C” Class Driver Licence.

content.jobHook: Help shape what’s next in data, AI, and advisory within Altis Consulting. We’re looking for a Principal Consultant to join the team and play a key...
content.unEditedContent:
Help shape what’s next in data, AI, and advisory within Altis Consulting.   We’re looking for a Principal Consultant to join the team and play a key role in building our Victorian success.  

This is more than a delivery role. We’re looking for someone who can bring strong technical capability, commercial thinking, and a modern advisory mindset to help clients solve real business problems with data. 

Join a growing team that values curiosity, collaboration, and practical innovation. You will be someone who is excited by evolving technology, comfortable navigating ambiguity, and motivated by creating solutions that are not only clever, but sustainable, governed, and valuable in the real world. 

In this role 

You will work closely with clients to understand their challenges, shape solutions, and deliver high-impact outcomes across modern data platforms and AI-enabled environments. 

Your role will include: 

  • Lead the design and delivery of modern data and analytics solutions 
  • Partner with clients to translate business problems into practical, scalable strategies 
  • Provide trusted advisory support, recommendations, and technical leadership 
  • Work across platforms such as Snowflake, Databricks, and Microsoft Fabric 
  • Support the development of governed, sustainable, and future-ready data solutions 
  • Mentor other team members, share expertise, and help foster a high-performing, collaborative team environment  
  • Engage confidently with stakeholders across both technical and non-technical backgrounds  

What you will bring 

We’re looking for someone who combines strong foundational skills with a modern mindset. 

Lets talk experience 

  • You will bring experience in consulting, advisory, or client-facing delivery roles within data and analytics (No specific industry) 
  • Strong capability across modern data platforms, particularly Snowflake, Databricks, and/or Fabric 
  • Apply strong data engineering and data modelling capability to build scalable, sustainable, and well-governed solutions that turn complex data into practical business value 
  • Exposure to AI- solutions, or a clear understanding of how AI can be applied responsibly in enterprise environments, is a bonus.  
  • The ability to solve real-world business challenges, not just build technical outputs 
  • Confidence in making recommendations, influencing stakeholders, and leading conversations with clients 
  • A strong understanding of how to deliver solutions that are scalable, practical, and well governed

Added Bonus 

  • Previous exposure to modern AI-assisted delivery tools (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, Snowflake Cortex Code or similar) and the judgment to use them responsibly to accelerate delivery while maintaining quality. 

The mindset that matters 

Technical capability is important, but it’s only part of the picture. 

We’re especially interested in people who demonstrate: 

  • A growth mindset 
  • Curiosity and a genuine interest in new and emerging technologies 
  • Resilience and adaptability in changing environments 
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills 
  • The confidence to challenge thinking, offer insight, and add value beyond delivery 
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach 

What’s in it for you 

  • Meaningful work within data, AI, and business advisory 
  • The chance to help shape client outcomes, team culture, and market presence 
  • A collaborative environment that values innovation, learning, and impact 
  • The opportunity to work with modern platforms and forward-thinking clients 

Your Next Chapter Starts Here

At Altis, we offer more than a job. We offer a career opportunity. You’ll have the tools, resources, and support to build your career, take on interesting projects, and work on challenging problems that make a real impact.

We are high performers who support each other to succeed. Our culture encourages bringing your whole self to work, embracing continuous learning, and fostering growth through diverse, complex projects. You’ll be part of a collaborative, inclusive environment where curiosity is valued, ideas are encouraged, and your contribution matters.


How We Invest in You:

  • A career pathway with ongoing learning and development
  • Exposure to varied and challenging projects across industries
  • A supportive, inclusive culture that values diversity and individuality
  • Hybrid working model
  • Competitive salary
  • A holistic health and wellness program that supports you and your family
  • Paid parental leave
  • Reward and recognition program

Let’s Start the Conversation

Apply now! We’d love to hear from you.

At Altis, Seeing Your Career Differently means creating an environment where respect, fairness, growth, and well-being are at the core of how we work. We welcome and celebrate people from all backgrounds, experiences, identities, abilities, and thinking styles, and we are committed to providing equal opportunities for all qualified applicants.

If you require adjustments or support during the application process, please let us know. We are here to ensure you can bring your best self to every stage.

At Altis, Seeing Your Career Differently means creating an environment where respect, fairness, growth, and well-being are at the core of how we work. We welcome and celebrate people from all backgrounds, experiences, identities, abilities, and thinking styles, and we are committed to providing equal opportunities for all qualified applicants.
If you require adjustments or support during the application process, please let us know. We are here to ensure you can bring your best self to every stage.

content.jobHook: As a Release Manager TPM, it is your mission to work closely with engineering, product, and marketing teams to build a sustainable culture of...
content.unEditedContent:
Company Description

Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, hello, hiya, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

Where and how you can work

Our flagship campus is in Sydney. We also have a campus in Melbourne and co-working spaces in Brisbane, Perth, Auckland and Adelaide. But you have choice in where and how you work. That means if you want to do your thing in the office (if you're near one), at home or a bit of both, it's up to you.

Job Description

What you’d be doing in this role

As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

As a Release Manager TPM, you will orchestrate the smooth execution of our major releases — ensuring that Canva Create and Droptober are delivered seamlessly, with high-quality features reaching our users without disruption. You will oversee the entire release lifecycle, from deployment through to go-live day and post-release activities.

At the moment, this role is focused on

  • Governance of the end-to-end release process, including the activities, steps, and procedures involved in preparing, executing, and finalizing major releases such as Canva Create and Droptober.

  • Develop and maintain a comprehensive release calendar, outlining key milestones, activities and procedures.

  • Spearhead the evolution of release practices — designing and implementing scalable release processes and tooling that support Canva’s growth and increasing feature complexity. 

  • Create and refine documentation to guide teams through the release process, ensuring clarity and consistency.

  • Coordinate and synchronize feature launches across multiple teams (product, engineering, marketing, and user feedback) to ensure smooth and successful major events.

  • Facilitate effective communication and collaboration between departments to address and resolve issues promptly.

  • Monitor the performance of each release and ensure alignment with Canva’s key strategies.

  • Drive continuous improvement of release processes and tooling based on retrospectives and feedback from stakeholders.

  • Manage the dynamic nature of coordinating major releases, adapting to varying feature scopes and evolving requirements.

  • Ensure a unified release process across teams, groups, and strategic goals.

  • Coordinate with engineering teams to ensure adherence to release timelines and instructions.

  • Align with the marketing team on release schedules and go-live activities, including B2B, brand, and PMM initiatives.

  • Navigate and manage scope changes to align with shifting business strategies.

You're probably a match if

  • A minimum of 5 years TPM or release management experience at an established and complex organization

  • Domain experience working with release engineering, deployment pipelines, or platform infrastructure

  • Deep understanding of release management processes, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment strategies

  • Experience coordinating large-scale, cross-functional releases involving product, engineering, and marketing teams

  • Comfortable with ambiguity in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities

  • A natural communicator who leads through influence, not authority — able to coordinate across diverse, senior stakeholders without direct authority

  • A love for navigating complexity and tackling ambiguous problems 

  • Process-oriented but flexible in approach

  • Experience building scalable and repeatable processes from the ground up

  • Dedicated to personal growth and improving in your craft as a TPM 

  • Leadership capability to ensure clarity, alignment and accountability to achieve our Crazy Big Goals

  • Ability to think strategically but also able to make crazy big goals happen. This role will be very hands-on!

About the Release Team

Major releases at Canva are executed by various teams and stakeholders across the organization, but to ensure a successful release, this is managed by a centralized release process. The core release coordinating team is mainly supported by the Reliability Platform and Developer Platform groups in the Infra supergroup. The release squad executes Canva-wide principles such as code freeze and experiment freeze, improves tooling such as feature control and deployment pipelines, and evolves incident management and capacity planning for major releases.

This role partners closely with teams across Platform, Product, and Marketing supergroups, ensuring all aspects of the release are planned and coordinated across complex timelines and dependencies.

About Technical Program Managers

At Canva, we’re all constantly striving towards our Crazy Big Goals! Since growing to a worldwide team of over 5,000 we need to work effectively together and improve our delivery ability as we scale, which is where our Technical Program Managers come in. 

As a Release Manager TPM, it is your mission to work closely with engineering, product, and marketing teams to build a sustainable culture of positive urgency in release delivery. You will lead complex, cross-organizational programs and be equally comfortable working with leadership to set strategic goals and clarify priorities, as you are coordinating release timelines, escalating issues, and managing dependencies across the organization. This role requires strong interpersonal skills, the ability to lead with context, and experience managing diverse, senior-level stakeholders. There is a clear growth path for this role to become a B4 — Staff Technical Program Manager.

Additional Information

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too

  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers

  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more

  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

Other stuff to know

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture. When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process.

We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva so even if you don’t feel like your skills quite match what’s listed above - we still want to hear from you!

Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

content.unEditedContent:
Merrimac State High School is one of the Gold Coast’s premium state‑run secondary schools (Years 7-12), known for its motto “Pride in Excellence” and a strong emphasis on respect, responsibility, and reliability in its internationally recognized curriculum. Merrimac State High School is located in Mermaid Waters on a 10.4-hectare campus in the heart of the Gold Coast, close to beaches, shops, and public transport. The area combines natural parks with urban convenience.

We're recruiting an English teacher for Years 10-12 to join our close-knit team. Whether you're just starting out or looking for a rewarding regional move, this is your chance to be part of something meaningful. 

What We Offer

  • Modern facilities and quality resources
  • Real career development opportunities

What You'll Need

  • Relevant teaching qualification
  • Full or provisional QCT registration
  • Australian working rights or valid visa
  • Pre-service and graduate teachers are encouraged to apply (include practicum reports, mentor statements & unofficial transcript)

How to apply

  • Click the Green 'Apply online' button below
  • Enter your personal details
  • Attach your resume including two professional referees

🔗 Explore the school: Visit the school website here https://merrimacshs.eq.edu.au/

All applicants are encouraged to apply to the Department of Education Teacher Application Portal to be considered for current and future roles.

Existing permanent teachers are encouraged to apply for the teacher transfer process, noting that relocation entitlements may not apply.

Applications from recruitment agencies will not be accepted.

json.title: Analyst II Supply Chain and Logistics

content.jobHook: In this position, you will oversee end‑to‑end logistics planning and execution for road and rail transport, ensuring efficient grain accumulation...
content.unEditedContent:
•  Long term career opportunity in a leading agribusiness
  • Key logistics role
  • Work from our brand‑new Eastwood office, just minutes from the CBD

About the role

Bunge is seeking an Analyst II – Supply Chain and Logistics to join our team in a critical role supporting the planning and execution of transport movements across South Australia.

In this position, you will oversee end‑to‑end logistics planning and execution for road and rail transport, ensuring efficient grain accumulation to port terminals. You’ll play a key role in aligning supply chain operations with vessel schedules, driving continuous improvements, and maximising supply chain value and financial returns.

This is a fast‑paced and highly collaborative role requiring strong analytical capability, attention to detail, and the ability to coordinate complex logistics activities while maintaining high levels of service and compliance.

Duties

  • Develop and manage logistics plans for bulk vessel accumulation, container programs and pre‑accumulation activities
  • Coordinate road and rail transport movements for port operations, vessel discharge and intrasite transfers
  • Monitor execution against plans, identify variances and implement corrective actions
  • Liaise with internal teams, service providers and customers to ensure alignment with shipping schedules and strategies
  • Supervise and support Freight Coordinators to ensure effective resolution of supply chain issues
  • Review site assembly and transport plans for export cargoes and third‑party operations
  • Ensure accurate system data, inventory integrity and timely completion of transactions
  • Maintain strong customer relationships to optimise supply chain outcomes and commercial returns
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives to enhance efficiency and identify cost savings opportunities
  • Ensure compliance with Chain of Responsibility, safety and legislative requirements
  • Assist with planning activities across other South Australian port terminals as required

About you

  • Demonstrated experience in logistics, supply chain planning or transport coordination (3–5 years preferred)
  • Solid understanding of road and/or rail transport operations and compliance requirements
  • Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills with the ability to make practical, data‑driven decisions
  • Ability to manage multiple stakeholders, including carriers, service providers and internal teams
  • Well‑developed communication and negotiation skills
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to manage competing priorities
  • Understanding of pricing principles and financial impacts within supply chain operations
  • Relevant qualification in Logistics and Transport or equivalent (desirable)
  • A team player who thrives in a collaborative environment

About us

Bunge connects farmers to consumers to deliver essential food, feed and fuel to the world.

Through our dynamic supply chain, we can move commodities efficiently from where there is surplus to where they are needed. In Australia, we operate around 60 storage and handling sites and seven port terminals across southern Western Australia, South Australia and western Victoria, two import sites in Victoria and New South Wales, and are one of the largest buyers and exporters of agricultural commodities including cereals, oilseeds, pulses and cotton.

By joining Bunge, you will enjoy a varied and interesting career and make a difference to local farmers and the communities we operate in.

In mid-2025, Bunge and Viterra combined, creating a premier agribusiness solutions with around 34,000 employees globally. 

Benefits

When you join Bunge, you’re not just starting a new job – you’re building a rewarding career with a global leader. We offer a supportive work culture that values respect, teamwork, and development. As part of the Bunge family, you’ll also enjoy a range of benefits, including:

  • Training and development opportunities, including access to LinkedIn Learning, Bunge workshops, and mentorship programs to support continuous learning and career growth
  • Employee assistance program – access to confidential and free support
  • Corporate health insurance funds, financial services, and computer offers
  • Novated leasing
  • Birthday leave
  • Years of service recognition
  • Rigorous safety practices
  • Primary and secondary paid parental leave
  • A supportive environment which prioritises respect and teamwork.

Ready to get started? Join Bunge and take your career to the next level in a role that’s both exciting and rewarding.

How to apply

To apply for the position please click on ‘Apply’ at the bottom of the page or for further information please contact, Manager Supply Chain and Logistics, Jordan Harrison on +61 8 8304 5153.

Applications close 11:45pm Sunday 7 June 2026.

Please note we are not accepting recruitment agency applications at this time.

We will be conducting interviews as we receive applications. Please note that we reserve the right to close the advertisement early should a suitable candidate be identified prior to the advertised closing date.

- Bunge Collection Notice.pdf

content.jobHook: Abt are seeking to engage a Team Leader who will be fully accountable for the leadership, performance and delivery of the Australia Pacific Leaders...
content.unEditedContent:
• Location: Canberra, Australia
  • Commencement: June 2026 
  • Duration of contract: 12 months to 30 June 2027
  • Open to those with full work rights for Australia

About the Program

The Australia Pacific Leaders Program (APLP) is an Australian Government initiative that seeks to empower current and emerging Pacific leaders to deliver outcomes in their communities, strengthen their skills and build relationships with Australian agencies and institutions. 

Activities include study tours, high-level visits, professional development and support for locally led projects, including assistance to deliver community-level initiatives.

APLP aims to:

  • empower leaders to deliver practical outcomes in their communities

  • build stronger, long-term relationships between Pacific leaders and Australia

  • strengthen leadership capability across the Pacific. 

About the Program Support Unit (PSU)

The Program Support Unit (PSU) supports DFAT to deliver the program. Abt Global is contracted to deliver the PSU. 

The PSU provides the practical support needed to deliver activities including planning, logistics, procurement and coordination. This includes supporting DFAT-led study tours and visits to Australia, coordinating training and events and supporting the delivery of grants and other program activities.

The PSU works closely with DFAT in Canberra and Posts across the Pacific to ensure activities are delivered to a high standard.

About the Opportunity

Abt are seeking to engage a Team Leader who will be fully accountable for the leadership, performance and delivery of the Australia Pacific Leaders Program (APLP) Program Support Unit (PSU) on behalf of DFAT.

The role will lead the PSU team, with responsibility for aligning with strategic direction, ensuring contractual and policy compliance, managing risk and resources, and delivering high‑quality outcomes aligned with DFAT direction.

The Team Leader will be the primary point of accountability and escalation for DFAT and Abt, leading complex stakeholder engagement across various delivery partners, service providers and participants. The role will require strong judgement, adaptability and the ability to manage simultaneous planned and emerging priorities in a dynamic operating environment.

Specific Responsibilities

Leadership and Program Delivery

  • Lead the APLP Program Support Unit (PSU) team ensuring delivery is fully aligned with DFAT policy and direction.

  • Support DFAT to translate priorities into coherent, prioritised and actionable delivery of planned activities.

  • Ensure program delivery is responsive, adaptive and informed by priorities, anticipating emerging risks, sensitivities and opportunities across Pacific contexts.

  • Focus on practical, delivery-oriented strategy that enables rapid mobilisation and reduces operational burden on DFAT.

DFAT Client Relationship and Representation

  • Act as the senior interface with DFAT, maintaining a trusted, solutions-oriented partnership focused on responsiveness and delivery.

  • Represent the PSU in senior engagements where required, ensuring alignment with DFAT positions and priorities.

  • Provide clear, concise and actionable advice to DFAT on delivery options, trade-offs, and risks, particularly in fast-moving or politically sensitive contexts.

  • Proactively support DFAT by anticipating needs and simplifying processes, including for leader engagement, visits and activity delivery.

Contractual, Financial and Risk Accountability

  • Ensure full compliance with contractual obligations under the DFAT Deed of Standing Offer and Services Orders.

  • Oversee financial management, procurement and resource allocation to ensure value for money and efficient delivery.

  • Maintain fit-for-purpose risk, safeguarding and fraud management systems that enable safe but proportionate delivery.

  • Ensure monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) systems generate practical insights and concise high quality reporting that demonstrate outcomes and inform adaptive delivery.

People Leadership and Organisational Performance

  • Lead a high-performing PSU team capable of operating across multiple countries and responding rapidly to DFAT tasking.

  • Set clear priorities and ways of working that emphasise responsiveness, collaboration with DFAT, and delivery discipline.

  • Build a team culture that is client-focused, inclusive, and grounded in Pacific contexts, with strong internal coordination across functions.

  • Ensure the PSU has the right surge capacity and capability mix to respond to fluctuating demand.

  • Make decisions on resourcing, structure, and capability requirements for the PSU.
     

Quality, Innovation, and Continuous Improvement

  • Ensure all deliverables, reporting, and outputs meet DFAT and Abt quality standards and are fit for senior decision making.

  • Promote adaptive management and continuous learning.

  • Identify practical innovations that improve speed, coherence and user experience for DFAT and participants

  • Ensure GEDSI, safeguarding, ethical standards and other cross cutting policy priorities are embedded pragmatically across all activities, not treated as add-ons.

About You

We are seeking an individual for this executive role who brings:

Qualifications

  • Graduate qualification in international development, public policy, international relations, leadership, or a related field; or equivalent senior-level experience delivering complex international programs.

Skills and Experience 

  • Demonstrated experience delivering complex, high-profile programs in international development, government or related fields (DFAT or Pacific experience highly desirable).

  • Excellent understanding and commitment to DFAT aid policy priorities, compliance requirements and performance environment

  • Demonstrated success in leading large, multidisciplinary teams and managing delivery in politically and operationally complex environments.

  • Proven experience operating in fast-paced, high-pressure environments, including managing short-notice requests, competing priorities and sensitive activities and being able to adapt under pressure.

  • Strong track record in people-to-people engagement or relationship-based programs, including working with senior leaders across government, civil society or private sector.

  • Strong capability in contract, financial, and risk management with full accountability for program performance.

  • Experience overseeing or supporting high-level visits, events, or international engagements, with strong attention to logistics, protocol, risk, and participant experience desirable.

  • Strong analytical, written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate with a variety of audiences and lead the production of high-level reports.

  • Exceptional interpersonal skills with a demonstrated ability to build and maintain positive relationships with a range of stakeholders across complex operating environments

  • Strong cultural and contextual awareness and understanding, preferably gained through experience working in the Pacific or a similar operating environment.

Don’t meet every requirement? Studies have shown that women and people with sexual diversity or disability, are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single requirement for a position. At Abt Associates we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you are excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every role requirement, we encourage you to apply in any case. sections: Location: Canberra, Australia

Duration of contract: 12 months to 30 June 2027
Open to those with full work rights for Australia
About the Program

The Australia Pacific Leaders Program (APLP) is an Australian Government initiative that seeks to empower current and emerging Pacific leaders to deliver outcomes in their communities, strengthen their skills and build relationships with Australian agencies and institutions.
Activities include study tours, high-level visits, professional development and support for locally led projects, including assistance to deliver community-level initiatives.
APLP aims to:
empower leaders to deliver practical outcomes in their communities
build stronger, long-term relationships between Pacific leaders and Australia
strengthen leadership capability across the Pacific.
About the Program Support Unit (PSU)
The Program Support Unit (PSU) supports DFAT to deliver the program. Abt Global is contracted to deliver the PSU.

The PSU provides the practical support needed to deliver activities including planning, logistics, procurement and coordination. This includes supporting DFAT-led study tours and visits to Australia, coordinating training and events and supporting the delivery of grants and other program activities.
The PSU works closely with DFAT in Canberra and Posts across the Pacific to ensure activities are delivered to a high standard.
About the Opportunity

Abt are seeking to engage a Team Leader who will be fully accountable for the leadership, performance and delivery of the Australia Pacific Leaders Program (APLP) Program Support Unit (PSU) on behalf of DFAT.

The role will lead the PSU team, with responsibility for aligning with strategic direction, ensuring contractual and policy compliance, managing risk and resources, and delivering high‑quality outcomes aligned with DFAT direction.

The Team Leader will be the primary point of accountability and escalation for DFAT and Abt, leading complex stakeholder engagement across various delivery partners, service providers and participants. The role will require strong judgement, adaptability and the ability to manage simultaneous planned and emerging priorities in a dynamic operating environment.
Specific Responsibilities
Leadership and Program Delivery
Lead the APLP Program Support Unit (PSU) team ensuring delivery is fully aligned with DFAT policy and direction.
Support DFAT to translate priorities into coherent, prioritised and actionable delivery of planned activities.
Ensure program delivery is responsive, adaptive and informed by priorities, anticipating emerging risks, sensitivities and opportunities across Pacific contexts.
Focus on practical, delivery-oriented strategy that enables rapid mobilisation and reduces operational burden on DFAT.
DFAT Client Relationship and Representation
Act as the senior interface with DFAT, maintaining a trusted, solutions-oriented partnership focused on responsiveness and delivery.
Represent the PSU in senior engagements where required, ensuring alignment with DFAT positions and priorities.
Provide clear, concise and actionable advice to DFAT on delivery options, trade-offs, and risks, particularly in fast-moving or politically sensitive contexts.
Proactively support DFAT by anticipating needs and simplifying processes, including for leader engagement, visits and activity delivery.
Contractual, Financial and Risk Accountability
Ensure full compliance with contractual obligations under the DFAT Deed of Standing Offer and Services Orders.
Oversee financial management, procurement and resource allocation to ensure value for money and efficient delivery.
Maintain fit-for-purpose risk, safeguarding and fraud management systems that enable safe but proportionate delivery.
Ensure monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) systems generate practical insights and concise high quality reporting that demonstrate outcomes and inform adaptive delivery.
People Leadership and Organisational Performance
Lead a high-performing PSU team capable of operating across multiple countries and responding rapidly to DFAT tasking.
Set clear priorities and ways of working that emphasise responsiveness, collaboration with DFAT, and delivery discipline.
Build a team culture that is client-focused, inclusive, and grounded in Pacific contexts, with strong internal coordination across functions.
Ensure the PSU has the right surge capacity and capability mix to respond to fluctuating demand.
Make decisions on resourcing, structure, and capability requirements for the PSU.
Quality, Innovation, and Continuous Improvement
Ensure all deliverables, reporting, and outputs meet DFAT and Abt quality standards and are fit for senior decision making.
Promote adaptive management and continuous learning.
Identify practical innovations that improve speed, coherence and user experience for DFAT and participants
Ensure GEDSI, safeguarding, ethical standards and other cross cutting policy priorities are embedded pragmatically across all activities, not treated as add-ons.
About You
We are seeking an individual for this executive role who brings:
Qualifications

Graduate qualification in international development, public policy, international relations, leadership, or a related field; or equivalent senior-level experience delivering complex international programs.
Skills and Experience
Demonstrated experience delivering complex, high-profile programs in international development, government or related fields (DFAT or Pacific experience highly desirable).
Excellent understanding and commitment to DFAT aid policy priorities, compliance requirements and performance environment
Demonstrated success in leading large, multidisciplinary teams and managing delivery in politically and operationally complex environments.
Proven experience operating in fast-paced, high-pressure environments, including managing short-notice requests, competing priorities and sensitive activities and being able to adapt under pressure.
Strong track record in people-to-people engagement or relationship-based programs, including working with senior leaders across government, civil society or private sector.
Strong capability in contract, financial, and risk management with full accountability for program performance.
Experience overseeing or supporting high-level visits, events, or international engagements, with strong attention to logistics, protocol, risk, and participant experience desirable.
Strong analytical, written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate with a variety of audiences and lead the production of high-level reports.
Exceptional interpersonal skills with a demonstrated ability to build and maintain positive relationships with a range of stakeholders across complex operating environments
Strong cultural and contextual awareness and understanding, preferably gained through experience working in the Pacific or a similar operating environment.
