content.unEditedContent:
Job Description

Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

About the team

With over a quarter of a billion users every month and over 400 designs created each second - the Discovery Group ensures that our users spend more time designing and less time trying to find what they’re looking for.

Building powerful, reliable, scalable search capabilities is critical to achieving this mission.

The Discovery Platform team sits within the Discovery Group. We build and maintain the core indexing and querying frameworks that all of Canva’s search systems rely on. From internal observability tooling to scalable, modular frameworks, we enable product teams to ship search experiences fast, with confidence. Every search on Canva starts here.
In this role you'll be responsible for delivering strategic AI, revenue and MAU product initiatives in the content marketplace, bringing together stakeholders in multiple teams to achieve big goals that make Canva the best place in the world to discover & create content.
 

What you’d be doing in this role

  • Define and own the Platform vision, roadmap, and priorities for the Discovery Platform, ensuring alignment with company-wide goals

  • Develop and maintain continuous alignment with user facing Discovery teams to ensure Discovery Platform capabilities is evolving in line to support the needs and scale required

  • Proactively engage with other teams in early-stage product discovery discussions to ensure Discovery Platform’s capabilities and constraints are considered before key decisions are made

  • Identify opportunities to streamline Discovery Platform’s services to maximise impact and efficiency, freeing up engineering capacity

  • Promote the development of innovative platform solutions that solve recurring challenges across Discovery, making the platform more scalable and extensible

  • Evolve our search and recommendation systems to meet the advanced needs of enterprise 

  • Explore how AI is transforming the search and discovery landscape and ensure our discovery platform leveraging the latest technologies

You're probably a match if

  • Strong technical background with a deep understanding of platforms, software development, and current technology trends.

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical teams.

  • Strategic thinker with a track record of executing large-scale projects successfully (ideally in technical platforms, cloud services, or other related areas)

  • Experience in a fast-paced, high-growth tech environment is preferred

  • Bonus experience

    • Experience in building search infrastructure and working with vector databases

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

Other stuff to know

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture. When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process.

We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva so even if you don’t feel like your skills quite match what’s listed above - we still want to hear from you!

Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

content.jobHook: Wavell Heights State High School is currently seeking a dedicated technical officer to join our IT team and support student learning in a...
content.unEditedContent:
Wavell Heights State High School is currently seeking a dedicated technical officer to join our IT team and support student learning in a collaborative environment.

Join our outstanding IT faculty in Empowering Learners, Empowering Futures.

If you are passionate about supporting students, creating a welcoming and inclusive environment where students feel valued, supported and motivated to achieve their best,

Apply now!

This is a progressional position as per the Role Description. The successful applicant will be appointed to the lower classification with eligibility for progression to the next, once specific criteria have been met or demonstrated. Please note salary rate shown is reflective of both classification ranges.

Who We Are:

Wavell State High School, which opened in 1959, is a large and highly regarded State Secondary school in the Inner Northern suburbs of Brisbane. 

Approximately one quarter of our students are drawn from a defined, local catchment while the majority of students gain enrolment through selective entry requirements.

Acceptance of enrolment is based on academic achievement, sporting performance, talent in the arts or some combination of these attributes.

Step Into Your Next Chapter:

  • Provide advice and assistance on maximising the potential of ICT operations within the school/college, including acquisition, installation, operation, maintenance, repair and replacement.
  • Support the school community with technical advice, instruction and assistance with electronic equipment, in accordance with departmental, school and manufacturer's policy, guidelines and network standards.
  • Assist in the provision of in-service training to staff, on the effective application of ICT tools to successfully achieve and deliver educational services to students.
  • Provide effective and efficient support to staff and students to resolve problems associated with school computing facilities, whilst ensuring high end customer focus and communication.

Please view the role description for a full list of responsibilities.

Submit Your Application:

  • Attach a brief resume including contact details for 2 referees (referees should have an understanding of your relevant work history)
  • Attach a 2-page response to the How you will be assessed section of the attached role description.

We welcome all applicants to share any support needed to ensure our recruitment process is inclusive.

Applications remain current for 12 months from the closing date and may be considered for appointment to identical or similar vacancies within the Department.

Applications from recruitment agencies will not be accepted.

content.unEditedContent:
Pinnacle Rehab is an award-winning workplace rehab provider, with the goal of achieving quality recovery and return-to-work outcomes for individuals who have been injured at work, our dedicated consultants support these individuals to regain their confidence and independence. 

Our people are at the forefront of the business, we are committed to staff development and training. The collaborative team culture, extensive induction and onboarding into the business will support you to build a solid foundation into the industry of occ rehab. 

  • Certified ‘Great Place to Work’ and #2 Best workplaces in Healthcare and Social Assistance in Australia, Best workplaces for Women 
  • Structured induction, and individually tailored on boarding program 
  • Flexibility to organise your own calendar with appointments, office days and work-from-home 
  • Ongoing support in a collaborative and fun team environment 
What is on offer: 
  • Excellent remuneration on offer plus achievable bonus 
  • All travel reimbursed at $0.99 per km, including tolls and parking expenses 
  • Structured induction and on-boarding with buddy system, including ongoing weekly and monthly team meetings to support your learning 
  • Professional development opportunities, internally and externally  
  • Latest technology with laptop and iPhone provided  
  • Regular seasonal social events throughout the year 
  • The Pinnacle of Wellbeing (health and wellbeing initiatives) 
  • Opportunity to participate in our Emerging Leaders Program for career development opportunities 
Your Wellbeing our Heartbeat - Our employee benefits program   
  • Wellbeing Support - Employee Assistance Programs
  • Employee Connection - Social entertainment budgets
  • Life Balance - Unplug agreement, flexible working arrangements
  • Paid Parental Leave - Entitlements to support your growing family
  • Learning and Development - Group supervision sessions, quarterly  formal professional development and monthly bites and insights
The Opportunity: 

Due to growth across the business and our expanding Same Employer Division, we have a great opportunity for New Graduate OR Experienced, Exercise Physiologist, Occupational Therapist or Physiotherapist looking to grow their clinical experience into a new direction of helping people. 
 
In your new role you will manage a portfolio of clients with a psychological disorder, creating and monitoring rehabilitation plans and aim to gradually return your clients back to work.   
    
You will develop the skills needed to conduct motivational interviews with clients as well as influencing stakeholders to achieve the best possible outcomes for your clients.  
 
Looking after a client portfolio, your day will include:  
  • Manage a portfolio of clients with a physical injury 
  • Complete initial assessments to better understand the injury, recovery time frames and return to work goals 
  • Visiting workplace to assess environment and duties within the role, identify with employer of any suitable duties while recovering 
  • Providing support through recommendations for community assistance or additional support through the insurer

content.jobHook: Sutherland Shire Council is seeking enthusiastic and qualified Certificate III Early Childhood Educators to join our Early Education & Child...
content.unEditedContent:
Sutherland Shire Council is seeking enthusiastic and qualified Certificate III Early Childhood Educators to join our Early Education & Child Protection Team. We currently have part-time and full-time opportunities, with both temporary and permanent vacancies across our services.

In this role, you will provide compassionate, high-quality education and care for children from birth to six years, supporting their wellbeing and learning every day.

You’ll be hands-on, engaging with and supervising children, assisting with daily routines and maintaining a safe, clean environment. You’ll contribute to engaging, play-based educational programs tailored to each child’s interests and development, while working closely with families the team.

What You’ll Do
  • Observe and document children’s learning, development and engagement in the centre program.
  • Contribute to planning and delivering play-based learning programs.
  • Build supportive and collaborative relationships with families and children.
  • Collaborate with colleagues and engage in ongoing professional development
What You’ll Bring
  • Completed Certificate III in Education and Care.
  • Current First Aid qualification HLTAID010, HLTAID011 and HLTAID012
  • CPR Certification HLTAID009
  • Evidence of Child Protection accreditation i.e. 'Identify and Respond to children and young people at risk CHCPRT025'
  • NSW Working with Children Check.
  • National Foundations of Child Safety Training Certificate (Geccko)
  • Sound knowledge of the NQF, including EYLF, NQS and relevant legislation
  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative, professional approach

Join our Team and Grow with Us!

If you are ready to take on a challenging and rewarding role that makes a real difference in the community, apply now to join our team at Sutherland Shire Council!

  • Apply by responding to our online application questions and submitting your resume outlining why we are a great fit!
  • Applicants will be contacted as opportunities arise. Previous applicants need not apply.
  • Hourly Rate: $35.80 gross per hour plus 12% superannuation.
  • Package: $70,742 gross p.a. (salary paid pro-rata for part time roles) plus 12% superannuation. The Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) Worker Retention Allowance will be applied to these roles in addition with Federal Government guidelines.
  • Hours of work: Part-time and full-time, temporary and permanent opportunities available. Applicants must be available to work a range of shifts between the hours of 6:00am - 7:00pm to support the operational requirements of the centres.   
  • To benefit your wellbeing you will have access to fitness passport, employee assistance program, annual flu shots, health and wellbeing programme and novated lease options.

Suitable candidates are subject to pre-employment screening which includes Reference Checks, Work Rights Verification, Identity and Functional/Medical History Checks, and will also include a Criminal History, Qualification and Working with Children Check. Employment is subject to clearance of all these checks.

Reach out to Jessica Chappell, Business Administration Supervisor, JChappell@ssc.nsw.gov.au for any job specific enquiries.
Jodi Johnson, Talent Acquisition Business Partner, JJohnson@ssc.nsw.gov.au can assist with any recruitment related enquiries.

json.title: Community Education Counsellor (Identified) - Bracken Ridge State High School

content.jobHook: As a Community Education Counsellor at Bracken Ridge State High School, you will play a vital role in supporting Aboriginal and Torres Strait...
content.unEditedContent:
Bracken Ridge State High School is seeking a dynamic Community Education Counsellor (Identified), for a temporary part-time position (0.50 FTE or 36 hours per fortnight) until 11 December 2026, unless otherwise determined.

If you share our vision and have a passion for making a lasting difference, we invite you to join us and help our students to strive to accomplish.

As a Community Education Counsellor at Bracken Ridge State High School, you will play a vital role in supporting Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students to engage, succeed and thrive in their education. '

Working closely with students, families, school staff and community, you'll help create a culturally safe, inclusive and supportive learning environment.

If this sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you!

Who We Are:

At Bracken Ridge State High School, we pride ourselves on offering a broad and dynamic curriculum that caters to diverse interests and ambitions.

Our school is large enough to provide a wide range of academic, cultural, and co-curricular opportunities, yet small enough to ensure every student is known, valued, and supported on their individual journey.

We are dedicated to helping each student discover their strengths and explore pathways that lead to success in further education, careers, and life.

Step Into Your Next Chapter:

  • Provide counselling and targeted support services to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander students to enhance their educational engagement and wellbeing.
  • Develop and implement programs and activities, both within and outside school, that encourage participation in education among students and their families.
  • Build and maintain strong partnerships between schools, families, and external organisations to support student development and access to services.
  • Offer cultural guidance and share knowledge of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives, ensuring cultural awareness and understanding within the school community.
  • Advise school staff and leaders on cultural protocols and effectively manage funded programs to support student outcomes and community engagement.
  • Participate in activities to develop productive partnerships between members of the school community.

Please view the role description for a full list of responsibilities.

What You Will Bring:

  • A strong connection to and understanding of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander cultures, communities and perspectives
  • Experience working with young people, families or communities in education, youth or community settings
  • The ability to build trust and develop meaningful relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders
  • Strong communication skills and the confidence to advocate for student needs
  • A genuine commitment to improving educational outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students

It would be great if you also have:

  • Qualifications or training in counselling, youth work, community services or a related field
  • Experience working in a school or education environment
  • Experience delivering programs, workshops or cultural awareness training
  • Knowledge of local community services and support networks

Submit Your Application:

  • Attach a brief resume including contact details for 2 referees (referees should have an understanding of your relevant work history)
  • Attach a 2-page written statement in response to the attached role description.

We welcome all applicants to share any support needed to ensure our recruitment process is inclusive.

Applications remain current for 12 months from the closing date and may be considered for appointment to identical or similar vacancies within the Department.

Applications from recruitment agencies will not be accepted.

content.jobHook: We want to be the most accessible design tool in the world—and with strong, sustained internal support from leadership and core product teams, our...
content.unEditedContent:
Job Description

Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora,你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point. 

Where and how you can work

Our flagship campus is in Sydney. We also have a campus in Melbourne and co-working spaces in Brisbane, Perth and Adelaide. But you have choice in where and how you work. That means if you want to do your thing in the office (if you're near one), at home or a bit of both, it's up to you. 

What you’d be doing in this role

As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Drive architectural decisions for accessibility infrastructure, ensuring it scales to support accessible-by-default development across Canva
  • Lead critical cross-team accessibility initiatives from conception to production, establishing frameworks and patterns that teams can adopt independently
  • Design, develop and deploy hands-on solutions while collaborating with leads, designers, and product managers to deliver accessible experiences worldwide
  • Mentor engineers and champion accessibility best practices company-wide, elevating standards across the organization
  • Shape technical direction and influence product vision, ensuring accessibility is embedded in Canva's strategic roadmap
  • Engage senior stakeholders to align accessibility initiatives with business objectives and secure organizational support
  • Build tooling and documentation that empower teams to create accessible features efficiently
  • Model initiative and ownership in resolving technical debt, improving processes, and scaling accessibility solutions
  • Identify and pursue cross-team collaboration opportunities that advance our accessibility mission
  • Thoughtfully integrate AI into accessibility workflows to maximize efficiency, inclusion and innovation

You're probably a match if you are:

  • An experienced technical leader who still loves writing code — hands-on, action-oriented, and impact-driven
  • Deep expertise in accessibility engineering, including WCAG 2.2 AA, ATAG 2.0, and universal design principles, with a nuanced understanding of different disability models
  • Strong frontend expertise (JavaScript, React, TypeScript, MobX) with solid CS fundamentals in architecture and design patterns
  • Strategic thinking that connects technical decisions to company-wide priorities and builds solutions that scale
  • Track record of delivering high-impact projects with minimal guidance, particularly in developer tooling and platform projects
  • Leadership by example — mentoring others, elevating engineering standards, and championing inclusive development practices
  • Confidence engaging senior stakeholders and articulating technical accessibility concepts to diverse audiences
  • Genuine commitment to creating accessible experiences for all users and staying ahead of accessibility trends and standards

About the team

We want to be the most accessible design tool in the world—and with strong, sustained internal support from leadership and core product teams, our Accessibility Teams are set to achieve this mission. Canva is in a really interesting position in the accessibility space where we need to think about how everyone can use the product as well as how people can make designs that are accessible, ideally by default. Imagine being able to confidently use a design tool to make a beautiful design without seeing it. This is a deep, complex problem that is on the cutting edge of not just frontend engineering but also modern web applications.

About the Role

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll lead the technical evolution of accessibility at Canva, architecting scalable solutions that enable accessible-by-default development across our entire platform. You'll provide strong technical leadership, shaping frameworks and best practices that empower teams to build accessible features independently. Your role involves hands-on implementation of critical accessibility infrastructure while driving strategic initiatives that position Canva as the world's most accessible design tool. You'll have broad impact across the organization, directly contributing to our mission of supporting 1 billion users.

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a stack of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

Other stuff to know

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture. When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process.

Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

content.unEditedContent:
The Role

Are you passionate about working outdoors, operating machinery, and contributing to the development of your community? We’re looking for a motivated and skilled Plant Operator / Labourer to join our dedicated Rural Operations team.

As a key member of our multi-disciplined team, you’ll operate a range of plant equipment—including graders, backhoes, front-end loaders, and rollers—while also supporting essential labouring tasks that help build and maintain Council’s vital infrastructure. Your expertise will play a key part in shaping safe, functional, and well-presented spaces for our community to enjoy.

If you are a highly motivated and experienced individual who enjoys contributing to a community in which you live, we would love to hear from you.

Pre-employment Screening

Preferred candidates will be required to participate in and complete:

  • A successful Functional Capacity Evaluation; and
  • Be willing and able to be immunised against Hepatitis A&B and Tetanus.

Skills, Experience and Qualifications

To be successful in this role, you will have:

  • The ability to competently and safely operate a grader, backhoe, front end loader and roller;
  • Construction Industry Induction (White Card); and
  • Possess and maintain a current HC class motor vehicle licence and the ability to operate a low loader.

We have an exciting opportunity for two Full-time experienced practitioner’s to join our inclusive team of professional staff, based throughout Victoria, responsible for the delivery of psychosocial support to families.

With backgrounds in social work, psychology, family therapy and counselling, the team provides a range of child and family-centred programs including counselling, sibling support, trained volunteers, group work activities and bereavement support.

If you are passionate about caring for children and are seeking more purpose, fulfilment, and connection in your everyday work, Very Special Kids might be your perfect fit?

content.jobHook:
Join Mareeba State High School as a Guidance Officer and support the work of the Student Services team.
This temporary opportunity is offered for...
content.unEditedContent:
Join Mareeba State High School as a Guidance Officer and support the work of the Student Services team.

This temporary opportunity is offered for Semester 2, 2026.

Provide professional expertise, leadership and support to develop and implement plans, programs and procedures that help students achieve positive educational, developmental and lifelong learning outcomes.

This is a temporary full-time position for Semester 2, to commence from 13 July 2026 until 11 December 2026, unless otherwise determined.

About the Department

Working for the Queensland Department of Education means joining an organisation that values its people and promotes leadership and innovation. Be part of an environment that respects professionalism and diversity, offers training and development opportunities and embraces flexible careers and work-life balance. Find out more about working with us.

About the School

Mareeba State High School is a secondary school in Far North Queensland, known for its strong sense of community, inclusive culture and commitment to student wellbeing and engagement.

The school provides a supportive environment where staff work collaboratively to improve outcomes for all learners.

About the Role

As the Guidance Officer, your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

  • Advocate for students and provide counselling, psychoeducational assessment, and individual support, including recommendations and advice to students, teachers and parents regarding educational, behavioural, career development, mental health and family matters.
  • Work as part of a multidisciplinary team to build effective partnerships with parents, school staff and external support agencies, delivering coordinated support, case management and referral services that optimise student access and engagement in educational programs.

  • Provide counselling and referral services to support students in decision-making across educational, personal, social, emotional and career development, and deliver ongoing support during the implementation of their decisions.

  • Conduct student observation and psychoeducational assessment to determine learning difficulties, disability, developmental levels or psychological and emotional status, and provide recommendations for appropriate educational adjustments and interventions.

Please refer to the attached role description for any mandatory requirements for this position.

Interested? To Apply

  • Attach a brief resume including contact details for 2 referees (referees should understand your relevant work history).
  • Attach a written response (2-page maximum) as per Role Description 'How you will be assessed' section - addressing Key Capabilities 1-3 only.
  • Attach a copy of your mandatory requirements outlined in the Role Description.

We welcome all applicants to share any support needed to ensure our recruitment process is inclusive.Applications remain current for 12 months from the closing date and may be considered for appointment to identical or similar vacancies within the Department.Applications from recruitment agencies will not be accepted.

content.unEditedContent:
Teaching in the Channel Country offers more than just a career opportunity — it’s a chance to experience the unique lifestyle, connection, and adventure of Outback Queensland. Based across Jundah State School and Windorah State School, this circuit teaching role provides the opportunity to work within two welcoming rural communities, build strong relationships with students and families, and deliver meaningful educational experiences across diverse learning environments. Nestled among iconic outback landscapes and rich community spirit, this position is ideal for educators seeking professional growth, collaboration, and the rewarding experience of making a genuine difference in remote education.

This unique circuit role offers educators the opportunity to deliver high-quality teaching and learning experiences across both Jundah State School and Windorah State School, working collaboratively within small school settings where every student is known, supported, and encouraged to succeed. Teachers in this role will build strong partnerships with families and the wider community, contribute to whole-school initiatives, and embrace the flexibility and innovation that come with rural and remote education. With access to supportive colleagues, diverse teaching experiences, and the opportunity to make a lasting impact, this position is ideal for passionate educators seeking both professional fulfilment and the adventure of Outback Queensland living.

Current Opportunities:

  • Prep - Year 6 (Circuit position- Jundah State School, 0.6FTE / Windorah State School 0.4FTE)

What We Offer

  • Generous rural teacher incentives
  • Modern facilities and quality resources
  • Real career development opportunities
  • Relocation and housing support 

What You'll Need

  • Relevant teaching qualification
  • Full or provisional QCT registration
  • Australian working rights or valid visa
  • Pre-service and graduate teachers are encouraged to apply (include practicum reports, mentor statements & unofficial transcript)

How to apply

  • Click the Green 'Apply online' button below
  • Enter your personal details
  • Attach your resume including two professional referees

🔗 Explore the school: Visit Jundah State School and Windorah State School websites
📄 Read about departmental incentives: Download PDF (PDF) 

All applicants are encouraged to apply to the Department of Education Teacher Application Portal to be considered for current and future roles.

Applications from recruitment agencies will not be accepted.

content.unEditedContent:
• We are seeking Casual Exam Supervisors to support students during examination periods
  • Join a professional and supportive team committed to student wellbeing and success
  • An exciting opportunity to contribute to a calm, organised and positive examination environment

About the Role

Our Exam Supervisors play a key role in following exam guidelines from both the NSW Department of Education for the Higher School Certificate (HSC) and the International Baccalaureate for the IB Diploma (IBDP).  Exam Supervisors work throughout our school-based Trial Exams and our Final Exam blocks.  This role is responsible for ensuring all our exam sessions are run with consistency and professionally for the school and our students.  As an Exam Supervisor, responsibilities will include monitoring students, including assessing and responding to instances of misconduct, room set-up, verification of student identity, and the distribution, collection and validation of completed exam papers

About You

You are dedicated, passionate and possess the following:

  • Be available for both trial and final exam periods and be committed to arriving on time for rostered shifts
  • Be able to actively supervise exams, including standing for long periods of time and moving around the exam room
  • Flexibility, including being willing to change allocated exam rooms, work later or fill in for absences
  • Ability to carry out duties with attention to detail, confidentially and with discretion
  • Ability to work collaboratively with other team members and school staff
  • Ability to follow the relevant Presiding Officers instructions at all times.

All team members at CGS are required to have:

  • Appropriate qualifications
  • A valid ACT Working with Vulnerable People Card
  • A current National Police Check; and
  • Full working rights within Australia.

Benefits for you

As a CGS team member, you have access to a range of additional benefits, including:

  • Complimentary daily barista-made coffee
  • Delicious daily morning tea and discounted lunches
  • 24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme
  • Onsite parking

Working at CGS

We aim to provide a vibrant and rewarding workplace that showcases your skills with a strong commitment to your professional learning. Working at Canberra Grammar School you will join a community committed to delivering the highest standard of education, inspiring students to achieve personal excellence within a warm and inclusive environment.

We are continuously growing our CGS community with people who are passionate and energetic in their profession and who place student learning and well-being at the forefront of all they do. We invite candidates of all ages, people with a disability and Indigenous Australians to apply.

How to Apply

1. Please refer to the position description below.

2. Please click the ‘Apply’ button and submit the following documents:

  • Cover letter (addressing the selection criteria in the Position Description)
  • Resume/CV

CGS is proud to be a School that takes child protection very seriously. All candidates for roles at Canberra Grammar School are subject to screening and assessment against child safety standards as part of our thorough recruitment process.

An early application is advised as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early if sufficient suitable applications are received.

Attachments:
- Exam Supervisor - Position Description - 2026.pdf

content.jobHook: Are you a passionate and experienced legal professional ready to make a real impact in the lives of Queenslanders? Legal Aid Queensland is seeking...
content.unEditedContent:
Are you a passionate and experienced legal professional ready to make a real impact in the lives of Queenslanders? Legal Aid Queensland is seeking exceptional individuals to join our Public Defender Chambers as Counsel. This is your opportunity to contribute to a fairer justice system while advancing your career in a dynamic and supportive environment.

About Legal Aid Queensland

Legal Aid Queensland's vision is to be a leader in a fair justice system where people are able to understand and protect their legal rights. Our purpose is to provide quality, cost effective legal services to financially disadvantaged people throughout Queensland.

We embrace diversity, flexibility, learning and continuous improvement to deliver quality legal services. The work is challenging but rewarding - and that is why staff wellbeing and work/life balance are a top priority for us.

About the role

As a Counsel in the Public Defender Chambers, you will:

  • Represent legally-aided clients in a variety of jurisdictions, including the Supreme Court, District Court, Children's Court, and Mental Health Court.
  • Appear in high-stakes matters such as sentence appeals, trials, bail applications, and Dangerous Prisoners (Sexual Offenders) Act 2003 proceedings.
  • Travel across Queensland, including regional and remote communities, to ensure access to justice for all.
  • Provide expert guidance, mentoring, and feedback to lawyers in case preparation.
  • Deliver training to legal professionals and contribute to strategy, policy, and administrative initiatives.

This role is more than just a job – it's a chance to be part of a collegiate team of legal professionals, tackling challenging and meaningful work that makes a tangible difference in people's lives.

About you

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced legal professional with extensive expertise in criminal law, a strong command of evidence and procedure, and a proven ability to represent clients in complex legal matters. The ideal candidate will be admitted (or eligible for immediate admission) as a legal practitioner in Queensland and hold a current practising certificate as a barrister. You will possess exceptional advocacy skills, demonstrate leadership qualities, and have the ability to mentor and inspire others. A commitment to social justice and fostering an inclusive, diverse, and supportive workplace is essential.

Find out more about the role and how to apply in the attached role description.

As a member of the Legal Aid Queensland Community, you will receive:

  • A 36.25 hour working week (full time hours)
  • Generous salary packaging
  • Employer super contributions of 12.75%
  • Flexible working hours
  • Study leave for approved work-related courses.

Find out more about working in Legal Aid Queensland here: https://www.legalaid.qld.gov.au/About-us/Careers

  • Permanent full-time opportunity
  • Beautiful Yorke Peninsula location

Are you ready to take your career to the next level with a global leader in agribusiness? Bunge is looking for a Maintenance Supervisor to join our team at Port Giles.

About the role

As our new Maintenance Supervisor, you’ll be at the heart of operations, leading the maintenance of both fixed and mobile plant equipment at the site. You’ll ensure everything runs smoothly by coordinating electrical and mechanical servicing, as well as maintenance updates.

If you have strong experience managing teams, a trade qualification in electro-technology, mechanical fitting, diesel, or a related field, this role is for you!

Join Bunge, a global leader in agribusiness, and bring your skills to a team committed to operational excellence.

Duties

  • Participate in developing, recommending and instigating sustainable maintenance plans and programmes to ensure projects are completed in time with operational requirements
  • Manage the maintenance of hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, fixed and mobile plant and equipment
  • Perform Root Cause Analysis Reports and initiate continuous improvement plans
  • Ensure the accurate and timely upkeep of all maintenance records within the company systems
  • Ensure that all export terminals are maintained in accordance with current Environmental Legislation and Acts
  • Motivate, coordinate and train employees to facilitate safe, competent and initiative driven outcomes

About you

  • Proven experience in managing teams with a trade qualification in electro-technology, mechanical fitting, diesel, or similar
  • Previous experience in the grain or bulk handling industry (desirable)
  • Ability to work at heights and in confined spaces
  • Strong people management skills, including performance reviews
  • Valid driver’s license and good knowledge of technology to support role delivery

About us

Bunge connects farmers to consumers to deliver essential food, feed and fuel to the world.

Through our dynamic supply chain, we can move commodities efficiently from where there is surplus to where they are needed. In Australia, we operate around 60 storage and handling sites and seven port terminals across southern Western Australia, South Australia and western Victoria, two import sites in Victoria and New South Wales, and are one of the largest buyers and exporters of agricultural commodities including cereals, oilseeds, pulses and cotton.

By joining Bunge, you will enjoy a varied and interesting career and make a difference to local farmers and the communities we operate in.

In mid-2025, Bunge and Viterra combined, creating a premier agribusiness solutions with nearly 37,000 employees globally. 

Benefits

When you join Bunge, you’re not just starting a new job – you’re building a rewarding career with a global leader. We offer a supportive work culture that values respect, teamwork, and development. As part of the Bunge team, you’ll also enjoy a range of benefits, including:

  • Competitive remuneration package
  • Sign on bonus
  • On the job and external training
  • Employee assistance program – access to confidential and free support
  • Corporate health insurance funds, financial services, and computer offers
  • Novated leasing
  • Birthday leave
  • Years of service recognition
  • Rigorous safety practices
  • Gender-inclusive paid parental leave

How to apply

To apply for the position please click on ‘Apply’ at the bottom of the page or for further information please contact Maintenance Manager, Douglas Waye on +61 477 553 509.

Applications close 11:45pm Sunday 7 June 2026.

Please note we are not accepting recruitment agency applications at this time.

These positions are available to those who have the unrestricted right to live and work in Australia.

content.jobHook: As an Enterprise Account Executive, you will lead BlackLine’s growth within the Retail and Wholesale Distribution sectors across Australia and New...
content.unEditedContent:
Get to Know Us:

It's fun to work in a company where people truly believe in what they're doing!

At BlackLine, we're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business of enterprise applications.

Since being founded in 2001, BlackLine has become a leading provider of cloud software that automates and controls the entire financial close process. Our vision is to modernize the finance and accounting function to enable greater operational effectiveness and agility, and we are committed to delivering innovative solutions and services to empower accounting and finance leaders around the world to achieve Modern Finance.

Being a best-in-class SaaS Company, we understand that bringing in new ideas and innovative technology is mission critical. At BlackLine we are always working with new, cutting edge technology that encourages our teams to learn something new and expand their creativity and technical skillset that will accelerate their careers.

Work, Play and Grow at BlackLine!


Make Your Mark:

As an Enterprise Account Executive, you will lead BlackLine’s growth within the Retail and Wholesale Distribution sectors across Australia and New Zealand. You won’t just sell software; you will act as a strategic partner to Controllers and CFOs, helping them transform their financial operations. From initial outreach to long-term account evolution, you will be the face of BlackLine - advocating for your clients’ success, navigating complex C-suite relationships, and expanding our footprint within a high-growth SaaS model. Working closely with our Sales Excellence and Customer Success teams, you will ensure our customers realize the full value of their investment while consistently achieving your own professional and revenue goals.


You'll Get To:
  • Drive the end-to-end sales process from strategic prospecting to closing high-impact enterprise deals.
  • Move beyond technical features to sell the tangible ROI and strategic value BlackLine brings to finance teams.
  • Develop and execute comprehensive account plans and tiering strategies to maximize market presence in the ANZ region.
  • Build deep trust with stakeholders by translating complex business challenges into compelling narratives and solutions.
  • Serve as a dedicated resource throughout the client lifecycle, ensuring long-term satisfaction and high retention.
  • Partner with Customer Success to identify opportunities for upgrades, migrations, and new module implementations.
  • Work in lock-step with Solution Advisors, Marketing, Alliances, and Legal to deliver a seamless experience for prospective clients.
  • Build meaningful relationships with VP and C-level executives to understand their priorities and influence global business decisions.
  • Ensure your pipeline and opportunities are accurately reflected in Salesforce to support data-driven decision-making.
  • Participate in continuous learning and contribute to a supportive, high-achieving team culture.

What You'll Bring:
  • Significant experience leading complex Enterprise software sales, with a strong foundation in SaaS environments.
  • A proven ability to build rapport and grow territories by focusing on the people behind the business.
  • High proficiency in account planning and execution, with a focus on long-term territory health.
  • Experience navigating and influencing at the C-Level across both IT and Finance business units.
  • The ability to articulate clear value statements and ROI that resonate with financial leaders.
  • A track record of meeting or exceeding professional targets through consistent effort and strategy.
  • The curiosity and ability to quickly learn and communicate the benefits of a sophisticated financial platform.
  • Excellent verbal and written skills, with the ability to tailor your message to diverse audiences.
  • The ability to thrive and remain productive in a fast-paced, evolving SaaS organization.
  • A Bachelor’s degree in a related field (Business, Finance, IT) or equivalent professional experience that demonstrates the same level of expertise.

Thrive at BlackLine Because You Are Joining:
  • A technology-based company with a sense of adventure and a vision for the future. Every door at BlackLine is open. Just bring your brains, your problem-solving skills, and be part of a winning team at the world's most trusted name in Finance Automation!
  • A culture that is kind, open, and accepting. It's a place where people can embrace what makes them unique, and the mix of cultural backgrounds and varying interests cultivates diverse thought and perspectives.
  • A culture where BlackLiner's continued growth and learning is empowered. BlackLine offers a wide variety of professional development seminars and inclusive affinity groups to celebrate and support our diversity.

BlackLine is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity or expression, race, ethnicity, age, religious creed, national origin, physical or mental disability, ancestry, color, marital status, sexual orientation, military or veteran status, status as a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking, medical condition, genetic information, or any other protected class or category recognized by applicable equal employment opportunity or other similar laws

BlackLine recognizes that the ways we work and the workplace itself has shifted. We innovate in a workplace that optimizes a combination of virtual and in-person interactions to maximize collaboration and nurture our culture. Candidates who live within a reasonable commute to one of our offices will work in the office at least 3 days a week.

companyProfile.name: Blackline
companyProfile.overview: Companies come to BlackLine (Nasdaq: BL) because their traditional manual accounting processes are not sustainable. BlackLine’s cloud-based financial operations management platform and market-leading customer service help companies move to modern accounting by unifying their data and processes, automating repetitive work, and driving accountability through visibility. BlackLine provides solutions to manage and automate financial close, accounts receivable and intercompany accounting processes, helping large enterprises and midsize companies across all industries do accounting work better, faster and with more control., Thousands of customers trust BlackLine to help them close faster with complete and accurate results. BlackLine is a global company with operations in major business centers around the world including Los Angeles, New York, the San Francisco Bay area, London, Paris, Frankfurt, Tokyo, Singapore and Sydney.

content.jobHook: Join us at Hervey Bay Hospital to provide compassionate, expert support for patients managed through the Palliative Care Support Service in the...
content.unEditedContent:
Join us at Hervey Bay Hospital to provide compassionate, expert support for patients managed through the Palliative Care Support Service in the Fraser Coast region. This is your chance, as a Registrar or PHO, to deliver holistic care that truly improves quality of life for patients and their families.

Take a chance, progress your career and discover all that the Wide Bay has to offer.

Your opportunity:

  • The purpose of the role is to participate in patient management in the ambulatory and in-patient settings of the Palliative Care Support Service.
  • Provide support for patients being managed through the Palliative Care Support Service in the Fraser Coast region of the Wide Bay Hospital and Health Service.

This position is accredited with RACGP and ACRRM. 

Temporary Full Time (76 hours p.f.) from date of appointment for 12 months with the possibility of extension. 

Find out more in the Role Description.

Our offer:

We are offering a competitive remuneration package value up to $181,097 p.a., including salary between $133,848 - $154,749 p.a., generous employer superannuation (up to 12.75%), salary sacrifice perks, and flexible rostering for optimal work/life balance. H2605WB682432

Regional Queensland residents enjoy a lower cost of living and affordable housing in one of the world's most beautiful and diverse regions.

Other benefits include:   

  • Generous superannuation contribution (up to 12.75%)
  • Annual Leave Loading (17.5%)
  • Fantastic salary sacrificing benefits
  • Professional Development Allowance 
  • Professional Development Leave 
  • Flexible work arrangements
  • Lower cost of living

Discover Fraser Coast   

The Fraser Coast, known for its diverse, natural landscapes, laid-back lifestyle and mild climate, is located just a quick 45-minute flight north of Brisbane. This destination with a difference is the stepping off point to the World Heritage-listed Fraser Island, the location of incredible whale watching encounters and has arguably the safest family-friendly beaches in Queensland. Stroll along the Hervey Bay esplanade for alfresco cafes, shops, picnic areas, playgrounds and vibrant marina, or soak up the history and culture in the provincial city of Maryborough.

json.title: Certificate III Educator | Woronora Heights Community Preschool 0-5

content.jobHook: Right now, we’re looking for a Certificate III Educator for Woronora Heights Community Preschool. With a homely, warm and friendly environment, the...
content.unEditedContent:
Certificate III Educator

  • Permanent, Full Time

Working at Big Fat Smile, there’s a lot to smile about. The trust you’ll be given in exchange for your expertise. The freedom you’ll be given to use your judgement, adapt learning approaches, and bring creativity and playfulness to a child’s day. And the beautiful relationships you’ll form with peers, children, and families – through shared experiences that are as rich as they are rewarding.

There are lots of reasons why a role with us is rewarding

  • Due to our size, there are big opportunities for those who want to go further. You’ll find meaningful career paths with opportunities for further development and promotions across our centres and head office.
  • Professional learning and growth are at the heart of everything we do, from learning more about infant-toddler pedagogy, trauma responsive practice, cultural immersion and truth telling, to leadership through a neuroscience lens – these are some of the things our people have benefited from.
  • Support to further your studies, such as scholarships, time off floor for coursework, study leave, paid prac and more.
  • Save money with our Perks Hub which has great deals and discounts from over 500 major retailers and the biggest brands, including groceries, cinema tickets, clothing, homewares, tech, travel and more.
  • Access to our Wellness Hub which has a wealth of curated content focused on your wellbeing, plus monthly health and wellbeing webinars, free flu vaccinations and more.
  • A holistic approach to your wellbeing with our employee assistance program, including counselling, First Nations clinicians, health assessments, financial and legal support, and a dedicated manager hotline.
  • Save with a 60% discount on early learning and care and out of school hours care services.
  • Focus on what matters most because you have support from head office specialists and expertise, such as safeguarding, inclusion professionals, and pedagogy and practice specialists.

Right now, we’re looking for a Certificate III Educator for Woronora Heights Community Preschool. With a homely, warm and friendly environment, the service is able to provide a wonderful space for the children to grow and thrive. Working alongside dedicated and experienced educators, the service values nature-based play outside, utilising local parks, playing fields and the community shopping centre. Empowering the children to use their voice, work together and respect the ideas of others.

As an Early Childhood Educator, you’ll play a critical role in shaping young minds. You’ll create happy, healthy relationships between a child and the most important people in their lives. You’ll bring fun, laughter and play to each day, but most importantly, you’ll create magical moments for children to experiment and grow.

What your work will involve

  • Providing quality education and care to all children
  • Contributing to planning educational programs that supports a child’s learning to meet their goals
  • Building strong relationships with children, families, and the community

What you need to succeed

  • Commitment to making sure the children in our care are safe and healthy
  • Dedication to improving the lives and minds of children, families, and the community
  • A fun-loving attitude and big smile!

Our commitment to safeguarding children

Safeguarding children is at the heart of every decision, policy and practice at Big Fat Smile. And we have a zero tolerance towards child abuse, harm and neglect.

This starts with ensuring the people we select to work here will contribute to our child safe culture. So during the recruitment process we conduct a range of pre-employment checks. To assist us with this, you will need:

  • A cleared valid for paid work, NSW working with Children’s Check (WWCC)
  • A cleared National Criminal Record Check
  • Demonstrated commitment to protecting all children from abuse, harm and neglect.
  • Demonstrated commitment to cultural safety for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and families.
  • Evidence of completion of the National Child Safety Training Foundation Course
  • Details of a minimum two referees, where one must be a manager or supervisor at your current or most recent workplace.

How to apply

Please send us:

  • A copy of your resume
  • A brief cover letter that outlines why you are a good fit for the role

At Big Fat Smile we are deeply committed to Reconciliation and encourage Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people to apply.

Big smiles and bigger opportunities

We’re Big Fat Smile. A not-for-profit that plays a pivotal role in the lives of thousands of children and families across Australia. We’re early education enthusiasts, with 40+ community preschools, long day care and out of school hours care centres, and a variety of community and inclusion programs. Each one dedicated to giving every child the best start in life. And each well-respected for the work it does.

Join us and you’ll be smiling too, when you make more of a difference.

json.title: Dispensary / Retail Pharmacist - Slade Pharmacy, Epworth Maternity Hospital

content.jobHook: Slade Pharmacy at Epworth Maternity Hospital in East Melbourne is seeking a part-time Dispensary Pharmacist to join our team on a permanent...
content.unEditedContent:
About the Opportunity
Slade Pharmacy at Epworth Maternity Hospital in East Melbourne is seeking a part-time Dispensary Pharmacist to join our team on a permanent part-time basis, working each Friday from 8am to 6pm.

In this role, you’ll contribute to the smooth operation of our retail pharmacy located within the hospital, providing medication and support services to patients, carers, and staff. You’ll be part of a welcoming and professional team committed to delivering high-quality pharmacy care.

Key Responsibilities

  • Dispense and supply medications and pharmacy products
  • Coordinate medication requirements for patients, including discharges and outpatient needs
  • Provide excellent customer service to patients, carers, and hospital staff
  • Attend to front-of-shop duties and support the day-to-day operations of the dispensary
  • Educate customers on medication use, health promotion, and general pharmacy queries
  • Support patients, carers, hospital staff and associated employees
  • Educate and advise staff and customers on health promotion, disease prevention, drug selection and the proper use of medicines
  • Prepare and package medications in dosage as necessary.
  • Attend the front shop to ensure the smooth running of the pharmacy.
  • Prepare and package medications as required
  • Participate in other dispensary duties as needed

About You
You’re a registered pharmacist who enjoys working in a retail pharmacy environment. Whether you’re newly registered or bringing prior experience, you’re reliable, approachable, and committed to delivering high-quality service. You work well independently and as part of a team.

Eligibility Requirements

  • Current AHPRA registration as a Pharmacist with no restrictions on practice.
  • Strong knowledge of the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS)
  • Australian working rights, valid for at least 13-months from time of employment.
  • Have time management, communication and teamwork skills
  • Excellent communication and time management skills
  • Ability to work autonomously and multitask
  • Retail pharmacy experience is welcomed but not essential

About Slade Pharmacy
Established as a family business in 1965, Slade Pharmacy is underpinned by 60 years’ of pharmacy experience. Slade delivers pharmacy services and best clinical practice through a hospital and oncology pharmacy governance framework. As part of Icon Group, Slade Pharmacy employs more than 1,100 pharmacists, technicians and support staff. Slade has more than 70 pharmacies across Australia and is dedicated to quality patient care delivered by an experienced team alongside longstanding partnerships with large private hospital groups. 

For more information visit https://sladepharmacy.com.au/ ;

Our Values

  • Purpose, at Pace: We remain focused on continually expanding our cancer treatment services and making them accessible to more people across Australia and internationally.
  • Impact, at Scale: We’re Australia’s largest dedicated provider of cancer care, with our global reach growing every day. Here you’ll know your work is making a difference.
  • Connection, at Heart: Our work isn’t easy but it’s extremely important. Our secret ingredient is our incredible, connected, and talented people. And their secret ingredient is each other.
  • Opportunity, at Hand: We’re continually innovating. We deliver over 2.5 million patient interactions, in over 120 places, across 5 countries. Every week brings changes, growth and new opportunities.

Visit https://icongroup.global/en/careers/our-people/stories/ to read the stories of our incredible people.

Here are some of the benefits available at Icon Group

  • Hands-on training provided to help you further your pharmacy career in a hospital setting
  • Competitive remuneration and structured professional development through our National Career Pathway
  • Valued rewards and recognition program
  • Incredible discounts and cashback on hundreds of brands through our internal Ignite app
  • Access to novated lease options via our partner RemServ
  • Access to paid parental leave for permanent employees
  • Resources and tools to help support and balance psychological and physical health

To Apply
Please attach a resume and cover letter showing us why you’d love to join us, and what makes you a great fit for the role.

Icon Group celebrates diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive workplace for all employees. We encourage applications from all diverse backgrounds.

Pre-Employment Health Requirement
Icon is committed to managing the risk of transmission of specified vaccine preventable diseases (VPDs). Certain roles may require the successful candidate to show evidence that they have been vaccinated against or are not susceptible to specified VPDs.

content.unEditedContent:
• Multiple positions available for level 1, 2 and 3
  • Hourly rates range from $31.99 to 48.05
  • Work for a multi-award-winning iconic community health organisation
  • Generous salary packaging options to reduce your cohealth taxable income

So why cohealth? cohealth leads the way in reducing health and social inequity in partnership with people and the communities in which they live. Named Premier's Health Service of the Year (Primary) and the Supporting LGBTIQ+ Health Service at the Victorian Public Healthcare Awards, cohealth's 1000 staff demonstrate courage, leadership, innovation, and agility in their commitment to providing inclusive and culturally safe health services that protect the human rights of all people of all gender identities, sexualities, ages, cultural and linguistic backgrounds, faiths, and abilities.

Our inclusive workplace culture enables staff to bring their whole selves to work, where uniqueness is valued, and people experience a feeling of belonging. Our aim is for everyone to thrive in their role. Please click here to find out more.

About the role This position sits within the Oral Health cluster which provides a range of evidence-based preventive, restorative and health promoting activities to enhance the Oral Health of the communities attending our clinical sites in Kensington, Niddrie, and Footscray as well as various outreach locations.

Please refer to the Position Descriptions below for more information:

Your duties include:

  • Provide oral health promotion, education, screening and treatment to clients and parents of children in clinic and outreach settings
  • Provide direct client care in accordance with cohealth policies, consistent with the level of scope and experience and in collaboration with the client and Oral Health Team
  • Perform all other program requirements aligned with scope, as rostered, as directed
  • Oral Health Therapist positions are required to work in the Smile Squad program and across all cohealth Oral Health clinic locations and other outreach locations at times

What cohealth offers:

  • Exciting Parental leave benefits
    • cohealth offers primary carers 14 weeks paid parental leave upon completion of only 6 months of continuous service
    • Eligible co-workers will continue to receive superannuation on unpaid parental leave as well
  • Novated Leasing available

  • A significantly discounted fitness membership with unlimited access to over 290 facilities for you and your family. To find out more click here

  • Counselling services for you and your immediate family through our EAP-Access provider, and mindfulness, resilience, and wellbeing programs
  • We offer inclusion, equality, and opportunity in a workplace where making a difference counts (based on our guiding principles and values)

Our ideal candidate:

  • Oral Health Therapists qualification - Adult Scope is desirable
  • Victorian Radiation Licence and AHPRA registration
  • An understanding and commitment to the principals of community health
  • Strong belief and personal alignment in cohealth Values and Mission

Application Process

To download the PD, and to apply for this job go to: https://cohealthcareers.org.au/Current-Jobs & enter ref code: 6893603.

Applications close 29 May at 10.00 PM.

We will be conducting interviews for this role as applications are received.

If you have any questions regarding this role, please contact Michelle Domingo on Michelle.Domingo@cohealth.org.au

All appointments are made subject to a satisfactory Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check (NCCHC), a Working With Children Check (WWCC), complete a Pre-Employment Declaration Form, evidence of legal rights to work in Australia, and evidence of vaccination.

Successful applicants will be required to provide evidence of immunisation assessment including Influenza within 12 weeks of commencement [B]. This is in accordance with the Victorian Minister of Health Mandatory Vaccination Orders and legislated requirement for influenza vaccination.

Sutherland Shire Council is looking for a dedicated Cook to join our Early Education Centre team. This is more than a kitchen role - it’s a chance to positively influence the health, development and daily experiences of children aged 0–5 through fresh, nourishing food.

About the Role

As our Early Education Centre Cook, you’ll plan and prepare balanced, high-quality meals that support the dietary, cultural and developmental needs of young children. You’ll play an important role in fostering healthy eating habits, while ensuring all meals align with Australian Dietary Guidelines and food safety standards. We are looking for someone to join our team in a part-time role at our 59-place centre, working Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday for 6 hours each day.

What You’ll Do
  • Prepare fresh, nutritious meals and snacks for children aged 0–5
  • Develop seasonal menus that reflect dietary guidelines and cultural diversity
  • Safely cater to individual dietary needs, including allergies and restrictions
  • Maintain high standards of food safety, hygiene and kitchen operations
  • Work closely with educators and families to create positive, inclusive mealtime experiences
About You

You’re organised, reliable and enjoy being part of a collaborative team. You bring creativity to meal preparation and have a genuine interest in supporting the health and wellbeing of young children. You’re comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and take pride in delivering quality meals every day.

Essential Requirements
  • Current Working With Children Check
  • Food Handler’s Certificate (or willingness to obtain)
Desirable
  • Experience in a childcare or hospitality setting
  • Basic nutrition training or knowledge
  • First Aid Certificate
  • Understanding of allergy-aware and anaphylaxis-safe food practices

Join our Team and Grow with Us!

If you are ready to take on a challenging and rewarding role that makes a real difference in the community, apply now to join our team at Sutherland Shire Council!

  • Apply by responding to our online application questions and submitting your resume outlining why we are a great fit!
  • Get your application in by 11.59pm: Monday 8th June 2026.
  • Interview date: Interviews will be facilitated within 2 weeks of job ad closing.
  • Hours of work: Part-time role, 18 hours per week. Flexibility to pick up additional shifts may be available, depending on operational needs. 
  • Hourly Rate: $29.62 gross per hour plus 12% superannuation.
  • Package: $58,545 gross p.a. (salary paid pro-rate for part time) plus 12% superannuation. The Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) Worker Retention Allowance will be applied to these roles in addition with Federal Government guidelines.  
  • To benefit your wellbeing you will have access to fitness passport, employee assistance program, annual flu shots, health and wellbeing programme and novated lease options.

Suitable candidates are subject to pre-employment screening which includes Reference Checks, Work Rights Verification, Identity and Functional/Medical History Checks (including Covid-19 Vaccination), and may also include a Criminal History, Qualification and Working with Children Check. Employment is subject to clearance of all these checks.

Reach out to Jessica Chappell, Business Administration Supervisor, JChappell@ssc.nsw.gov.au for any job specific enquiries.
Jodi Johnson, Talent Acquisition Business Partner, JJohnson@ssc.nsw.gov.au can assist with any recruitment related enquiries.

Click on the link to check out the Position Description

Council is a Child Safe Organisation and is committed to ensuring the NSW Government’s Child Safe Standards are incorporated in our procedures, practices, programs, and events.

content.jobHook: We are currently seeking a Maintenance Electrician to join our maintenance team in a well-established role at our Wallaroo Terminal. In this role,...
content.unEditedContent:
• Dynamic career opportunity in a leading agribusiness based on the Yorke Peninsula
  • Key role supporting maintenance operations at our Wallaroo terminal
  • Competitive remuneration package + sign on bonus + on call allowances + more!

About the role

We are currently seeking a Maintenance Electrician to join our maintenance team in a well-established role at our Wallaroo Terminal. In this role, you will manage operational requirements to ensure plant and equipment is maintained to the highest standard and running efficiently, while focusing on safety. Maximising uptime is critical to ensuring we can deliver an efficient and reliable service to our customers.

This role will also provide you with day-to-day variety and problem solving, while also incorporating long term planning projects as part of our preventative and predictive maintenance programmes.

Join Bunge, a global agribusiness, bringing your expertise to maintain and enhance performance at Wallaroo, located on the beautiful Yorke Peninsula; enjoy the lifestyle, stunning coastline and welcoming community.

Duties

  • Implement and conduct fault finding and repairs to electrical and pneumatic systems.
  • Assist Mechanical staff with repairs to Diesel and 12V equipment.
  • Assist in developing and implementing solutions and strategies to ensure the timely and effective response to equipment failures and breakdowns.
  • Perform electrical (including PLC diagnostic) and repairs.
  • Work with the maintenance manager to identify and implement plant improvements and future capital projects.
  • Provide On Call support during shipping and harvest periods.
  • Travel within the region assisting other teams as required.
  • Execute the preventative maintenance program in line with terminal operations.

About you

  • An Electrical workers licence Class A (South Australia)
  • Have a willingness to learn bearing lubrication techniques.
  • Competent in interpreting hydraulic and pneumatic diagrams
  • Experience with hydraulic, electrical, mechanical and pneumatic systems
  • Experience maintaining fixed and mobile plant and equipment
  • Willingness to Assist mechanical staff and learn new skills.
  • Positive attitude and teamwork mindset.
  • The ability to work at heights and within confined spaces
  • Current drivers licence is essential 

About us

Bunge is a premier agribusiness solutions company. With our agile workforce, enhanced global footprint, increased access to key markets and diversified agriculture network covering all major crops, Bunge is able to manage seasonal cycles, weather and other risks, better connecting growers to consumers to deliver essential food, feed and fuel to the world.

By joining Bunge, you will enjoy a varied and interesting career and make a difference to local growers and the communities we operate in.

On 2 July, Bunge successfully completed its combination with Viterra. Going forward, our business will operate as Bunge, and transition to the brand over the coming months.

Benefits

When you join Bunge, you’re not just starting a new job – you’re building a rewarding career with a global leader. We offer a supportive work culture that values respect, teamwork, and development. As part of the Bunge family, you’ll also enjoy a range of benefits, including:

  • On call allowances plus additional payment when called in to attend site
  • Competitive remuneration package
  • Sign on bonus
  • Tools of trade provided
  • On the job and external training
  • Employee assistance program – access to confidential and free support
  • Corporate health insurance funds, financial services, and computer offers
  • Novated leasing
  • Birthday leave
  • Years of service recognition
  • Rigorous safety practices
  • Gender-inclusive paid parental leave

How to apply

To apply for the position please click on ‘Apply’ at the bottom of the page or for further information please contact Maintenance Manager, Douglas Waye on 0477 553 509.

Applications close 11:45pm Sunday 7th June 2026

Please note we are not accepting recruitment agency applications at this time.

These positions are available to those who have the unrestricted right to live and work in Australia.

Please note that we may close this advertisement early if a suitable candidate is found before the listed closing date. We encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible.

Bunge is an equal opportunity employer and we welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds.
