json.title: Additional Educator | Port Kembla Community Preschool

content.jobHook: Right now, we’re looking for an Additional Educator (Certificate III Qualified) for our Port Kembla Community Preschool – an ‘Exceeding NQS’ rated...
content.unEditedContent:
Additional Educator:

  • Maximum Term, part-time position
  • 24 hours per week
  • Monday, Thursday and Friday (8 hours per day)

Working at Big Fat Smile, there’s a lot to smile about. The trust you’ll be given in exchange for your expertise. The freedom you’ll be given to use your judgement, adapt learning approaches, and bring creativity and playfulness to a child’s day. And the beautiful relationships you’ll form with peers, children, and families – through shared experiences that are as rich as they are rewarding.

There are lots of reasons why a role with us is rewarding

  • Due to our size, there are big opportunities for those who want to go further. You’ll find meaningful career paths with opportunities for further development and promotions across our centres and head office.
  • Professional learning and growth are at the heart of everything we do, from learning more about infant-toddler pedagogy, trauma responsive practice, cultural immersion and truth telling, to leadership through a neuroscience lens – these are some of the things our people have benefited from.
  • Support to further your studies, such as scholarships, time off floor for coursework, study leave, paid prac and more.
  • Save money with our Perks Hub which has great deals and discounts from over 500 major retailers and the biggest brands, including groceries, cinema tickets, clothing, homewares, tech, travel and more.
  • Access to our Wellness Hub which has a wealth of curated content focused on your wellbeing, plus monthly health and wellbeing webinars, free flu vaccinations and more.
  • A holistic approach to your wellbeing with our employee assistance program, including counselling, First Nations clinicians, health assessments, financial and legal support, and a dedicated manager hotline.
  • Save with a 60% discount on early learning and care and out of school hours care services.
  • Focus on what matters most because you have support from head office specialists and expertise, such as safeguarding, inclusion professionals, and pedagogy and practice specialists.

Right now, we’re looking for an Additional Educator (Certificate III Qualified) for our Port Kembla Community Preschool – an ‘Exceeding NQS’ rated service. Our educational program is guided by the Early Years Learning Framework; ‘Belonging, Being and Becoming’ and we are committed to developing children’s awareness of the world around them. Through the creative arts and music, the children are involved in learning multicultural language and music from various cultures on a daily basis.

We have a transition to school program which promotes the development of both emotional and academic skills. We take annual excursions to our local public school as part of our transition to school program.

Lastly, we love our school borrowing library to foster language and literacy skills as well as encourage the love of books.

As an Early Childhood Educator, you’ll play a critical role in shaping young minds. You’ll create happy, healthy relationships between a child and the most important people in their lives. You’ll bring fun, laughter and play to each day, but most importantly, you’ll create magical moments for children to experiment and grow.

What your work will involve

  • Providing quality education and care to all children
  • Contributing to planning educational programs that supports a child’s learning to meet their goals
  • Building strong relationships with children, families, and the community

What you need to succeed

  • Commitment to making sure the children in our care are safe and healthy
  • Dedication to improving the lives and minds of children, families, and the community
  • A fun-loving attitude and big smile!

Our commitment to safeguarding children

Safeguarding children is at the heart of every decision, policy and practice at Big Fat Smile. And we have a zero tolerance towards child abuse, harm and neglect.

This starts with ensuring the people we select to work here will contribute to our child safe culture. So during the recruitment process we conduct a range of pre-employment checks. To assist us with this, you will need:

  • A cleared valid for paid work, NSW working with Children’s Check (WWCC)
  • A cleared National Criminal Record Check
  • Demonstrated commitment to protecting all children from abuse, harm and neglect.
  • Demonstrated commitment to cultural safety for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and families.
  • Evidence of completion of the National Child Safety Training Foundation Course
  • Details of a minimum two referees, where one must be a manager or supervisor at your current or most recent workplace.

How to apply

Please send us:

  • A copy of your resume
  • A brief cover letter that outlines why you are a good fit for the role

At Big Fat Smile we are deeply committed to Reconciliation and encourage Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people to apply.

Big smiles and bigger opportunities

We’re Big Fat Smile. A not-for-profit that plays a pivotal role in the lives of thousands of children and families across Australia. We’re early education enthusiasts, with 40+ community preschools, long day care and out of school hours care centres, and a variety of community and inclusion programs. Each one dedicated to giving every child the best start in life. And each well-respected for the work it does.

Join us and you’ll be smiling too, when you make more of a difference.

Safeguarding children is embedded in all we do. Through our Child Safe Framework and Values, we are committed to ensuring the safety and well-being of all children entrusted to our care.

content.jobHook: Rural Allied Health are seeking an experienced and client focused Allied Health Assistant to join their highly skilled Medical Imaging Department...
content.unEditedContent:
Rural Allied Health are seeking an experienced and client focused Allied Health Assistant to join their highly skilled Medical Imaging Department at INGHAM HOSPITAL.

PLEASE NOTE: This is a permanent full-time role.

About the opportunity   

Working under a delegated model of practice to achieve consumer-focussed outcomes, as the Medical Imaging Assistant you will support the effective and efficient running of the medical imaging service at the Ingham Hospital.

With all the lifestyle and community benefits that the Hinchinbrook area offers, this position is a key member of the Medical Imaging Team at the Ingham Hospital. 

PLEASE NOTE - This is a permanent full-time role. 

Role requirements

  • Whilst not mandatory, possession of a Certificate IV Allied Health Assistant, or experience in a similar role would be highly desirable.
  • It is highly desired that the successful applicant holds, or is willing to obtain and use a Rural or Remote Area Radiography use licence (x-ray operator licence) to support the operational functions of the imaging department
  • Successful applicants to this position will possess a Class C Motor Vehicle licence
  • The successful candidates will be required to participate in roster that involves shift work, weekend work and public holidays.
  • Blue Card Checks: Potential applicants are advised that the Commission for Children and Young People and Child Guardian Act 2000 requires Queensland Health to seek a ‘working with children check' from the Commission for Children and Young People and Child Guardian prior to appointment to this position. 5.1.
  • This is a Vaccine Preventable Disease (VPD) risk role. Hepatitis B, Measles, Mumps, Rubella, Varicella, Pertussis and Tuberculosis.

Please refer to the Role Description for further details.

Work/Life Balance and Lifestyle Benefits

Ingham Health Service provides an integrated service encompassing a range of community-based services, provision of Allied Health services and traditional hospital-based services of an Inpatient ward, an Emergency Department, a limited range of surgical procedures and a range of support services including
X-ray, Pharmacy, Administration and Operational Services.

Ingham is culturally diverse town with a rich Italian history; just over an hour's drive north from Townsville it offers a unique collection of culture, fresh produce and vast green landscapes.

Competitive salary and benefits:

We offer attractive remuneration packages and generous leave entitlements.

  • Salary range: $2624.50 - $2759.10 p.f. (CA3)
  • 4 weeks annual leave with 17.5% loading
  • Locality allowance
  • 12.75% employer contribution to superannuation
  • Plus Salary Sacrificing options may be available

Apply now

Enquiries are welcome; please contact: Bridget Webber on 0429 727 028

Apply ONLINE: https://apply-springboard.health.qld.gov.au/jobs/QLD-TV682959

Applications close: Sunday, 31 May 2026

Unsolicited resumes from recruitment agencies will not be accepted.

Please download the Role Description from the `Documents' section below for application/interview preparation and future reference.

content.jobHook:
We are looking for a passionate and dedicated OOSH Coordinator to join our team here at Bishop Tyrrell Anglican College!
About the role
You will...
content.unEditedContent:
Bishop Tyrrell Anglican College
Fletcher, NSW

Monday- Friday

Split shifts - 6.15 am to 10.15am and 2.30pm to 6.00pm

We are looking for a passionate and dedicated OOSH Coordinator to join our team here at Bishop Tyrrell Anglican College!

About the role
You will provide leadership and management to educators and staff regarding all aspects of the operation of the service in line with relevant regulations, policies and procedures. Work closely with and provide periodical reports to the Operations Manager regarding matters relating to the operation of the service and support educators and staff with professional training and mentoring to effectively manage the service, whilst providing feedback regarding performance on a regular systematic basis.

Why Work for us?
Our families, community and our team are the heart of what we do here at Bishop Tyrrell Anglican College and the Newcastle Anglican Schools Corporation. As a part of our organisation, you have access to the following great benefits:

  • Up to 40% off school fees at our Anglican schools.
  • Free access to our corporate Employee Assistance Program
  • Access to Fitness Passport via Association of Independent Schools NSW 
  • The opportunity to make a significant difference in our students’ futures
  • Career and development opportunities!
  • The opportunity to work within an innovative, collaborative team environment!

About us
Bishop Tyrrell Anglican College is an independent Preschool to Year 12 co-educational school providing Hunter Valley families with a globally innovative and future focused education for their children.

Bishop Tyrrell Anglican College focuses on the development of the whole child, emotionally, physically, intellectually and spiritually, within a caring, Christian environment. 

We foster a deep sense of community within our school, and work towards helping each student reach their potential through providing opportunities for everyone to learn, lead and serve. 

We endeavour to be a learning gateway to a world of opportunities for our students. We will prepare them well for the years that follow schooling by encouraging them to embrace their individual talents and interests, strive for excellence and seize the day!

Your skills and experience: 

  • Minimum 3 years’ experience in a Nominated Supervisor position
    in an Out of School Hours Care/Vacation Care Service or minimum
    5 years’ experience in a leadership position in an Out of School
    Hours Care service
  • Previous experience in administrative procedures, curriculum development, parent and community liaison, staff development and training 
  • Understanding and working knowledge of WHS legislation
  • Strong knowledge of the NQF, NQS and MTOP framework
  • Demonstrated knowledge of service requirements of the childcare subsidy system and ability to perform software application for compliance 

Essential criteria:

  • Degree in Early Childhood from a recognised University (as listed
    on the approved qualification list by ACECQA), or Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care (or equivalent)
  • Current First Aid Course in a Childcare Setting HLTAID012
  • Valid NSW Working with Children Check
  • National Criminal History Check (Newcastle Anglican will consider the relevance of any reported outcomes)
  • Applicants will be screened for appropriate child protection purposes as we are a Child Safe School.
  • Committed to our school values and proactively contribute to our team. 

How to apply:
Applications to be submitted online via the advertising platform, your application must include your CV and a cover letter addressing your experience and the essential criteria.
We encourage early applications; we will begin reviewing submissions as they are received.


Who we are? 
Formerly known as the Anglican Diocese of Newcastle, Newcastle Anglican is a faith-based organisation serving the people of the Hunter and Central Coast.

We offer a leading Christian presence to our community through our parishes, four schools, Anglican Care and Samaritans. 


Our vision is for people to flourish because of what we do, inspired by the way of Jesus. 

We provide a culturally safe environment for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and welcome all applications. 

You must have the right to live and work in Australia.


Newcastle Anglican Schools Corporation supports the rights of children and young people.

Reporting...
content.unEditedContent:
• 14/14 days and nights roster | FIFO from Perth to the Roy Hill Mine
  • Base + FIFO Allowances + Shift Allowances + Super + Bonuses
  • Family friendly even time roster to achieve true life/work balance
  • Employee travel benefits for FIFO employees – airport parking, flights, accommodation

About the role:

Our Water Network team is looking for a motivated and safety-focused Water Maintenance Supervisor to join us in a full-time opportunity.

Reporting to the Superintendent Water Execution, you’ll play an important role in leading safe and efficient dewatering operations, supporting maintenance teams, and contributing to reliable water network performance across site infrastructure.

This is an opportunity to step into a leadership role where you can make a meaningful impact on safety, operational performance and team culture. You’ll be supported by a collaborative team environment that values inclusion, development and continuous improvement.


Duties:

  • Coordinate and communicate water management schedules to support safe and efficient operations
  • Lead and support field-based maintenance teams, ensuring compliance with safety standards and critical controls
  • Work collaboratively across teams to achieve operational targets and deadlines
  • Foster a positive, inclusive and high-performing team culture through coaching, mentoring and development
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across water network operations and maintenance activities

Skills and Experience:

  • Current WA A Grade Electrical Licence (essential)
  • DEMIRS (LGIRS) Statutory Supervisor Competency S26 (essential)
  • Experience within mining and dewatering operations
  • Previous leadership or supervisory experience in a maintenance environment
  • Strong problem-solving, organisational and analytical skills
  • Experience using Microsoft Office and SCADA water network management systems
  • Confident communication skills and experience with CMMS/SAP systems

data.title: Casual Sales Assistant
data.descriptionHtml:
Bakers Delight Rose Bay is looking for a Casual Senior Sales Assistant to join our team. We provide a fun work environment, comprehensive training, and excellent opportunities for career advancement. Minimum experience of 1 year Preferred.

As a Sales Assistant, you will:

  • Work as part of a small team, providing exceptional customer service, and getting to know your regular customers
  • Be responsible for merchandising product and executing marketing campaigns
  • Also work alongside your team to keep the bakery clean, and assist with production assistance as needed.

What we’re looking for:

  • outgoing personality, is able to work with minimal supervision after training,
  • has an attention to detail with respect to cleaning,
  • is able to following instructions and the processes, policies and procedures of the business
  • reliability is a MUST!
  • Able to work weekends and some public holidays
  • You have a positive attitude and self-motivated, and you enjoy learning new skills
  • You are a team player who enjoys working with people
  • You take pride in providing a great experience for your customers.

Your main duties will include customer service (including up-selling and add-on selling), merchandising and general cleaning.

We will train you to use the tills, slice and package bread and deliver delightful customer service to our customers. Attention to detail is essential, as is an ability to follow instructions.

You must be prepared to adhere to Bakers Delight policies and respect the Bakers Delight brand.

We offer a friendly work environment and are reasonably flexible with rosters.

Must be available; Afternoon shifts from 2pm onwards for closes

Pay: From $34.48 per hour

Benefits:

  • Employee discount
  • Employee mentoring program
  • Free food

Experience:

  • Working towards sales targets and KPIs: 1 year (Preferred)
  • Retail: 1 year (Preferred)
  • Sales: 1 year (Preferred)
  • Customer service: 1 year (Preferred)

data.title: Administration Officer
data.descriptionHtml:
Administration Officer

Division: Child Protection and Family Support

Position No: Pool Ref COM8626

Salary: Level 3, $86,439 - $92,795 pa + Super - PSCSAA 2024

Work Type: Fixed Term - Full Time, Permanent - Full Time

Location: Whiteman or Stoneville

Closing Date: 2026-05-29 4:00 PM (YYYY-MM-DD)

About the Residential Care directorate
The Department provides therapeutic residential care in 14 metropolitan and 11 country houses that care for children with a range of ages and abilities. Care is provided in all these services by trained staff who undertake shifts using a rotating roster model.

Administration Officers support the delivery of these services by working closely with the Director to ensure the Directorate runs smoothly and effectively. They do this by:

  • Developing and maintaining quality administrative services.
  • Providing and ensuring quality assurance through financial analysis.
  • Facilitating the induction of staff.
  • Human resource planning and salary management.
  • Facilitating the development and maintenance of quality information management and technology systems.

Please refer to the attached Job Description Form (JDF) for more information. For any position specific enquiries, we encourage you to contact Mandy Millar, Coordinator Business Support, on (08) 6277 4848 or via email to Mandy.Millar@communities.wa.gov.au during business hours only.

The Opportunity
Suitable applicants will be placed in a pool from which appointments will be made for future permanent and temporary (full time) vacancies that arise for this or similar roles within the next 12 months across the Department of Communities.

In return for your skills, passion, and commitment we will offer you a challenging job, a safe and healthy working environment, and a range of benefits (subject to eligibility) including:

  • Flexible working arrangements (including flexible working hours, 9-day fortnight consideration, and work from home options)
  • Additional 3 Days Public Service Leave per annum
  • Eligibility to join the Fitness Passport program
  • 3 months long service leave for every seven years consecutive service
  • 18 weeks paid parental leave
  • 10 days Disability Leave
  • 5 days Reproductive Health Leave
  • Discount on private health insurance
  • Comprehensive learning and development opportunities that focus on your career aspirations
  • Access to free and confidential Employee Assistance Programs for you and your family
  • 5 days cultural and ceremonial leave for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander employees
  • Working for a nationally recognised Accredited Carer Friendly Employer through the Carers + Employers program.

Want to join us?
Apply online by clicking the ‘Apply for Job’ button (above or below) and provide the following documents in Word or PDF format only:

  • A current resume/CV.
  • A two (2) page written application addressing all the Essential Work Related Requirements (Selection Criteria) as stated on the JDF.
  • A copy of all qualification/s (regardless of the relevance to the role) as specified in your application or resume/CV (if applicable).

For technical difficulties while applying online, general recruitment enquiries, or to request any document in an alternative format, please contact the HR Recruitment team at HRRecruitment@communities.wa.gov.au.

We can also be contacted via the National Relay Service on the following numbers:

TTY/voice calls - 133 677
Speak & Listen - 1300 555 727
SMS relay - 0423 677 767

Integrity and Honesty
The public sector is built on a strong foundation of integrity where employees act ethically, and public sector bodies promote and maintain integrity.

In line with Communities policies, applicants may be asked for consent to undergo criminal record screening and integrity checks during the application process. For more information on these requirements, click here.

Equity and Diversity
The Department of Communities is committed to improving employment opportunities and outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. As a measure to achieve equality and support, section 51 of the Equal Opportunity Act 1984 (WA) will apply to this position. Aboriginal people are encouraged to apply. If you are an Aboriginal person who would like assistance with your application, please contact Jobs and Skills WA on 13 64 64.

If you have any access needs that may require adjustments to allow you to fully participate in the application and interview process, or alternative methods of communication, please contact HR Recruitment team via HRRecruitment@communities.wa.gov.au.

Lodgement is system generated. Any emailed applications or late submissions on or after 4:00pm will not be accepted.

data.title: Equipment Specialist - Repco (SA)
data.descriptionHtml:
• Time to get off the tools? Yet enjoy being hands on?

  • Exciting opportunity, strong company growth, supportive team

  • Company vehicle & mobile phone provided

Are you a Mechanic looking to get off the tools and change your direction. Maybe a Service advisor who has had enough of the 7:30 to 5:30 days, as well as being stuck behind a desk dealing with retail customers. This is an opportunity for you!

  • Is it time to get off the tools & out of the office but still stay connected to the industry with a mix of hands on as well as selling

  • Exciting opportunity to move into a service-based sales role with an awesome trade customer network to work with

  • Company vehicle, mobile phone and laptop provided so you can work with your customers on site and not spend your days behind a desk

Perfect role for a mechanic or tyre fitter looking for a change. Utilise your expertise & experience to provide service to our customers. Mon to Fri

Are you a Mechanic looking to get off the tools and change your direction? We are currently seeking a permanent full time Workshop Equipment Sales Specialist to join our team based in Woodville, to provide exceptional customer service to our SA customers through advising and guiding them through our range of equipment products.

Responsibilities include:

  • Provide customer service and advice to new and existing customers

  • Workshop equipment sales

  • Customer follow ups

  • Workshop equipment demonstrations and installations

  • After-sales equipment training

In an Equipment Specialist position you will:

  • Ideally have mechanical/automotive knowledge and must hold a valid driver's licence

  • Be able to communicate in both a technical and non-technical manner

  • Possess a team focus with strong relationship building skills

  • Have the ability to work autonomously and organise and prioritise efficiently

We can offer you:

  • Recognition programs and team incentives for your performance

  • Attractive product discounts across all GPC Asia Pacific businesses: Repco, NAPA, AMX, McLeod's Accessories, and more

  • An inclusive team environment; our team are important members GPC

  • The opportunity to join a progressive global company that continually strives to remain the number one in the automotive aftermarket

  • Ongoing training and career development; we genuinely care about supporting you to reach your full potential

  • Discounts internally and with external partners including health providers

  • We proactively support our working parents in a variety of meaningful ways, and our parental leave top-up allowance is one of the ways we do this

  • Paid volunteer leave allowing you to give back to your chosen charity/community organisation

Repco is Australia's leader in Automotive Aftermarket Parts and is one of the most widely recognised brands in the Australian and New Zealand markets.

GPC Asia Pacific

data.title: Auntie Anne's Team Member
data.descriptionHtml:
Join the Auntie Anne’s Team – We’re Hiring! Freshly baked pretzels. Handcrafted with care. Served from the heart.

Auntie Anne’s is looking for passionate and reliable team members to join us and grow with the brand.

At Auntie Anne’s, we’re known for our warm, soft pretzels and friendly service. We believe great food starts with great people. Our team is the heart of what we do — working together to deliver freshly baked products and an outstanding guest experience every single day.

What We’re Looking For:

  • A positive, team-oriented mindset
  • Someone that can do opening shifts at 6am with Monday - Friday availabilities
  • Willingness to learn and support others
  • Good communication skills
  • Availability for either part-time or full-time hours
  • Someone who strive for excellence, consistent, dependable, and committed to doing things well every day
  • Ability to follow precise recipes and measurements accurately
  • Someone who understands and respects workplace rules, especially those that support a respectful and safe environment
  • Awareness of the importance of keeping work sections clean, tidy, and organised at all times
  • A strong work ethic and commitment to team success
  • Someone open to learning and constructive feedback – if you have a strong “I Know Better” attitude, this role may not be the right fit.

Our Working Style:
At Auntie Anne’s, we work as a team to serve guests and ensure every product is prepared fresh and to standard. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Preparing, shaping, baking, and flavouring our signature pretzels
  • Serving coffee and specialty beverages (note: this is not a barista or all-rounder role)
  • Welcoming and serving customers with warmth and efficiency
  • Keeping the store clean and presentable
  • Completing daily checklists and tasks
  • Taking initiative and supporting the team where needed
  • Preparing and portioning ingredients such as dipping sauces, cream cheese, sausages, and lemon juice

****This work position requires you to multitask in a fast paced environment*****

Trial After Interview:

Firstly, you will be invited to attend a 1–2 hour unpaid trial.

This allows us to see how you blend with the team and ensures that you feel comfortable with the role and work environment.

After the Trial:

If you’re selected to join the Auntie Anne’s team, we will discuss your roster and training schedule with you.

What We Offer:

  • A friendly, inclusive, and supportive work environment
  • Comprehensive training and development opportunities
  • A pathway to long-term employment and career growth

If you're looking to be part of a team that values consistency, respect, quality, and positive energy, then we’d love to meet you.

Apply now and become part of the Auntie Anne’s family as we continue to grow and expand

Positions available at both our Town Hall, QVB and Westfield Parramatta store

*Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

**Salary packages depends on age and positions **

Job Types: Full-time, Part-time, Casual

Pay: $12.00 – $35.00 per hour

Ability to commute/relocate:

  • Sydney NSW 2000: Reliably commute or planning to relocate before starting work (Preferred)

Application Question(s):

  • Do you have any upcoming holiday trip soon?

Experience:

  • Hospitality: 2 years (Preferred)

Language:

  • Fluent English (Preferred)

Work Authorisation:

  • Australia (Required)

Work Location: In person

data.companyDescription:
Auntie Anne's is the world’s largest hand-rolled soft pretzel franchise known for mixing, twisting, and baking pretzels to golden brown perfection in full view of customers. With a variety of snack and meal options for people on-the-go, Auntie Anne's is a popular quick-service restaurant that can be found in shopping malls, transportation sites, colleges and universities, and non-traditional shopping and entertainment centers around the globe. 

Auntie Anne’s freshly baked, hand-rolled soft pretzels come in a variety of flavors from Cinnamon Sugar to Sour Cream & Onion. All products are backed by a Pretzel Perfect Guarantee, which simply states  “We guarantee you’ll love your pretzel or we’ll replace it with one that you do.” The core product lineup includes Original, Cinnamon Sugar, Sweet Almond, Sour Cream and Onion, and Roasted Garlic & Parmesan Pretzels, along with the Pretzel Dog. Auntie Anne’s most popular pretzel flavors are also available in bite-size, portable offerings: Pretzel Nuggets and Mini Pretzel Dogs. To complement pretzel selections, the brand’s famous lemonade can be enjoyed in its signature version or as Lemonade Mixers in four bold fruity flavors.
data.companyBriefDescription: Auntie Anne’s, Inc. serves as a support network to more than 350 franchise partners with more than 1,600 locations in 48 states and 30 countries.

data.title: Restaurant Manager
data.descriptionHtml:
At Zeus Street Greek, we believe in bold flavours, legendary hospitality, and the power of food to bring people together. As a Restaurant Manager, you will take full ownership of your restaurant and lead the charge in delivering exceptional food, service and team culture.


You will inspire and develop your leadership team, drive performance through people, and manage your restaurant’s P&L. This is a hands-on leadership role where you will maintain the highest standards of quality and safety, while living and breathing the Zeus Street Greek values and lightning bolt energy.


What’s in it for you?
So much! Here’s what you can look forward to:

  • Competitive salary + bonus opportunities
  • Flexible rosters and employment stability – let’s talk about what work-life balance means to you
  • Career progression – level up to Regional Restaurant Manager and Area Manager and beyond
  • Comprehensive training and ongoing support to set you up for success
  • Heavily discounted Zeus Street Greek meals
  • Free ZSG uniforms and exclusive merchandise
  • Cultural celebrations and brand moments
  • Opportunities to grow into head office


About You
We value diverse experience, but ideally you’ll bring:

  • Demonstrated leadership experience in a fast-paced, high-energy environment
  • Strong financial and commercial acumen, with the ability to identify sales and P&L opportunities and partner with your team on solutions
  • A proven track record of achieving and driving KPIs
  • Outstanding customer service capability
  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills

If you’re ready to take ownership of a restaurant and lead with lightning bolt energy, we’d love to hear from you.

data.title: Educator with Responsible Person Duties Chancellor OSHC Casual or Part-Time
data.descriptionHtml:
Chancellor OSHC is seeking a dedicated and capable Casual / Part-Time Educator to join our team. This role is ideally suited to an experienced educator who is confident in undertaking Responsible Person duties and supporting the daily leadership, compliance, and smooth operation of the service.

This is an excellent opportunity for a professional who is passionate about school age care, values high-quality practice, and can provide calm, effective leadership during shifts.

Position Details

  • Casual and Part-Time opportunities available
  • Morning and afternoon shifts
  • Split shift allowance applicable
  • Additional hours available during vacation care
  • Commencement: Immediate or negotiable

About the Role

In this role, you will contribute to the delivery of a safe, engaging, and high-quality program for children aged 5 to 12 years. You will also be expected to step into Responsible Person duties when required and support the effective day-to-day operation of the service.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Leading and participating in quality experiences and activities for children
  • Undertaking Responsible Person duties during shifts as required
  • Providing leadership, direction, and support to educators on shift
  • Making sound operational decisions to support the safe and effective running of the service
  • Supporting compliance with the National Quality Framework, service policies, and relevant procedures
  • Maintaining high standards of supervision and child safety
  • Confident with opening and closing procedures
  • Building positive and professional relationships with children, families, and colleagues
  • Contributing to a positive team culture and a well-organised service environment

About You

To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate professionalism, initiative, and the ability to lead with confidence in a busy OSHC environment.

You will have:

  • A strong commitment to child safety, wellbeing, and creating a child-safe culture
  • A relevant qualification in Children’s Services, School Age Care, or Education and Care, Certificate III or higher
  • Experience in OSHC, early childhood, or primary-aged care settings
  • Willingness and capability to undertake Responsible Person duties
  • Strong leadership, communication, and decision-making skills
  • A sound understanding of supervision, compliance, and safe service operations
  • A current Blue Card
  • Current First Aid, CPR, Asthma, and Anaphylaxis qualifications, or willingness to obtain
  • A genuine commitment to child wellbeing, inclusion, and quality practice

Why Join Chancellor OSHC

  • Supportive leadership and a collaborative team culture
  • Professional development and training opportunities
  • Flexible working arrangements
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to your local community
  • Guaranteed Christmas and New Year closure period.

If you are a motivated educator ready to take the next step in your OSHC career and contribute to the leadership of a quality service, we would welcome your application.

Pay: $27.62 – $39.19 per hour

Education:

  • High School (Year 9-11) (Preferred)

Experience:

  • Childcare: 1 year (Required)

Licence/Certification:

  • Blue Card (Required)

Work Location: In person

data.descriptionHtml:
Teacher / Tutor (English, Maths & Early Learning)

About FutureNest

FutureNest is a growing education and family learning centre dedicated to building confidence, academic skills, and real-world capabilities in children through engaging and supportive learning experiences.

We are currently looking for passionate and dedicated educators to join our team across English, Maths, and Early Learning programs.

Available Teaching Areas

  • English Teacher
  • Maths Teacher
  • Early Learning Teacher (Ages 3–5)

Role Overview

As a FutureNest Teacher, you will deliver engaging tutoring and learning sessions through 1:1 and small group formats. You will support students in developing confidence, foundational academic skills, literacy, numeracy, communication, and school readiness in a nurturing and positive environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Deliver engaging and structured learning sessions
  • Support literacy, numeracy, comprehension, communication, and problem-solving skills
  • Adapt lessons based on student learning levels and needs
  • Facilitate play-based and structured learning activities for younger learners
  • Monitor student progress and provide simple feedback when required
  • Create a safe, supportive, and encouraging learning environment
  • Draft simple learning plans where required
  • Encourage curiosity, confidence, and active participation in learning
  • Use creative teaching strategies, digital tools, and AI-assisted resources to enhance student engagement

Schedule

  • Weekdays: After-school hours
  • Weekends: Flexible shifts available

Compensation

  • Above award salary

Requirements

  • Degree in Teaching, Early Childhood Education, English, Mathematics, or related field
  • Experience in teaching or tutoring children preferred
  • Strong communication and classroom management skills
  • Passion for working with children across different age groups and ability levels
  • Strong lesson planning and organisational skills
  • Familiarity with the Australian Curriculum is an advantage
  • Warm, patient, and encouraging teaching approach
  • Open to using digital tools and AI to enhance teaching and student learning

Preferred Skills

  • Experience teaching literacy, reading, writing, and comprehension
  • Strong foundational maths knowledge
  • Understanding of early childhood development and school readiness
  • Ability to conduct both individual and small group sessions effectively

Join FutureNest and help shape confident, capable, and curious learners in a positive and supportive environment.

Pay: $40.00 – $60.00 per hour

Work Location: In person

We are currently looking for an experienced Lash & Brow Artist to join our growing team in a casual or part-time role, with late nights and additional cover shifts available.

This role is best suited to someone who is already confident working independently in a salon environment and is looking for a long-term position within a professional, fun and supportive team.

About the role

As part of our team, you will be responsible for delivering high-quality lash and brow services while providing an exceptional experience for our clients.

Our core services include:

  • Lash extensions
  • Lash lifts & dyes
  • Brow services (threading, waxing, shaping, laminations)

We are looking for someone who:

  • Has previous salon experience (2+ years) and is confident performing lash sets independently to a high standard
  • Produces safe, clean and consistent work
  • Takes pride in client experience and attention to detail
  • Is reliable, professional and works well in a fast-paced environment
  • Is confident working independently while also being part of a team
  • Has a positive attitude and strong work ethic
  • Is open to continued learning and upskilling the Whiplash’d way
  • Has experience with brow services (preferred)
  • Has experience using Timely or salon software (a bonus)
  • Is available for evening shifts and occasional last-minute cover when needed

What we offer

  • An established and heavily booked salon with a loyal client base
  • A supportive, fun and professional team environment
  • Ongoing training and development opportunities
  • Staff perks and discounts
  • Consistent work with regular clientele
  • Free staff services
  • No weekends or public holidays
  • Two weeks off at Christmas

About Us

Whiplash’d has been operating on the Central Coast for over 10 years (previously Just Lashes) and has built a reputation for exceptional client service and strong team culture. We pride ourselves on creating a workplace where our team genuinely enjoys coming to work.

To apply

Please send your cover letter, resume, availability and photos/videos of your work, along with a short introduction about yourself and your experience within the industry.

Job Types: Part-time, Casual

Pay: $34.00 – $38.00 per hour

Benefits:

  • Employee discount
  • Employee mentoring program
  • Professional development assistance

Application Question(s):

  • What do you think makes a great client experience?
  • Why do you want to work with us?
  • How many years experience do you have in the beauty industry and performing the services we offer?

data.descriptionHtml:

Employment Type: Temporary Full Time , 38 hours per week until 28/02/2027
Remuneration: $1601.32 - $1639.18 per annum + 12% Superannuation + Salary Packaging
Location: Clinical Information Department, Campbelltown and Camden Hospitals

Contact: Jesswy Rajdev - Patient Administration System Manager on 0246 343 637 | Jesswy.Rajdev@health.nsw.gov.au


With your skills and experience, you can contribute to the millions of ways we're enriching health, and develop your career as part of the largest health organisation in Australia.


Achieve Something Great
Step into a role where your work directly supports high-quality patient care by ensuring patient administration systems and medical records processes run smoothly and efficiently. As part of a collaborative and supportive team, you’ll work closely with key stakeholders to strengthen data integrity and improve the overall accuracy of patient information. Your contribution will play a vital role in maintaining reliable records within the eMR, helping clinicians deliver the best possible care outcomes.



Are You the Right Fit?
We’re looking for someone with strong attention to detail, excellent verbal and written communication skills, and the ability to problem-solve and make confident decisions. You’ll bring proficiency in PAS and Microsoft applications, along with experience in running and creating reports. If you enjoy providing system and technical support, delivering staff training, and being part of a team dedicated to continuous improvement, this could be the perfect opportunity for you.



Selection Criteria
To help us assess your suitability for the role, please tell us as much as you can about yourself in response to the questions below.

  • Demonstrated high level knowledge and experience with Cerner PAS, including PM and Scheduling.
  • Proven advanced proficiency in using PC based software including Microsoft office suite and network based applications.
  • Demonstrated experience in information systems training, support and developing training materials and manuals.
  • Demonstrated strong organisational and problem solving skills with the ability to be flexible and prioritise workloads to meet strict deadlines.
  • Applicants must possess an Australian C-Class driver's license (including P1 or P2). Those who hold a C class license (P1 or P2 included) from a state other than NSW must obtain a NSW C class (P1 or P2 included) license within three months of appointment. Learner's licenses are not permitted.



If you’d like more details, we’re here to help.

  • Position Information
    • Applicants will be assessed against the criteria in the Position Description.
  • How to Apply
    • Read our application guide and tips for improving your application.
  • Diversity, Culture & Inclusion
    • We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer dedicated to accessibility and a supportive recruitment experience. If you require adjustments or assistance during the application process, please contact SWSLHDJobs@health.nsw.gov.au
    • We value the diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives of our workforce and are committed to fostering a respectful and welcoming environment. We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, neurodivergent individuals, those from Refugee, multicultural and multifaith backgrounds, and members of the LGBTQI+ community.
  • Aboriginal Workforce
    • For Aboriginal candidates who would like to talk to our Aboriginal Workforce Team, please contact SWSLHD-AboriginalWorkforce@health.nsw.gov.au. Support is also available through the Stepping Up website.



More Than Just a Job – Why Work With Us?

  • Financial Perks
    • 12% superannuation
    • Salary packaging and novated leasing via Smart Salary
    • Annual leave with 17.5% leave loading (for full-time and part-time staff)
    • One extra day off each month for full-time employees
  • Work-Life Balance
    • Flexible work options, including hybrid and varied hours (depending on the role)
    • Paid maternity and parental leave
    • Generous leave options like long service and carers leave
  • Grow Your Career
    • Access to learning opportunities through our dedicated Education and Organisational Development team, who support staff with training, workshops, and career development programs.
  • Health & Wellbeing
    • Discounted gym membership through Fitness Passport
    • Free and confidential support for staff and their families via our Staff Wellbeing and Support Service (EAP)

    • Wellbeing programs that promote mental health, resilience, and balance




Additional Information

  • Temporary visa holders
    • May be considered if no suitable citizen or permanent resident is found.
  • Vaccination Requirements
    • All staff must meet NSW Health’s vaccination and screening requirements before starting.
  • Child Safe Employment
    • South Western Sydney Local Health District is dedicated to fostering a child-safe environment that respects and upholds the rights of children and young people, aligned with NSW Health’s commitment to implementing the Child Safe Standards. We aim to ensure that children and young people feel safe, supported, and included in their care. All current and prospective staff are expected to prioritise the safety, welfare, and well-being of children and young people, actively working to protect them from harm and abuse.

NSW Health supports the executive and statutory roles of the NSW Minister for Health and monitors the performance of the NSW public health system. Their vision is for everyone in NSW Health to work together to achieve "Healthy People - now and in the future".

NSW Health's goals are to:

* keep people healthy

* provide the health care that people need

* deliver high quality services and

* manage health services well.

There are 15 Local Health Districts that are responsible for providing health services in a wide range of settings, from primary care posts in the remote outback to metropolitan tertiary health centres. In addition, two specialist networks will focus on Children's and Paediatric Services, and Forensic Mental Health. A third network will operate across the public health services provided by three Sydney facilities operated by St Vincent's Health: these include St Vincent's Hospital and the Sacred Heart Hospice at Darlinghurst and St Joseph’s at Auburn.

The Ambulance Service of NSW is responsible for the delivery of front line pre-hospital care, medical retrieval and health related transport.

Other public health organisations provide statewide or specialist health services:

- Justice Health

- Children's Hospital at Westmead

- Clinical Excellence Commission

The Cancer Institute is a statutory body charged with substantially improving cancer control in NSW.

data.title: Gym Sales Representative - Casual Hours - Food Sampling
data.descriptionHtml:
With over 20 years of expertise in sales and marketing, Hive Direct Marketing Solutions collaborates with leading brands to promote outstanding products. We’re thrilled to partner with the market leader in healthy, fresh, ready-made meals delivered directly to customers’ doors. This is a fantastic opportunity for individuals, whether new to sales or seasoned, to launch or advance their career in the vibrant field of marketing and brand representation.

Join our team promoting a premium healthy ready-to-heat meal delivery service designed to fuel gym-goers and help them smash their fitness goals. In this hands-on, customer-facing position, you’ll visit gyms across Melbourne to:

- Set up members with an exclusive discount offer.

- Provide free samples of our high-protein range.

- Highlight how our convenient, nutrition-packed meals support training and recovery.

No hard selling required – just enthusiastic sampling and sharing the benefits of delicious, goal-focused nutrition. Perfect opportunity to build confidence, develop sales and communication skills, and connect with the fitness community.

Why Join Us?

  • Earn $1,500+ per week based on performance (not commission-only).
  • Comprehensive coaching and ongoing mentorship from experienced leaders.
  • A fun, social, and collaborative work environment with a dynamic team.
  • Opportunities for career development and personal growth.
  • Frequent team events and nights out to celebrate achievements.
  • Travel opportunities for organised events.
  • Weekly and monthly incentives.
  • Backpackers are welcome to apply!

Your Day-to-Day:

  • Work in numerous gyms across Melbourne, sampling & promoting our clients amazing products. We can accommodate to your location, wherever you're based!
  • Be part of a team with a strong focus on communication and customer engagement.
  • Participate in ongoing coaching sessions to enhance your skills.
  • Be part of a fun, upbeat team.

What We’re Looking For:

  • A positive, energetic personality.
  • Excellent communication and customer service skills.
  • Strong ambition and self-motivation.
  • Willingness to develop sales skills in a supportive, fun environment.
  • Experience in sales, retail, or customer service is preferred but not essential.
  • Applicants must be based in the Melbourne area with work rights.

Hours and Location:

  • Monday - Thursday 3:00pm-7:30pm & Friday 10.00am-2.00pm (Saturdays also available.)
  • Our office is based in the Melbourne CBD, However we operate in various gyms across Melbourne, engaging with a wide number of different customers by sampling & promoting our client's products.

Please Note: Due to the high volume of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Job Types: Part-time, Contract

Pay: $750.00 – $2,000.00 per week

Benefits:

  • Free drinks
  • Free food
  • Professional development assistance

Application Question(s):

  • Available Monday-Thursday 3.00pm-7.30pm and Friday 10.00am-2.00pm?
  • Do you have a notice period with your current employer?

Language:

  • English (Required)

Licence/Certification:

  • Driver Licence (Preferred)

Work Authorisation:

  • Australia (Required)

Work Location: In person

data.title: Permanent Dairy Hand
data.descriptionHtml:
Permanent Dairy Farm Hand – Tasmania

Progressive pasture-based dairy operation in Tasmania seeking a motivated and reliable permanent Dairy Farm Hand to join our team.

We milk approximately 700 cows through a modern 50-bail rotary dairy and operate a strong pasture-focused system with a major emphasis on animal health, breeding performance, pasture management and efficient farm systems. The farm also uses Halter virtual fencing technology across the operation.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone wanting to build a long-term career in the dairy industry while working with modern systems and quality livestock.

The Role:

  • Milking in a 50-bail rotary dairy
  • Herd movements and stock handling
  • Pasture allocation and general farm operations
  • Assisting with calving and young stock when required
  • Feeding and machinery operation
  • Animal health treatments
  • Fencing and general farm maintenance
  • Working within a strong team environment

About You:

  • Previous dairy farming experience preferred
  • Reliable, physically fit and hardworking
  • Able to work independently and in a team
  • Good stock sense and attention to detail
  • Interest in pasture-based dairying
  • Machinery experience an advantage
  • Driver’s licence preferred

What We Offer:

  • Permanent full-time position
  • Competitive salary based on experience
  • Furnished accommodation available
  • Supportive team environment
  • Opportunity to work with modern dairy technology and systems
  • Long-term career progression opportunities

Located in Tasmania, this role offers an excellent lifestyle opportunity in one of Australia’s leading dairy regions.

To apply, please send a brief introduction outlining your experience, availability and references.

Pay: $30.00 – $35.00 per hour

Benefits:

  • Housing provided
  • Professional development assistance

data.companyDescription:
SA Health is committed to protecting and improving the health of all South Australians by providing leadership in health reform, public health services, health and medical research, policy development and planning, with an increased focus on well being, illness prevention, early intervention and quality care.

SA Health is the brand name for the health portfolio of services and agencies responsible to the Minister for Health and the Minister for Mental Health and Substance Abuse. The portfolio consists of the Department of Health, Central Adelaide Local Health Network, Northern Adelaide Local Health Network, Southern Adelaide Local Health Network, Women’s and Children’s Health Network, Country Health SA Local Health Network, and SA Ambulance Service.

SA Health provides many important services to the South Australian community including:

- public hospitals

- metropolitan and country health service delivery

- environmental health

- communicable disease control

- epidemiology

- health promotion

- pathology services

- drug and alcohol services

- emergency and ambulance

- organ donation.

SA Health liaises closely with other agencies in government, particularly:

- Department of Education and Children’s Services

- Department for Families and Communities

- Department of Planning and Local Government

- Department of the Premier and Cabinet

- Department of Treasury and Finance

SA Health also engages with some non government and community service providers on a formal, direct basis and more broadly, on policy and planning matters.

data.title: Customer Service Assistant
data.descriptionHtml:
Casual Customer Service Assistant – SpudBARAbout SpudBAR

At SpudBAR, our purpose is simple: to make fast food feel good again.

For over 25 years, we’ve been serving fresh, satisfying comfort food built around the mighty spud — combining big flavours, real ingredients and fast service without compromise.

We pride ourselves on creating an energetic, supportive and fast-paced environment where team culture and guest experience come first.

About the Role

We’re looking for a positive, energetic and customer-focused Casual Customer Service Assistant to join the team at SpudBAR.

This role is perfect for someone who enjoys working with people, thrives in a fast-paced environment and takes pride in delivering a great customer experience.

You’ll play an important role in creating a welcoming atmosphere, preparing food to SpudBAR standards and supporting the overall flow of the store during service.

Key ResponsibilitiesGuest Experience & Service

  • Greet and assist customers in a friendly and professional manner
  • Help customers navigate the menu and build their perfect bowl
  • Deliver fast, attentive and positive customer service
  • Maintain a calm and upbeat presence during busy periods

Food Preparation & Product Execution

  • Prepare menu items to recipe and portion standards
  • Build bowls neatly, consistently and efficiently
  • Follow all food safety and hygiene standards
  • Maintain speed of service without compromising quality

Store Operations

  • Assist with opening, closing and cleaning duties
  • Maintain cleanliness and organisation across the store
  • Restock ingredients, packaging and utensils as required
  • Support the team wherever needed during busy periods

Team Contribution

  • Bring positive energy to every shift
  • Communicate clearly with team members and supervisors
  • Take direction well and apply feedback quickly
  • Support a strong team culture and collaborative environment

What We’re Looking For

  • Friendly and confident communication skills
  • Strong work ethic and reliability
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
  • Positive attitude and willingness to learn
  • Hospitality or customer service experience is preferred but not essential

Our Service Pillars

At SpudBAR, we value team members who:

  • Bring positive energy
  • Know the product
  • Move with urgency
  • Take ownership
  • Deliver genuine hospitality

Why Join SpudBAR?

  • Supportive team environment
  • Ongoing training and development
  • Flexible casual hours
  • Fast-paced and energetic workplace
  • Opportunity to grow within the business

Customers are looked after, the food hits, and every shift runs smoothly — that’s how we know we’re winning.

Pay: From $33.00 per hour

Benefits:

  • Employee discount

Work Location: In person

data.title: Casual Sales Assistant - Mandurah
data.descriptionHtml:
WHO ARE WE

Known best as the 'Undisputed King of Trainers', JD Sports reigns supreme as one of the biggest and best global Sports Fashion brands across footwear and apparel.

Founded in 1981 in Greater Manchester, UK, JD Group has achieved remarkable growth through rapid global expansion, now standing as the leading global sports fashion retailer. With over 3,400 stores worldwide, we strive to inspire the emerging generation through a captivating connection to the universal culture of sport, music, and fashion.

In 2017, JD Sports launched in Australia and New Zealand and has since grown to over 70+ stores. We now operate across NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA & TAS, with exciting plans for continued expansion.

Our mission? To offer unparalleled service and style to all our consumers. To bring this to life, we offer access to the biggest brands, the best products and a memorable experience that sets us apart.

Working at JD Sports is a state of mind. It's an attitude and a way of challenging the norm. We don’t conform; we create our own path and are elite within our field.

We’re seeking energetic, focused, and passionate individuals to join our team.

THE ROLE

At JD Sports, our customer is at the heart of everything we do. As a Casual Sales Assistant, your mission is to provide exceptional customer service that creates a memorable shopping experience and a lasting positive connection to our brand.
A Sales Assistant at JD is energetic, genuine and customer-focused, offering personalised assistance to our customers who have come seeking the best products and biggest brands.

As a Sales Assistant you are responsible for, but not limited to:

  • Act as a brand ambassador, always showing positivity and professionalism

  • Gain and maintain up to date product knowledge to best assist our customers

  • Provide personalised 1:1 customer service

  • Assist customers with all queries and process sales

  • Work in collaboration with the wider Management and store team to achieve KPI’s and targets

  • Support wider team with ad hoc tasks, including VM set up, store cleanliness and presentation etc.

  • Escalate any customer complaints to management

  • Consistently complete any mandatory training relevant to product, policy & procedure etc

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • Customer service experience within retail, hospitality or like industry

  • Ability to provide excellent service and go above & beyond

  • Passionate about sports fashion or has a knowledge of key brands

  • A positive can-do attitude and ability to work as a team

  • Thrives in a fast paced, ever-changing environment

  • Enthusiastic to overcome challenges and learn new skills

  • Strong communication skills, someone who thrives through engagement with customers and team work

  • Ability to multi-task

  • Flexibility to work across various shifts, including weekends and holidays, based on store needs

WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU?

  • Work in a dynamic business and engage with some of the best product and biggest sports fashion brands in the market

  • Training and development opportunities to kickstart, evolve and shape your career

  • Opportunity to progress across all areas of the business in a wide array of roles including Retail, Support Office, and our Distribution Centre

  • Access to our attractive staff discount! This can also be used for friends and family

  • Access to our Employee Assistance Program & Mental Health champions

  • One month paid parental leave for full-time employees

We are passionate about connecting with driven and skilled individuals who are invested in their development, so that together we can evolve our brand's success, alongside evolving your career.

JD values diversity and inclusion and champions a culture where everyone feels, valued, included, and celebrated.

What are you waiting for? Apply today and kick start your JD Sports Journey.

Please note, be applying for this role you consent for us to complete a VEVO Check in order to verify your working rights where required.

data.title: Stylist | Part Time | Rockhampton
data.descriptionHtml:
Join the Lovisa Team – Where Fashion and Fun Come Together!

Ready to dive into the world of super stylish jewellery that doesn’t break the bank? Lovisa is the ultimate go-to destination for trendy, affordable jewellery, and we’re growing fast – and we want YOU to be part of it! If you’re passionate about fashion, love the idea of working in a fun, high-energy team, and want to develop your skills while helping others shine, this is your dream job.


What’s In It for You:


  • Endless Growth: We’re constantly expanding (hello, global opportunities!), and we want you to grow with us! Whether it’s leveling up within your local store or taking on an international role, the possibilities are endless.
  • Fashion Perks: Get discounts on our fabulous jewellery, plus access to global competitions with amazing prizes – because we love rewarding our team.
  • Training & Skills: Not only will you get hands-on experience in retail, but we’ll train you to become an expert in everything from customer service to piercing (yep, we teach you how to do that too!).
  • A Team That Gets It: Work with a group of fun, energetic people who love what they do and always have each other's backs. Your team is your support system, and together, you'll crush it!

What We’re Looking For:

If you're obsessed with fashion and love helping others express their unique style, then we’re all in! We want someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, enjoys delivering amazing customer experiences, and is ready to bring that positive, can-do energy every day.

  • Fashion Enthusiast: You get excited about helping people find the perfect piece of jewelry to level up their look. You’re on top of the trends and always ready to style up any outfit.
  • Go-Getter: You’ve got that hustle – you’re proactive, motivated, and always find a way to get things done. You bring the energy!
  • Team Player: You love being part of a squad that’s always supporting each other and working together to hit goals (and have fun while doing it!).
  • Customer-Focused: You know that delivering an incredible customer experience is EVERYTHING. Every customer is unique, and you’re ready to help them shine!
The Role:
As a Part-Time Team Member at Lovisa, you’ll play a key role in creating unforgettable experiences for our customers! You'll be:

  • Providing next-level customer service that makes people feel amazing
  • Helping customers find that perfect jewelry piece (the one they won’t stop wearing)
  • Keeping the store looking fresh, organised, and picture-perfect at all times
  • Learning how to pierce (training provided!) and making sure customers leave with a smile
  • Having fun in a high-energy environment where every day is a new adventure

How to Apply:
We’re not asking for a CV – just a 1-minute video that answers these 3 simple questions:

  • What excites you about joining Lovisa?
  • What does the phrase “It’s about the customer, always” mean to you?
  • What 3 skills do you bring to the team?

Dress to impress – this is your chance to show us why YOU are the perfect fit for Lovisa!

Why Lovisa?

We’re all about diversity, creativity, and building a team that represents the world around us. Whether you're from across the street or across the globe, we celebrate your uniqueness and know it’s what makes our team so awesome.

Ready to join a global brand that’s growing fast and all about making the world a more stylish place?

Apply now and start your Lovisa journey – we can’t wait to meet you!

About ServiceNSW
Service NSW is making it easier for people and businesses across NSW to access government services. Since launching in July 2013, we have successfully transformed and streamlined NSW Government service delivery with cutting edge digital solutions and an award-winning culture of passion and teamwork. Our customer-centric solution offers simpler and faster access to government transactions through our digital channels, a 7-day-a-week phone service and an expanding network of service centres. We currently partner with over 50 agencies to offer over 1,000 NSW Government transactions.
About the team
As a Business Concierge, you will be responsible for supporting businesses at every stage of their journey, offering personalised guidance, resources and support both in person and over the phone.

You will work closely with aspiring business owners and businesses in your local area, to assist them start, manage and grow. You will build and maintain strong relationships and proactively engage with the community to understand and respond to their needs.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide personalised support and case management to small businesses
  • Proactively engage with businesses in your community
  • Engage with stakeholders (eg local councils) and partner with them to support businesses in your local area
  • Partner with your Team Leader and Business Relationship Manager to plan and deliver outreach activities, including events and presentations
  • Support inbound and outbound customer interactions through phone and digital channels
  • Build strong relationships with business customers to ensure ongoing support and positive outcomes when navigating government.

  • Experience working with multicultural communities; bilingual or multilingual capability is highly desirable
  • A strong understanding of the small business landscape and the challenges faced by business owners in NSW
  • Ability to adapt your approach to meet differing customer needs while maintaining high service standards

  • A proactive, customer-focused mindset
  • The ability to support businesses primarily based in the Cumberland & Fairfield LGA’s

data.title: Transport Officer
data.descriptionHtml:
ABORIGINAL IDENTIFIED POSITION

Casual Position


Join a progressive organisation delivering community-led programs with the Northern Territory's largest Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Service.


$65,149 to $67,996 per annum, pro-rata

Total Effective Package*

$83,678 to $86,910 pro-rata


About the role

The Transport Officer is responsible for providing an efficient transport service to enable Congress clients access to Congress health services.


What are we looking for?

Someone to fit our team with the following requirements:

  • Identifies as an Aboriginal person; recognised and accepted as an Aboriginal person by the Central Australian Aboriginal community.
  • Current NT C Class Drivers Licence
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to communicate sensitively in a cross-cultural environment.
  • Experience in community work and an awareness of the consultation process relevant to Aboriginal people and a community controlled organisation.


What we offer:

Congress offers rewarding career options and a wide range of employee benefits including:

  • Work that is community-led, impact-focused and a part of the bigger picture.
  • Opportunities to grow, including 15 days of professional development per year, with pathways including master's programs and study placements.
  • A flexible work policy including flexible start and finish times, compressed work weeks, part-time and casual roles, job sharing, remote work, hybrid work models and the possibility to purchase additional paid leave.
  • Salary packaging for full-time, part-time and casual employees.
  • Total Effective Package includes base salary, district allowance, superannuation, leave loading, and estimated tax saving from salary packaging options


Got you interested?

Don't meet all the role requirements, but think you'd be a great asset to our team? We'll never know unless you hit the Apply Now button.


For more information on the position please contact our Transport Coordinator

Monique Davis on 0490 803 046 or monique.davis@caac.org.au


Applications close when a suitable applicant is found

data.companyDescription:
For over 40 years, Central Australian Aboriginal Congress (Congress) has provided support and advocacy for Aboriginal people in the struggle for justice and equity.

Since that time, Congress has expanded to become the largest Aboriginal community-controlled health organisation in the Northern Territory, providing a comprehensive, holistic and culturally-appropriate primary health care service to Aboriginal people living in and nearby Alice Springs, including five remote communities; Amoonguna, Ntaria (and Wallace Rockhole), Santa Teresa, Utju (Areyonga) and Mutitjulu.

Today, we are one of the most experienced Aboriginal primary health care services in the country, a strong political advocate of closing the gap on Aboriginal health disadvantage and a national leader in improving health outcomes for all Aboriginal people.

data.title: Emergency Veterinarian
data.descriptionHtml:
About Us

Casey Pet Emergency is a purpose-built 24-hour emergency and critical care veterinary hospital located in Narre Warren, South-East Melbourne. Our hospital is designed to support high-quality patient care, efficient workflows, and sustainable veterinary practice.

We manage a diverse and dynamic caseload including medical, surgical, trauma, and critical care patients, supported by advanced diagnostics, modern equipment, and an experienced nursing team.

The Role

We are seeking a qualified Veterinarian to join our Emergency & Critical Care team. This role is suited to veterinarians with a minimum of 3 years’ clinical experience who are confident in managing a varied caseload or are looking to transition into emergency practice with structured support.

Key Responsibilities

  • Triage and manage emergency and critical care patients
  • Perform diagnostic work-ups including bloodwork, imaging, and clinical assessments
  • Develop and implement treatment plans for medical and surgical cases
  • Perform emergency surgical procedures where indicated (e.g. GDV, foreign body, wound repair)
  • Provide inpatient care and ongoing case management through to discharge
  • Communicate clearly with clients regarding diagnosis, treatment options, and prognosis
  • Maintain accurate and compliant medical records
  • Collaborate with veterinary nurses and support staff to deliver high-quality patient care
  • Participate in case discussions, rounds, and clinical development activities
  • Manage anaesthesia and pain control for critical and surgical patients

Skills & Experience Required

  • DVM or BVSc (or equivalent) eligible for registration in Victoria
  • Victorian Veterinary Registration
  • Radiation license and preferred CT license
  • Minimum 3 years’ clinical veterinary experience
  • Experience or strong interest in emergency and critical care
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Strong diagnostic, clinical reasoning, and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent communication and client care skills
  • Commitment to high standards of patient care and record keeping

Facilities & Support

You will be supported by:

  • Fully equipped ICU with advanced monitoring
  • Ventilators and respiratory support capability
  • Digital radiography and in-house CT (with specialist interpretation)
  • Ultrasound and comprehensive diagnostic tools
  • In-house pathology for rapid clinical decision-making
  • Integrated systems (EzyVet, SmartFlow, Modeus) for workflow efficiency
  • Highly skilled and supportive nursing team

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary
  • Flexible full-time or part-time rotating roster
  • 5 weeks annual leave
  • Continuing education allowance and professional development support
  • Structured onboarding and mentorship
  • A well-supported, collaborative clinical environment

Location

Narre Warren, Victoria – South-East Melbourne

Pay: $110,000.00 – $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

  • Employee mentoring program
  • Extended annual leave
  • Professional development assistance
  • Visa sponsorship

Education:

  • Bachelor Degree (Hons) (Preferred)

Experience:

  • Veterinary: 3 years (Preferred)

Licence/Certification:

  • Victorian Veterinary Registration (Required)

Work Location: In person

data.title: Retail Store Manager, Essendon DFO
data.descriptionHtml:
Requisition ID: 14847
Job Location(s): Essendon, VIC, AU, 3044
Time in Office: Onsite

At Crocs, Inc., every career offers a chance to make a real impact. No two journeys look the same. And that's exactly how we like it. Whether you’re welcoming customers into our stores, collaborating with global teams at our headquarters, or keeping operations moving at our distribution centers, your impact is real and valued. At Crocs, Inc. you’re not expected to fit a mold. You’re encouraged to break it and create something better.

Overview

As the Store Manager, you will lead a dedicated team of store associates & leaders every day, to create an exceptional consumer experience. Your focus will be on driving sales, providing excellent customer service, maintaining visual presentations, and developing talent within the store. This role offers opportunity to grow and collaborate with industry leading teammates and partners.

What You'll Do

  • Deliver outstanding service to our consumers using our C.H.A.R.M service model
  • Leads the store team in surpassing performance metrics including sales, consumer service and charms
  • Apply analytical thinking & company reporting to find opportunities within store, empowering the team to make strategic decisions
  • Lead visual presentation, product flow, replenishment, and operational standards throughout the store
  • Foster a welcoming, inclusive environment that engages promotes internal growth and builds an external network of talent
  • Coordinate, delegate, prioritize and meet store deadlines while ensuring effective follow up on daily activities
  • Contribute to crafting a team environment that encourages sharing of suggestions, ideas, and concerns while upholding Crocs Inc. values
  • Learn & assist in various departments including consumer service, product knowledge, visual presentation, and stock room management.
  • Support team members in the daily execution of retail operations i.e., POS system management and use, stock replenishment, assist in pricing and markdown processes seasonally, promote loyalty programs, maintain cleanliness and recovery standards etc.
  • Adhere to Crocs, Inc. Asset Protection policies and procedures, including shortage prevention, inventory control, and compliance procedures

What You'll Bring to the Table

  • Minimum 18+ years old
  • Possess at least A Level / SSCE/ Diploma / Advanced Diploma or above preferred
  • Minimum 5 years of total retail experience; preferably with previous Store Manager experience.
  • Demonstrated leadership abilities, with a passion for challenging, empowering, and driving team results
  • Professional working proficiency in English, proficiency of other language(s) will be an advantage
  • Proven communication skills (written and verbal) to successfully connect with store team, operations managers, District Managers & corporate partners
  • Flexible to work on rotational shift basis, including nights, Saturdays, Sundays and Public Holidays.
  • Intermediate computer proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Email and able to operate retail Point of Sale system
  • Demonstrated leadership abilities, with a passion for challenging, empowering, and driving team results
  • Desire to succeed in a high growth, fast-paced retail environment
  • The work environment and physical demands described here are representative of but not limited to those that an employee will encounter while performing the essential functions of this job.
  • Ability to climb and descend ladders carrying merchandise daily
  • Ability to lift 15kg or more with assistance daily

The Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to a diverse and inclusive work environment.


All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability, or any other protected classification.


At Crocs, Inc. we believe in the power of a blend of in-person and virtual collaboration to drive creativity and strengthen relationships. Your participation in this flexible schedule plays a key role in building a connected and successful team. In-office requirements vary by our work personas: Resident (5 days), Collaborator (4 days), Connector (2-3 days), Explorer (fully remote). This role has been aligned to the Resident persona.
